paras.t: Potest tamen hic locus convenientius exponi, hoc modo : Quoniam Dominus Jesus, qui est princeps regum terræ ; excelsus, quia secundum divinitatem est Patri æqualis, secundum humanitatem vero dedit ei Deus nomen quod est super omne nomen creatum, videlicet esse mediatorem Dei ac hominum, dicente Apostolo, Deus exaltavit illum, et dedit illi nomen quod est super omne nomen ; terribilis, propter futurum judicium, sicut ipse testatur : Erunt signa in sole et luna et stellis, et in terris pressura gentium præ confusione sonitus maris et fluctuum, arescentibus hominibus præ timore et exspectatione quæ supervenient universo orbi ; et tunc videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nube cum potestate magna et majestate. Ecce quam vere et inæstimabiliter terribilis Christus, qui potestatem habet et corpus et animam perdere in gehennam ignis. Rex magnus super omnem terram : id est, Jesus Christus in toto mundo ad ipsum converso, est rex magnus et præpotens, quemadmodum Balaam prophetavit : Orietur stella ex Jacob, et exsurget homo de Israel ; et erit Idumæa possessio ejus. Per Idumæam autem gentilitas designatur. Unde alia translatio habet : Et erit omnis terra possessio ejus. Propter quod Christus per Malachiam prophetam ait : Nomen meum horribile in gentibus.
paras.en: This place can, however, be expounded more fittingly in this way: [[46:3|For the Lord|Quoniam Dominus]] Jesus, who is [[Apoc 1:5|the prince of the kings of the earth|princeps regum terræ]]; [[46:3|high|excelsus]], because according to his divinity he is equal to the Father, while according to his humanity God gave him a name that is above every created name, namely to be the mediator between God and men, as the Apostle says: [[Phil 2:9|God also hath exalted him and hath given him a name which is above all names|Deus exaltavit illum, et dedit illi nomen quod est super omne nomen]]; [[46:3|terrible|terribilis]], because of the judgement to come, as he himself testifies: [[Luke 21:25|there shall be signs in the sun and in the moon and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, by reason of the confusion of the roaring of the sea, and of the waves|Erunt signa in sole et luna et stellis, et in terris pressura gentium præ confusione sonitus maris et fluctuum]], [[Luke 21:26|Men withering away for fear and expectation of what shall come upon the whole world|arescentibus hominibus præ timore et exspectatione quæ supervenient universo orbi]]; [[Luke 21:27|And then they shall see the Son of man coming in a cloud, with great power and majesty|et tunc videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nube cum potestate magna et majestate]]. See how truly and how beyond all reckoning terrible Christ is, who has power to destroy both body and soul in the hell of fire[[Matt 10:28||]]. [[46:3|A great king over all the earth|Rex magnus super omnem terram]]: that is, Jesus Christ, in the whole world converted to him, is a great and most mighty king, as Balaam prophesied: [[Num 24:17|A STAR SHALL RISE out of Jacob|Orietur stella ex Jacob]], and a man shall rise up out of Israel [the Vulgate has "a sceptre (*virga*) shall spring up from Israel"; Denis's "a man" is the reading of the Septuagint]; [[Num 24:18|and he shall possess Idumea|et erit Idumæa possessio ejus]]. By Idumea the Gentiles are signified; hence another translation has: And all the earth shall be his possession. For this reason Christ says through the prophet Malachias[[Mal 1:11||]]: [[Mal 1:14|my name is dreadful among the Gentiles|Nomen meum horribile in gentibus]].

paras.t: Subjecit populos nobis, et gentes sub pedibus nostris. Hæc est vox Apostolorum seu primitivæ Ecclesiæ : quibus Christus subjecit populos, id est Judæos ad fidem conversos, et gentiles credentes : imo Deus vult totum mundum esse subjectum Ecclesiæ militanti ; et non subjectos, æternaliter cruciabit, quemadmodum in Isaia Ecclesiæ dicitur : Gens et regnum quod non servierit tibi, peribit.
paras.en: [[46:4|He hath subdued the people under us; and the nations under our feet.|Subjecit populos nobis, et gentes sub pedibus nostris]] This is the voice of the Apostles, or of the early Church, to whom Christ subjected the peoples, that is, the Jews converted to the faith and the believing Gentiles; indeed God wills the whole world to be subject to the Church militant, and those not subject he will torment eternally, as is said to the Church in Isaias: [[Is 60:12|the nation and the kingdom that will not serve thee, shall perish|Gens et regnum quod non servierit tibi, peribit]].

paras.t: Deinde Ecclesia electorum summum Dei beneficium commemorans, dicit : Elegit nobis hereditatem suam : id est, Christus decrevit nobis dare bona cœlestia, non terrena, felicitatem vitæ æternæ, non prosperitatem vitæ mundanæ ; magisque voluit nos facere heredes Dei, coheredesque sui, quam dare nobis temporalia bona, quæ esse possunt malis ac bonis communia. Sic ergo elegit nobis, id est ad nostram salutem, hereditatem suam, id est felicitatem æternam, videlicet speciem Jacob, id est pulchritudinem electorum vitia supplantantium, quem Jacob, seu designatos per Jacob, Deus dilexit. Nam et sanctum Jacob Deus dilexit, sicut Malachias fatetur : Nonne frater erat Esau Jacob ? et Jacob dilexi, Esau autem odio habui. Electos quoque per Jacob significatos dilexit Christus, quemadmodum legitur in Apocalypsi : Qui dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo. Hereditas itaque Dei, quam Deus elegit dare electis, est speciem Jacob, id est summus ornatus ac decor pulcherrimus electorum, quum sit summa eorum perfectio. Propter quod superius dictum est : Domine, dilexi decorem domus tuæ, id est beatitudinem patriæ.
paras.en: Then the Church of the elect, recalling God's supreme benefit, says: [[46:5|He hath chosen for us his inheritance|Elegit nobis hereditatem suam]]: that is, Christ decreed to give us heavenly goods, not earthly ones, the happiness of eternal life, not the prosperity of the life of this world; and he willed rather to make us heirs of God and his own joint heirs[[Rom 8:17||]] than to give us temporal goods, which can be common to the wicked and the good. So, then, he [[46:5|hath chosen for us|elegit nobis]], that is, for our salvation, [[46:5|his inheritance|hereditatem suam]], that is, eternal happiness, namely [[46:5|the beauty of Jacob|speciem Jacob]], that is, the loveliness of the elect who supplant vices [an allusion to the name Jacob, "supplanter"]; [[46:5|which|quem]] Jacob, or those signified by Jacob, God [[46:5|hath loved|dilexit]]. For God loved holy Jacob too, as Malachias declares: [[Mal 1:2|Was not Esau brother to Jacob|Nonne frater erat Esau Jacob]]? [[Mal 1:2|and I have loved Jacob|et Jacob dilexi]], [[Mal 1:3|But have hated Esau|Esau autem odio habui]]. Christ also loved the elect signified by Jacob, as we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:5|who hath loved us and washed us from our sins in his own blood|Qui dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo]]. The inheritance of God, then, which God chose to give the elect, is the beauty of Jacob, that is, the highest adornment and most lovely comeliness of the elect, since it is their highest perfection. For which reason it was said above: [[Ps 25:8|I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house|Domine, dilexi decorem domus tuæ]], that is, the beatitude of the heavenly fatherland.

paras.t: Ascendit Deus, id est Dei Unigenitus Jesus Christus, super omnes cælos, in jubilo, id est in ineffabili laude et gaudio tam sui ipsius, quam sanctæ multitudinis quæ ipsum ascendere vidit, quam angelorum sanctorum, qui ipso ascendente dicebant : Dominus fortis et potens, Dominus potens in prælio ; et, Dominus virtutum ipse est rex gloriæ : sicut in expositione psalmi vicesimi tertii plenius dictum recordor. Christus quippe cum jubilo proprii cordis ascendit, dicens ad angelos sanctos : Ego qui loquor justitiam, et propugnator sum ad salvandum. De Apostolis quoque et aliis qui Christum ascendentem videbant, scriptum est : Eduxit eos Jesus foras in Bethaniam, et benedixit eis, et ferebatur in cælum ; et ipsi adorantes, regressi sunt in Jerusalem cum gaudio magno, laudantes et benedicentes Deum. Dominus in voce tubæ : id est, Christus ascendit cum voce tubali angelorum discipulos consolantium, secundum quod in Actis scriptum est : Quumque intuerentur in cælum euntem illum, ecce duo viri (id est duo angeli in forma virili) adstiterunt juxta illos in vestibus albis, qui et dixerunt : Viri Galilæi, quid statis adspicientes in cælum? Vel, Dominus ascendit in voce tubæ, id est cum sonora altaque voce sui ipsius, quia (ut dicit Lucas) elevatis manibus benedixit eis, et recessit ab ipsis. Et alia multa atque sublimia dixit discipulis ascensurus, ut in Actibus dicitur.
paras.en: [[46:6|God is ascended|Ascendit Deus]], that is, the Only-begotten of God, Jesus Christ, above all the heavens, [[46:6|with jubilee|in jubilo]], that is, amid unspeakable praise and joy, both his own and that of the holy multitude that saw him ascend, and that of the holy angels, who said as he ascended: [[Ps 23:8|the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle|Dominus fortis et potens, Dominus potens in prælio]]; and, [[Ps 23:10|the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory|Dominus virtutum ipse est rex gloriæ]], as I remember having said more fully in the exposition of the twenty-third psalm. For Christ ascended with the jubilation of his own heart, saying to the holy angels: [[Is 63:1|I, that speak justice, and am a defender to save|Ego qui loquor justitiam, et propugnator sum ad salvandum]]. Of the Apostles too, and the others who saw Christ ascending, it is written: Jesus [[Luke 24:50|led them out as far as Bethania|Eduxit eos Jesus foras in Bethaniam]], and [[Luke 24:50|he blessed them|benedixit eis]], and [[Luke 24:51|was carried up to heaven|ferebatur in cælum]]; [[Luke 24:52|And they adoring went back into Jerusalem with great joy|et ipsi adorantes, regressi sunt in Jerusalem cum gaudio magno]], [[Luke 24:53|praising and blessing God|laudantes et benedicentes Deum]]. [[46:6|And the Lord with the sound of trumpet|Dominus in voce tubæ]]: that is, Christ ascended with the trumpet-like voice of the angels consoling the disciples, according to what is written in the Acts: [[Acts 1:10|And while they were beholding him going up to heaven|Quumque intuerentur in cælum euntem illum]], [[Acts 1:10|behold two men|ecce duo viri]] (that is, two angels in the form of men) [[Acts 1:10|stood by them in white garments|adstiterunt juxta illos in vestibus albis]], [[Acts 1:11|Who also said: Ye men of Galilee, why stand you looking up to heaven?|qui et dixerunt : Viri Galilæi, quid statis adspicientes in cælum?]] Or: [[46:6|the Lord|Dominus]] ascended [[46:6|with the sound of trumpet|in voce tubæ]], that is, with his own loud and lofty voice, because (as Luke says) [[Luke 24:50|lifting up his hands, he blessed them|elevatis manibus benedixit eis]], and [[Luke 24:51|he departed from them|recessit ab ipsis]]. And when he was about to ascend he said many other lofty things to the disciples, as is told in the Acts[[Acts 1:3||]].

paras.t: Quum ergo sit ita, o omnes fideles, Psallite Deo nostro, videlicet Jesu Christo creatori, salvatori, ac judici nostro, psallite, id est, bonis operibus ipsum laudate ; psallite regi nostro, scilicet Christo, qui cælum terramque regit, et Ecclesiam suam non deserit, psallite. Quoniam rex omnis terræ Deus : id est, Christus est Dominus totius mundi in ipsum credentis. Unde dixit Apostolis : Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ. Et Apostolus ait : Novissime diebus istis locutus est nobis Deus in Filio, quem constituit heredem universorum.
paras.en: Since this is so, then, O all ye faithful, [[46:7|Sing praises to our God|Psallite Deo nostro]], namely to Jesus Christ, our creator, saviour and judge, [[46:7|sing ye|psallite]], that is, praise him with good works; [[46:7|sing praises to our king|psallite regi nostro]], that is, to Christ, who rules heaven and earth and does not forsake his Church, [[46:7|sing ye|psallite]]. [[46:8|For God is the king of all the earth|Quoniam rex omnis terræ Deus]]: that is, Christ is the Lord of the whole world that believes in him. Hence he said to the Apostles: [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth|Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ]]. And the Apostle says: [[Heb 1:1|last of all|Novissime]], [[Heb 1:2|In these days, hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things|diebus istis locutus est nobis Deus in Filio, quem constituit heredem universorum]].

paras.t: Psallite sapienter : id est, cum interiori mentis sapore cordialique gustu, verba psalmodiæ proferte, Deum laudate ac honorate, non cum vago et arido corde : quatenus sicut gustus corporis singulas alimenti particulas discernit, sapit, ac digerit; ita interior animæ gustus singula verba Spiritus Sancti attendat, gustet, atque revolvat. Hoc modo psallere, est vere sapienter psallere : quoniam sapientia dicitur quasi sapora scientia. Quidam vero insipienter psallunt et orant. De quibus Dominus per Prophetam ait : Populus hic labiis me honorat; cor autem eorum longe est a me. Et talis laudatio sive oratio infructuosa est, juxta illud Apostoli : Si orem lingua, mens mea sine fructu est. Ideo subdit : Orabo spiritu, orabo et mente; psallam spiritu, psallam et mente. Quod quam salubre fructuosumque sit, pandit subjungens : In Ecclesia volo quinque verba loqui sensu meo, quam decem millia in lingua. Studeamus ergo psallere sapienter : quod ad nos solitarios tanto amplius pertinet, quanto præ ceteris ad majorem mentis puritatem tenemur. Vel sic : Psallite sapienter, id est, Christum laudate et colite, non solum ut hominem, sed etiam ut verum Deum : secundum quod ait Apostolus, Et si Christum secundum carnem cognovimus, tamen jam nunc non novimus.
paras.en: [[46:8|Sing ye wisely|Psallite sapienter]]: that is, utter the words of the psalmody with an inward savour of the mind and a heartfelt relish; praise and honour God, not with a wandering and dry heart; so that, just as the bodily taste discerns, savours and digests each morsel of food, so the inward taste of the soul may attend to, taste and turn over each word of the Holy Ghost. To sing psalms in this way is truly to sing wisely, since wisdom (*sapientia*) is so called as being savoury knowledge (*sapora scientia*) [a play on *sapere*, which means both "to taste" and "to be wise"]. But some sing psalms and pray unwisely. Of them the Lord says through the Prophet: This people [[Is 29:13|with their lips glorify me, but their heart is far from me|labiis me honorat; cor autem eorum longe est a me]] [Denis's wording is that of the quotation in Matt 15:8]. And such praise or prayer is fruitless, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 14:14|if I pray in a tongue|Si orem lingua]], [[1 Cor 14:14|my understanding is without fruit|mens mea sine fructu est]]. Therefore he adds: [[1 Cor 14:15|I will pray with the spirit, I will pray also with the understanding, I will sing with the spirit, I will sing also with the understanding|Orabo spiritu, orabo et mente; psallam spiritu, psallam et mente]]. How wholesome and fruitful this is he shows when he goes on: [[1 Cor 14:19|in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding|In Ecclesia volo quinque verba loqui sensu meo]], [[1 Cor 14:19|than ten thousand words in a tongue|quam decem millia in lingua]]. Let us strive, then, to sing wisely: which concerns us solitaries [that is, Carthusian monks, who live as hermits] all the more, as we are bound beyond others to a greater purity of mind. Or thus: [[46:8|sing ye wisely|Psallite sapienter]], that is, praise and worship Christ not only as man but also as true God, according to what the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 5:16|And if we have known Christ according to the flesh: but now we know him so no longer|Et si Christum secundum carnem cognovimus, tamen jam nunc non novimus]].

paras.t: Regnavit Deus super gentes, ad se per fidem et cultum conversas. Deus sedet super sedem sanctam suam, id est, Christus sedet ad dexteram Patris in throno majestatis. Vel, Super sedem sanctam suam, id est in mente omnium Beatorum, secundum quod infra habetur : Qui sedes super Cherubim, manifestare. Unde Propheta ait: Adspiciebam donec throni positi sunt, et Antiquus dierum sedit, etc. Thronus ejus flammæ ignis, id est angeli sancti : de quibus in sequentibus scriptum est, Qui facis angelos tuos spiritus, et ministros tuos ignem urentem. Apostolus vero ita allegat hunc versum : Qui facit angelos suos spiritus, et ministros suos flammam ignis.
paras.en: [[46:9|God shall reign over the nations|Regnavit Deus super gentes]] [the text has *Regnavit*, "hath reigned"; the margin gives the reading *Regnabit*, "shall reign", as in the Vulgate], that is, over the nations turned to him by faith and worship. [[46:9|God sitteth on his holy throne|Deus sedet super sedem sanctam suam]], that is, Christ sits at the right hand of the Father on the throne of majesty. Or, [[46:9|on his holy throne|Super sedem sanctam suam]], that is, in the mind of all the Blessed, according to what is found further on: [[Ps 79:2|Thou that sittest upon the cherubims, shine forth|Qui sedes super Cherubim, manifestare]]. Hence the Prophet says: [[Dan 7:9|I beheld till thrones were placed, and the ancient of days sat|Adspiciebam donec throni positi sunt, et Antiquus dierum sedit]], etc. [[Dan 7:9|his throne like flames of fire|Thronus ejus flammæ ignis]], that is, the holy angels, of whom it is written further on in the psalms: [[Ps 103:4|Who makest thy angels spirits: and thy ministers a burning fire|Qui facis angelos tuos spiritus, et ministros tuos ignem urentem]]. The Apostle, however, cites this verse thus: [[Heb 1:7|He that maketh his angels spirits and his ministers a flame of fire|Qui facit angelos suos spiritus, et ministros suos flammam ignis]].

paras.t: Principes populorum congregati sunt cum Deo Abraham. Hoc communiter ita exponitur : Principes populorum, id est quidam ex principalibus plebis, sicut Centurio et alii principes conversi, congregati sunt cum Deo Abraham, id est, Christo, qui est Deus Abrahæ, per fidem conjuncti sunt. Sed convenientius magisque proprie ad litteram de Apostolis exponendum videtur : quibus Christus in Evangelio ait, Beati oculi qui vident quæ vos videtis ; et iterum, Vobis datum est nosse mysterium regni Dei ; rursusque, Non possunt filii Sponsi lugere, quamdiu cum illis est Sponsus. Ipsi enim corporaliter cum Deo Abrahæ, id est cum Filio Dei incarnato in mundo, conversati sunt ; inveneruntque pretiosissimam illam margaritam, per quam Christus in Evangelio ipsum significat. Et quod ista expositio sit magis ad litteram, constat ex eo quod in natalitiis Apostolorum cantantur verba prædicta de Apostolis loco antiphonæ.
paras.en: [[46:10|The princes of the people are gathered together, with the God of Abraham|Principes populorum congregati sunt cum Deo Abraham]]. This is commonly expounded thus: [[46:10|The princes of the people|Principes populorum]], that is, some of the leading men of the people, such as the Centurion and other princes who were converted, [[46:10|are gathered together, with the God of Abraham|congregati sunt cum Deo Abraham]], that is, they were joined by faith to Christ, who is the God of Abraham. But it seems more fitting, and more properly the literal sense, to expound it of the Apostles, to whom Christ says in the Gospel: [[Luke 10:23|Blessed are the eyes that see the things which you see|Beati oculi qui vident quæ vos videtis]]; and again: [[Luke 8:10|To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God|Vobis datum est nosse mysterium regni Dei]]; and again: [[Matt 9:15|the children of the bridegroom|filii Sponsi]] cannot [[Matt 9:15|mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them|lugere, quamdiu cum illis est Sponsus]]. For they lived bodily with the God of Abraham, that is, with the Son of God incarnate in the world, and they found that most precious pearl[[Matt 13:45||]][[Matt 13:46||]] by which Christ in the Gospel signifies himself. And that this exposition is more literal is plain from the fact that on the feasts of the Apostles the words above are sung of the Apostles as an antiphon.

paras.t: Quoniam dii fortes terræ, id est sancti Apostoli per excellentiam gratiæ deificati, et terræ (id est hominum) dii effecti, eos regendo et instruendo, et quasi salvando, vehementer elevati sunt : quia primitias Spiritus Sancti receperunt, tam in donis gratum facientibus quam gratuitis, et ipsi constituti sunt principes super omnem terram, sicut in alio psalmo tractatum est. Si autem scire optamus quam vehementer elevati sunt dii terræ, id est sancti Apostoli, pensemus quid eis in Evangelio Christus dicat : Quorum, inquit, remiseritis peccata, remittuntur eis ; et quorum retinueritis, retenta sunt. Et denuo : Vos qui secuti estis me, sedebitis super sedes duodecim, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel. Itemque : Vos estis lux mundi ; et, Vos estis sal terræ. Et iterum : Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi super serpentes et scorpiones, et supra omnem virtutem inimici ; et nihil vobis nocebit. Et rursus : Mortuos suscitate, infirmos curate, leprosos mundate, dæmones ejicite. Unde tales ac tantos futuros esse Apostolos prævidens Isaias, vehementer admiratus est, dicens : Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant, et quasi columbæ ad fenestras suas? Volabant enim ut nubes, sublimiter contemplando, velociter per mundum currendo, atque altissime prædicando. De quibus accipi potest illud in Threnis : Candidiores nive, nitidiores lacte, rubicundiores ebore antiquo. Erant nempe Apostoli candidiores nive, propter splendorem sapientiæ sibi infusæ; nitidiores lacte, propter innocentiam atque munditiam vitæ ; rubicundiores quoque ebore antiquo, propter ardorem caritatis divinæ atque fraternæ. Merito ergo dii terræ dicuntur, quia doctores et judices hominum facti sunt, aliisque excellenter prælati. Unde Dominus ait ad Moysen : Ecce constitui te Deum Pharaonis.
paras.en: [[46:10|For the strong gods of the earth|Quoniam dii fortes terræ]], that is, the holy Apostles, deified by the excellence of grace and made gods of the earth (that is, of men) by ruling and instructing them and, as it were, saving them, [[46:10|are exceedingly exalted|vehementer elevati sunt]]: for they received the firstfruits of the Holy Ghost[[Rom 8:23||]], both in the gifts that make one pleasing to God and in those freely given [that is, sanctifying grace (*gratia gratum faciens*) and the graces given freely for the good of others (*gratiæ gratis datæ*), such as prophecy and miracles], and they were appointed [[Ps 44:17|princes over all the earth|principes super omnem terram]], as was treated in another psalm. If we wish to know how exceedingly the gods of the earth, that is, the holy Apostles, are exalted, let us weigh what Christ says to them in the Gospel: [[John 20:23|Whose sins|Quorum]], he says, [[John 20:23|you shall forgive, they are forgiven them: and whose sins you shall retain, they are retained|remiseritis peccata, remittuntur eis ; et quorum retinueritis, retenta sunt]]. And again: [[Matt 19:28|you who have followed me|Vos qui secuti estis me]] [[Matt 19:28|shall sit on twelve seats judging the twelve tribes of Israel|sedebitis super sedes duodecim, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel]]. Likewise: [[Matt 5:14|You are the light of the world|Vos estis lux mundi]]; and, [[Matt 5:13|You are the salt of the earth|Vos estis sal terræ]] [the margin gives only Matt. v, 14; the salt of the earth is v. 13]. And again: [[Luke 10:19|Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall hurt you|Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi super serpentes et scorpiones, et supra omnem virtutem inimici ; et nihil vobis nocebit]]. And again: [[Matt 10:8|raise the dead|Mortuos suscitate]], [[Matt 10:8|heal the sick|infirmos curate]], [[Matt 10:8|cleanse the lepers, cast out devils|leprosos mundate, dæmones ejicite]]. Hence Isaias, foreseeing that the Apostles would be such and so great, marvelled greatly, saying: [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds, and as doves to their windows|Qui sunt isti qui ut nubes volant, et quasi columbæ ad fenestras suas]]? For they flew as clouds, by lofty contemplation, by running swiftly through the world, and by preaching most sublimely. Of them can be taken that saying in Lamentations: [[Lam 4:7|whiter than snow, purer than milk, more ruddy than the old ivory|Candidiores nive, nitidiores lacte, rubicundiores ebore antiquo]]. For the Apostles were whiter than snow because of the splendour of the wisdom poured into them; purer than milk because of the innocence and cleanness of their life; and more ruddy than the old ivory because of the ardour of their charity toward God and toward their brethren. Rightly, then, are they called gods of the earth, for they were made teachers and judges of men and set high above others. Hence the Lord says to Moses: [[Ex 7:1|Behold, I have appointed thee the god of Pharao|Ecce constitui te Deum Pharaonis]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmus iste eloquio brevis, quam vere amœnus est, pulcher, et dulcis ac sententiosus, in quo tam repetitis vicibus ad Dei laudem excitamur : nam quinquies in eo psallere Deo admonemur.
paras.en: See how truly this psalm, brief in its wording, is delightful, beautiful, sweet and full of meaning: in it we are roused to the praise of God so many times over, for five times we are bidden in it to sing psalms to God.

paras.t: Precatio. Rex omnis terræ Deus, sedens super sedem sanctam tuam, elige nos tibi in hereditatem : ut tecum regnantes in æterna gloria, te præstante exsultemus coram te lætitia inenarrabili et glorificata : qui cum eodem Deo Patre et Spiritu Sancto vivis et regnas in omnia sæcula. Amen.
paras.en: Prayer. [[46:8|King of all the earth|Rex omnis terræ]], O God, sitting upon thy holy throne, choose us for thyself as thine inheritance: that, reigning with thee in eternal glory, we may by thy gift exult before thee with joy unspeakable and glorified: who with the same God the Father and the Holy Ghost livest and reignest for all ages. Amen.

47.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI QUADRAGESIMI SEPTIMI : MAGNUS DOMINUS ET LAUDABILIS NIMIS.
47.title_en: Exposition of the forty-seventh psalm: Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised.

paras.t: Præponitur demum psalmo nunc exponendo hic titulus: Psalmus cantici, filiis Core, secunda sabbati: id est, psalmus iste, qui canticum appellatur quoniam agit de rebus divinis, in quibus solis vera ac sancta exsultatio est habenda, convenit filiis Core, id est imitatoribus Crucifixi; secunda sabbati, id est, tractans de his quæ facta sunt in secunda sabbati. Prima enim sabbati fecit Deus cœlum et terram, divisitque lucem a tenebris: et per hanc mystice intelligitur dies dominicæ resurrectionis, in quo Christus omnia creavit. Secunda vero sabbati seu hebdomadæ fecit firmamentum: per quam spiritualiter designatur constitutio Ecclesiæ, quæ post Christi resurrectionem, adveniente Spiritu Sancto, in Christo fundata atque firmata est: et de hac fundatione Ecclesiæ psalmus iste ad litteram loqui videtur.
paras.en: Lastly, the psalm now to be expounded is headed by this title: [[47:1|A psalm of a canticle, for the sons of Core, on the second day of the week|Psalmus cantici, filiis Core, secunda sabbati]]: that is, this psalm, which is called a canticle because it treats of divine things, in which alone true and holy exultation is to be had, befits the sons of Core, that is, the imitators of the Crucified [the name Core was taken to mean "Calvary", so that its sons are the followers of the Crucified]; on the second day of the week, that is, treating of the things that were done on the second day of the week [*sabbatum*, "sabbath", here stands for the week; *prima sabbati* and *secunda sabbati* are its first and second days]. For on the first day of the week God made heaven and earth[[Gen 1:1||]], and divided the light from the darkness[[Gen 1:5||]]: and by this day is understood mystically the day of the Lord's resurrection, on which Christ created all things anew. And on the second day of the sabbath, or of the week, he made the firmament[[Gen 1:7||]]: by which is signified spiritually the establishing of the Church, which after Christ's resurrection, when the Holy Ghost came[[Acts 2:1||]], was founded and made firm in Christ: and it is of this founding of the Church that this psalm seems to speak according to the letter.

paras.t: AIT ergo sanctus Propheta, cui Christi mysteria excellentissime claruerunt: Magnus Dominus et laudabilis nimis: quod licet de tota Trinitate, qualibetque Persona divina accipi possit, propter sequentia tamen de Christo specialiter dictum est. Ipse enim est magnus Dominus, imo immensus et laudabilis nimis, utpote in infinitum. Quantum enim res habet de bonitate, in tantum laudabilis est. Quum ergo Dei natura sit bonitas incircumscripta ac pura, patet quod ipse in infinitum laudabilis sit, nec digne, nec satis a creatura laudari queat. Propterea alibi scriptum est: Terribilis Dominus et magnus vehementer, et omnipotens super omnia opera sua. Glorificate Dominum quantumcumque potueritis, supervalebit adhuc: major est enim omni laude.
paras.en: So the holy Prophet, to whom the mysteries of Christ were most excellently made clear, says: [[47:2|Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised|Magnus Dominus et laudabilis nimis]]: which, though it may be taken of the whole Trinity and of each divine Person, is nevertheless said especially of Christ, because of what follows. For he is the great Lord, indeed the immeasurable one, and exceedingly to be praised, that is, infinitely. For a thing is praiseworthy in the measure in which it has goodness. Since, then, the nature of God is goodness unbounded and pure, it is plain that he is infinitely to be praised, and cannot be praised worthily or enough by any creature. Therefore it is written elsewhere: [[Ecclus 43:31|The Lord is terrible, and exceeding great|Terribilis Dominus et magnus vehementer]], and [[Ecclus 43:30|the Almighty himself is above all his works|omnipotens super omnia opera sua]]. [[Ecclus 43:32|Glorify the Lord as much as ever you can, for he will yet far exceed|Glorificate Dominum quantumcumque potueritis, supervalebit adhuc]]: [[Ecclus 43:33|for he is above all praise|major est enim omni laude]].

paras.t: In civitate Dei nostri, id est in Jerusalem divino cultui deputata, quam evangelista Matthæus appellat sanctam civitatem; specialiter tamen in monte sancto ejus, id est in templo ædificato in monte Moria, seu altiori loco urbis istius. Vel, In monte sancto ejus, id est in cœnaculo, in quo ipse Christus novissimam Cœnam cum Apostolis fecit. Hoc enim cœnaculum situm fuit in monte prædicto, non longe a templo. Itaque Christus dicitur magnus et laudabilis nimis in civitate et monte prædictis, quoniam majestas atque laudabilitas ejus in hac civitate præcipue monstrata est, sicut patebit. Propter quod apud Matthæum legitur: Quum intrasset Jesus Jerosolymam, commota est universa civitas, dicens: Quis est hic? Populi autem dicebant: Hic est Jesus propheta a Nazareth Galilææ. Maxime vero apparuit Christi majestas et laus in monte sancto hujus civitatis, id est in templo atque cœnaculo: quia in templo multa miracula fecit, quemadmodum evangelista Matthæus ibi subjungit: Accesserunt ad eum cæci et claudi in templo, et sanavit omnes.
paras.en: [[47:2|in the city of our God|In civitate Dei nostri]], that is, in Jerusalem, set apart for the worship of God, which the evangelist Matthew calls [[Matt 27:53|the holy city|sanctam civitatem]]; but especially [[47:2|in his holy mountain|in monte sancto ejus]], that is, in the temple built [[2 Par 3:1|in mount Moria|in monte Moria]], or on the higher ground of that city. Or, [[47:2|in his holy mountain|In monte sancto ejus]], that is, in the upper room[[Luke 22:12||]] in which Christ himself held the Last Supper with the Apostles. For this upper room stood on the aforesaid mountain, not far from the temple. So Christ is said to be great and exceedingly to be praised in the aforesaid city and mountain, because his majesty and praiseworthiness were shown above all in this city, as will be made plain. Hence we read in Matthew: [[Matt 21:10|when he was come into Jerusalem, the whole city was moved, saying: Who is this?|Quum intrasset Jesus Jerosolymam, commota est universa civitas, dicens: Quis est hic?]] [[Matt 21:11|And the people said: This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth of Galilee.|Populi autem dicebant: Hic est Jesus propheta a Nazareth Galilææ]] But the majesty and praise of Christ appeared most of all in the holy mountain of this city, that is, in the temple and in the upper room: for in the temple he worked many miracles, as the evangelist Matthew adds there: [[Matt 21:14|there came to him the blind and the lame in the temple: and he healed them|Accesserunt ad eum cæci et claudi in templo, et sanavit omnes]].

paras.t: Fundatur exsultatione universæ terræ: id est, civitas sancta Jerusalem ædificata est ad magnam lætitiam omnium in toto mundo credentium: quia in ea fuit primitiva Ecclesia Christi, cœpitque fides catholica primo in ea per Apostolos prædicari, et exinde diffusa est fides Christi per omnes gentes. Propter quod per Isaiam scriptum est: De Sion exibit lex (haud dubium quin evangelica), et verbum Domini de Jerusalem. Ex hoc autem gaudium magnum ortum est omnibus gentibus ad Christum conversis, secundum quod legitur Paulus ad Judæos dixisse: Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei; sed quia repulistis illud, ecce convertimur ad gentes, etc. Audientes autem gentes, gavisæ sunt, et glorificabant verbum Domini. Hinc quoque angelus ad pastores dixit: Annuntio vobis gaudium magnum quod erit omni populo, quia natus est vobis hodie Salvator. Hæc enim nativitas primo prædicata est publice in Jerusalem. Mons Sion, qui est ex uno latere Jerusalem, latera aquilonis, id est pars huic monti opposita, sunt civitas regis magni, id est Dei altissimi. Ex extremitatibus enim partium suarum constituitur civitas; et partes simul acceptæ, sunt idem quod totum.
paras.en: [[47:3|With the joy of the whole earth|Fundatur exsultatione universæ terræ]] is it founded: that is, the holy city of Jerusalem was built to the great gladness of all who believe throughout the whole world: for in it was the first Church of Christ, and in it the Catholic faith first began to be preached by the Apostles, and from there the faith of Christ was spread through all nations. Hence it is written by Isaias: [[Is 2:3|the law shall come forth from Sion|De Sion exibit lex]] (no doubt the law of the Gospel), [[Is 2:3|and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem|et verbum Domini de Jerusalem]][[Mich 4:2||]]. And from this great joy arose for all the nations converted to Christ, according as we read that Paul said to the Jews: [[Acts 13:46|To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God|Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei]]; but [[Acts 13:46|because you reject it|quia repulistis illud]], [[Acts 13:46|behold we turn to the Gentiles|ecce convertimur ad gentes]], etc. [[Acts 13:48|And the Gentiles hearing it were glad and glorified the word of the Lord|Audientes autem gentes, gavisæ sunt, et glorificabant verbum Domini]]. Hence too the angel said to the shepherds: [[Luke 2:10|I bring you good tidings of great joy that shall be to all the people|Annuntio vobis gaudium magnum quod erit omni populo]]: [[Luke 2:11|For, this day is born to you a Saviour|quia natus est vobis hodie Salvator]]. For this birth was first preached publicly in Jerusalem. [[47:3|mount Sion|Mons Sion]], which is on one side of Jerusalem, and [[47:3|on the sides of the north|latera aquilonis]], that is, the part over against this mountain, are [[47:3|the city of the great king|civitas regis magni]], that is, of God most high. For a city is made up of the outermost bounds of its parts; and the parts taken together are the same as the whole.

paras.t: Potest quoque spiritualis hic locus explanari, et redit quasi in idem. Magnus Dominus et laudabilis nimis in civitate Dei nostri, id est in Ecclesia militante, quæ per fidem et gratiam fundata est in monte sancto ejus, id est in Christo, qui est mons magnus, propter omnium divinorum charismatum eminentiam. De quo in Daniele scriptum est: Lapis qui abscissus est de monte sine manibus, crevit in montem magnum, et implevit universam faciem terræ. Vel quod dicitur, In monte sancto ejus, est idem quod prædixit, In civitate Dei nostri: quia Ecclesia Christi est mons magnus propter altitudinem gratiæ. Propter quod apud Isaiam de ea scriptum est: Erit in novissimis diebus præparatus mons domus Domini in vertice montium, et elevabitur super colles, et fluent ad eum omnes gentes. Per dies autem novissimos intelligunt tempus gratiæ atque evangelicæ legis, quæ est lex finalis ac ultima. Hoc itaque tempore fuit mons Domini, id est Ecclesia Christi, in vertice montium, id est sublimior in donis ac gratiis Spiritus Sancti Synagoga et omnium electorum ecclesia quæ a principio mundi fuit usque ad Christi adventum. Vel mons domus Domini appellatur mons Sion: qui tempore Christi fuit in vertice montium, id est altior monte Sinai et Thabor, non propter situm localem, sed propter præsentiam et prædicationem atque miracula Christi, qui in monte Sion, id est in templo et in domo cœnaculi, præsentialiter apparuit, prædicavit, et miracula maxima fecit: præsertim in cœnaculo seu conclavi, in quod ingressus est januis clausis, in quo consecravit corpus et sanguinem suum, in quo etiam misit Apostolis Spiritum Sanctum in signo visibili, dans eis omnium linguarum ac divinarum Scripturarum præclaram notitiam.
paras.en: This passage can also be explained spiritually, and it comes back to much the same thing. [[47:2|Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised in the city of our God|Magnus Dominus et laudabilis nimis in civitate Dei nostri]], that is, in the Church militant, which by faith and grace is founded [[47:2|in his holy mountain|in monte sancto ejus]], that is, in Christ, who is a great mountain because of the pre-eminence of all divine gifts. Of whom it is written in Daniel: [[Dan 2:34|a stone was cut out of a mountain without hands|Lapis qui abscissus est de monte sine manibus]], which [[Dan 2:35|became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth|crevit in montem magnum, et implevit universam faciem terræ]]. Or what is said, [[47:2|in his holy mountain|In monte sancto ejus]], is the same as what he said before, [[47:2|in the city of our God|In civitate Dei nostri]]: for the Church of Christ is a great mountain because of the height of grace. Hence it is written of her in Isaias: [[Is 2:2|in the last days the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared on the top of mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills, and all nations shall flow unto it|Erit in novissimis diebus præparatus mons domus Domini in vertice montium, et elevabitur super colles, et fluent ad eum omnes gentes]]. By the last days they understand the time of grace and of the law of the Gospel, which is the final and last law. So in this time the mountain of the Lord, that is, the Church of Christ, was on the top of the mountains, that is, more exalted in the gifts and graces of the Holy Ghost than the Synagogue and the church of all the elect that was from the beginning of the world until the coming of Christ. Or the mountain of the house of the Lord is the name given to mount Sion: which in the time of Christ was on the top of the mountains, that is, higher than mount Sinai and Thabor, not by its situation, but because of the presence, the preaching and the miracles of Christ, who on mount Sion, that is, in the temple and in the house of the upper room, appeared in person, preached, and worked the greatest miracles: above all in the upper room or chamber, into which he entered, [[John 20:26|the doors being shut|januis clausis]], in which he consecrated his body and blood[[Matt 26:26||]], in which also he sent the Holy Ghost to the Apostles in a visible sign[[Acts 2:1||]], giving them a splendid knowledge of all tongues and of the divine Scriptures[[Acts 2:4||]].

paras.t: Fundatur exsultatione universæ terræ: id est, primitiva Ecclesia in Christo fundata stabilitaque est ad omnium exsultationem fidelium. Ex hoc enim quod primitiva Ecclesia tantam a Christo gratiam et virtutem recepit, totus mundus ad Christum conversus est: ex qua conversione electi summe gavisi sunt. Mons Sion, id est populus ex Judæis conversus, latera aquilonis, id est gentiles, vitiis torpidi, affectu insipidi, et in bonis operibus frigidi. Aquilo enim est plaga frigida, juxta illud Ecclesiastici, Frigidus ventus Aquilo flavit, et gelavit crystallus ab aqua. Hi ergo sunt civitas regis magni, id est Ecclesia Christi: quia in Christo sicut in lapide angulari, conjuncti sunt Judæi atque gentiles, ad constituendam unam civitatem seu templum, in quo Deus per gratiam habitat. De quo templo in Zacharia scriptum est: Ecce vir, Oriens (id est Messias) nomen ejus; et ædificabit templum Domino, id est militantem Ecclesiam, et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos, id est inter montem et latera aquilonis, secundum expositionem jam habitam.
paras.en: [[47:3|With the joy of the whole earth|Fundatur exsultatione universæ terræ]] is it founded: that is, the first Church was founded and established in Christ to the exultation of all the faithful. For because the first Church received such grace and power from Christ, the whole world was converted to Christ: and at this conversion the elect rejoiced exceedingly. [[47:3|mount Sion|Mons Sion]], that is, the people converted from the Jews, and [[47:3|the sides of the north|latera aquilonis]], that is, the gentiles, sluggish with vices, without savour in their affections, and cold in good works. For the north is a cold quarter, according to that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 43:22|The cold north wind bloweth, and the water is congealed into crystal|Frigidus ventus Aquilo flavit, et gelavit crystallus ab aqua]]. These, then, are [[47:3|the city of the great king|civitas regis magni]], that is, the Church of Christ: for in Christ, as in the corner stone[[Eph 2:20||]], Jews and gentiles are joined together, to make up one city or temple, in which God dwells by grace[[Eph 2:21||]]. Of which temple it is written in Zacharias: [[Zach 6:12|BEHOLD A MAN, THE ORIENT|Ecce vir, Oriens]] (that is, the Messias) [[Zach 6:12|IS HIS NAME|nomen ejus]]; [[Zach 6:12|and shall build a temple to the Lord|et ædificabit templum Domino]], that is, the Church militant, and [[Zach 6:13|the counsel of peace shall be between them both|et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos]], that is, between the mountain and the sides of the north, according to the exposition already given.

paras.t: Et hoc est quod ait Apostolus: Qui eratis sine Christo et sine Deo in hoc mundo; nunc in Jesu Christo, qui aliquando eratis longe, facti estis prope in sanguine ipsius. Ipse enim est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum, et medium parietem maceriæ solvens, inimicitias in carne sua; legem mandatorum decretis evacuans, ut duos condat in semetipso in unum novum hominem, faciens pacem per crucem, interficiens inimicitias in semetipso.
paras.en: And this is what the Apostle says: You who were [[Eph 2:12|without Christ|sine Christo]] and [[Eph 2:12|without God in this world|sine Deo in hoc mundo]]; [[Eph 2:13|now in Christ Jesus, you, who some time were afar off, are made nigh by the blood of Christ|nunc in Jesu Christo, qui aliquando eratis longe, facti estis prope in sanguine ipsius]]. [[Eph 2:14|For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and breaking down the middle wall of partition, the enmities in his flesh|Ipse enim est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum, et medium parietem maceriæ solvens, inimicitias in carne sua]] [[Eph 2:15|Making void the law of commandments contained in decrees: that he might make the two in himself into one new man, making peace|legem mandatorum decretis evacuans, ut duos condat in semetipso in unum novum hominem, faciens pacem]] [[Eph 2:16|by the cross, killing the enmities in himself|per crucem, interficiens inimicitias in semetipso]].

paras.t: Deus in domibus ejus, id est a civibus seu habitatoribus Jerusalem, cognoscetur, quum suscipiet eam, id est, quum per gratiam suam vocaverit eam ad fidem et gloriam tantam. Cognitus est namque Christus a Simeone et Anna et aliis multis, in civitate Jerusalem. Vel: In domibus ejus, id est in Ecclesiis particularibus seu singulis Christi fidelibus, cognoscetur, quum suscipiet eam, id est, quum Ecclesiam ita illuminaverit, ut cognoscatur ab omnibus, quemadmodum per Isaiam prædictum est: Repleta est terra scientia Domini, sicut aquæ maris operientes.
paras.en: [[47:4|In her houses|Deus in domibus ejus]], that is, by the citizens or inhabitants of Jerusalem, [[47:4|shall God be known, when he shall protect her|cognoscetur, quum suscipiet eam]] [*suscipiet*, "shall protect" in the Douay-Rheims, is literally "shall take up" or "receive"], that is, when by his grace he shall have called her to faith and to so great glory. For Christ was known by Simeon and Anna and many others in the city of Jerusalem[[Luke 2:1||]]. Or: [[47:4|In her houses|In domibus ejus]], that is, in the particular Churches, or in each of Christ's faithful, [[47:4|shall God be known, when he shall protect her|cognoscetur, quum suscipiet eam]], that is, when he shall have so enlightened the Church that he is known by all, as was foretold by Isaias: [[Is 11:9|the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the covering waters of the sea|Repleta est terra scientia Domini, sicut aquæ maris operientes]].

paras.t: Sed quia habitatores Jerusalem inducti sunt ad cognoscendum Christum esse natum, ex adventu trium Magorum in Jerusalem venientium atque dicentium, Ubi est, qui natus est, rex Judæorum? idcirco subjungitur: Quoniam ecce reges, videlicet tres Magi, congregati sunt corporaliter, convenerunt in unum spiritualiter, scilicet in una fide et intentione adorandi Christum natum. Ipsi, id est habitatores Jerusalem, scilicet Herodes et principes sacerdotum, ac alii multi, videntes sic Magos venire cum tanto comitatu et gloria, admirati sunt, conturbati sunt, id est inquietati propter sollicitudinem, commoti sunt ad invidiam; tremor apprehendit eos, quia Herodes timuit regno privari, et ex hoc ceteri Judæi timebant magnas sibi persecutiones instare. Unde legitur: Audiens autem Herodes rex, turbatus est, et omnis Jerosolyma cum eo.
paras.en: But because the inhabitants of Jerusalem were led to know that Christ was born by the coming of the three Magi, who came into Jerusalem saying: [[Matt 2:2|Where is he that is born king of the Jews?|Ubi est, qui natus est, rex Judæorum?]] therefore it is added: [[47:5|For behold the kings|Quoniam ecce reges]], namely the three Magi, [[47:5|assembled themselves|congregati sunt]] in body, [[47:5|they gathered together|convenerunt in unum]] in spirit, that is, in one faith and one intention of adoring the new-born Christ. And [[47:6|they|Ipsi]], that is, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, namely Herod and the chief priests and many others: [[47:6|So they saw|videntes sic]] the Magi coming with so great a retinue and glory, and [[47:6|they wondered, they were troubled|admirati sunt, conturbati sunt]], that is, were disquieted with anxiety, [[47:6|they were moved|commoti sunt]] to envy; [[47:7|Trembling took hold of them|tremor apprehendit eos]], because Herod feared to be deprived of his kingdom, and because of this the rest of the Jews feared that great persecutions were coming upon them. Hence we read: [[Matt 2:3|And king Herod hearing this, was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.|Audiens autem Herodes rex, turbatus est, et omnis Jerosolyma cum eo]]

paras.t: Vel sic: Ipsi, id est tres Magi, videntes sic stellam sibi apparere, et postea disparere, ac iterum apparere, admirati sunt; conturbati sunt per tristitiam, quando stella disparuit; commoti sunt ad interrogandum ubi Christus nasceretur; tremor apprehendit eos, id est, timor reverentialis intravit mentem eorum, ex eo quod Spiritu Sancto revelante, cognoverunt puerum quem viderunt et adoraverunt, esse verum Deum. Unde cum metu et reverentia maxima offerebant ei munera, secundum quod Isaias prædixit: Reges videbunt et consurgent principes, et adorabunt propter Dominum Deum tuum. Hoc tamen intelligi potest de omnibus terræ principibus ad fidem conversis.
paras.en: Or thus: [[47:6|they|Ipsi]], that is, the three Magi, [[47:6|So they saw|videntes sic]] the star appear to them, and afterwards disappear, and appear again, and [[47:6|they wondered|admirati sunt]]; [[47:6|they were troubled|conturbati sunt]] with sadness when the star disappeared; [[47:6|they were moved|commoti sunt]] to ask where Christ should be born; [[47:7|Trembling took hold of them|tremor apprehendit eos]], that is, a reverential fear entered their minds, because by the revelation of the Holy Ghost they knew that the child whom they saw and adored was true God. Hence with fear and the greatest reverence they offered him gifts, according as Isaias foretold: [[Is 49:7|Kings shall see, and princes shall rise up, and adore for the Lord's sake|Reges videbunt et consurgent principes, et adorabunt propter Dominum Deum tuum]], thy God. This, however, can be understood of all the princes of the earth converted to the faith.

paras.t: Ibi, scilicet in terra Judæ, dolores ut parturientis: quia genitrices infantium qui ab Herode occidebantur, tantum affligebantur de filiorum suorum interitu, sicut partu.
paras.en: [[47:7|There|Ibi]], namely in the land of Juda, [[47:7|were pains as of a woman in labour|dolores ut parturientis]]: for the mothers of the infants who were slain by Herod were as much afflicted at the death of their sons as in childbirth.

paras.t: In spiritu vehementi, id est in ira impetuosa, conteres, Domine Deus, id est, ab Herode comburi permittes, naves Tharsis. Videns enim Herodes se a Magis illusum, iratus est valde; fecitque destrui naves Tharsis, eo quod audierat per eas redisse Magos ad propria.
paras.en: [[47:8|With a vehement wind|In spiritu vehementi]], that is, in headlong wrath [*spiritus* is both "wind" and "spirit"; Denis takes it as a violent spirit, that is, anger], [[47:8|thou shalt break in pieces|conteres]], O Lord God [these words, *Domine Deus*, are in Denis's text of the verse but not in the Clementine Vulgate], that is, thou wilt permit to be burned by Herod, [[47:8|the ships of Tharsis|naves Tharsis]]. For Herod, seeing that he had been deluded by the Magi, was exceeding angry; and he had the ships of Tharsis destroyed, because he had heard that the Magi had gone back to their own country in them.

paras.t: Deinde Propheta ait in persona primitivæ Ecclesiæ, quæ Christi mysteria vidit impleri, seu omnium Christianorum, qui facta Christi fideliter contemplantur: Sicut audivimus in Scripturis divinis, sic vidimus oculo mentis aut corporis, in civitate Domini virtutum, utpote in civitate Dei nostri, id est in Jerusalem, quia in ea Christus apparuit, sicut Prophetæ vaticinati erant. Vel, In civitate Domini virtutum, id est in Ecclesia, quæ est civitas Dei, qui est Dominus virtutum, id est angelorum. Deus fundavit eam, id est Ecclesiam, in æternum, quia fides Ecclesiæ usque in finem mundi durabit, quemadmodum Christus Apostolis in persona Ecclesiæ dixit: Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi.
paras.en: Then the Prophet speaks in the person of the first Church, which saw the mysteries of Christ fulfilled, or of all Christians, who faithfully contemplate the deeds of Christ: [[47:9|As we have heard|Sicut audivimus]] in the divine Scriptures, [[47:9|so have we seen|sic vidimus]] with the eye of the mind or of the body, [[47:9|in the city of the Lord of hosts|in civitate Domini virtutum]], that is, [[47:9|in the city of our God|in civitate Dei nostri]], that is, in Jerusalem, for in it Christ appeared, as the Prophets had foretold. Or, [[47:9|in the city of the Lord of hosts|In civitate Domini virtutum]], that is, in the Church, which is the city of God, who is the Lord of hosts, that is, of the angels [*Dominus virtutum*, "Lord of hosts", is literally "Lord of the powers"; the Powers, *virtutes*, are an order of angels]. [[47:9|God hath founded it|Deus fundavit eam]], that is, the Church, [[47:9|for ever|in æternum]], because the faith of the Church will last until the end of the world, as Christ said to the Apostles in the person of the Church: [[Matt 28:20|behold I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi]].

paras.t: Suscepimus, o Deus Pater, in die Purificationis, misericordiam tuam, id est Christum Filium tuum nobis misericordissime missum ac natum: de quo per Isaiam dixisti, Prope est ut veniat salus mea; et denuo, Dabo in Sion salutem, et in Jerusalem gloriam meam; in medio templi tui: quia tunc Virgo beata obtulit Christum in templo, suscepitque eum Simeon in ulnas suas, et Anna sancta confitebatur eidem, loquens de eo omnibus qui exspectabant consolationem Israel, quemadmodum apud Lucam legitur.
paras.en: [[47:10|We have received|Suscepimus]], [[47:10|O God|o Deus]] the Father, on the day of the Purification, [[47:10|thy mercy|misericordiam tuam]], that is, Christ thy Son, most mercifully sent and born to us: of whom thou didst say by Isaias: [[Is 56:1|my salvation is near to come|Prope est ut veniat salus mea]]; and again: I will give salvation in Sion, and my glory in Jerusalem[[Is 46:13||]] [Denis reads *in Jerusalem* where the Vulgate has *in Israel*]; [[47:10|in the midst of thy temple|in medio templi tui]]: for then the blessed Virgin offered Christ in the temple[[Luke 2:22||]], and Simeon took him into his arms[[Luke 2:28||]], and holy Anna gave praise to him, speaking of him to all who looked for the consolation of Israel[[Luke 2:38||]], as we read in Luke.

paras.t: Hanc autem repræsentationem Christi in templo, etiam Malachias propheta clarissime prædixit. Loquens enim in Christi persona, Ecce, inquit, ego mitto angelum meum, et præparabit viam ante faciem meam: quod certum est de Christi præcursore esse prædictum. Deinde subjungit de Christi adventu, Et statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti quem vos vultis. Porro et Aggæus propheta de eodem pulchre locutus est. Quum enim dixisset, Veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus, statim subjecit, Et implebo domum istam gloria, dicit Dominus. Scientibus autem Scripturas certum est, quod loquitur de templo in Jerusalem ædificato post reditum a captivitate Babylonica: ad cujus reædificationem ipse et Zacharias hortabantur Judæos. De hujus autem templi gloria subdit: Magna erit gloria domus istius novissimæ, plus quam primæ, dicit Dominus. Hæc vero excellentia domus novissimæ ultra templum a Salomone ædificatum, in nullo fuit nisi quod Christus in propria persona in ea apparuit, docuit, atque miracula fecit. Alias enim templum illud novissimum, nullius erat reputationis ad templum primum a Salomone constructum. Propter quod scriptum est, quod ædificato templo secundo, illi qui viderant templum primum, vehementer lugebant; qui vero illud non viderant, multum gaudebant. Ex quibus accipi potest evidens argumentum, quod rex Messias jam venit, et in templo illo apparuit quod jam diu a Romanis destructum est.
paras.en: Now this presentation of Christ in the temple the prophet Malachias also foretold most clearly. For speaking in the person of Christ, he says: [[Mal 3:1|Behold|Ecce]], [[Mal 3:1|I send my angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face|ego mitto angelum meum, et præparabit viam ante faciem meam]]: which was certainly foretold of Christ's forerunner. Then he adds of the coming of Christ: [[Mal 3:1|And presently the Lord, whom you seek, and the angel of the testament, whom you desire, shall come to his temple|Et statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti quem vos vultis]]. And the prophet Aggeus too spoke beautifully of the same thing. For when he had said, [[Agg 2:8|THE DESIRED OF ALL NATIONS SHALL COME|Veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus]], he added at once, [[Agg 2:8|and I will fill this house with glory: saith the Lord|Et implebo domum istam gloria, dicit Dominus]]. And to those who know the Scriptures it is certain that he speaks of the temple built in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian captivity: to the rebuilding of which he and Zacharias exhorted the Jews[[1 Esd 5:1||]][[1 Esd 5:2||]][[1 Esd 6:14||]]. And of the glory of this temple he goes on: [[Agg 2:10|Great shall be the glory of this last house more than of the first, saith the Lord|Magna erit gloria domus istius novissimæ, plus quam primæ, dicit Dominus]]. But this excellence of the last house over the temple built by Solomon lay in nothing except that Christ in his own person appeared in it, taught, and worked miracles. For otherwise that last temple was of no account beside the first temple built by Solomon. Hence it is written that when the second temple was built, those who had seen the first temple wept bitterly[[1 Esd 3:12||]], while those who had not seen it rejoiced greatly[[1 Esd 3:13||]]. From which a clear proof can be drawn that the King Messias has already come, and appeared in that temple which long ago was destroyed by the Romans.

paras.t: Secundum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: id est, secundum magnitudinem tuam seu nominis tui majestatem, diffusa est fama sublimitatis tuæ, et publicata dignitas tua, exhibeturque reverentia tibi in omnibus partibus mundi. Deo enim impenditur latriæ cultus, qui ei soli debetur: et ita secundum nomen suum ipse ubique honoratur, quamvis nemo possit ipsum laudare, amare, aut honorare, quantum ipse dignus exsistit. Et hoc est quod ipse Dominus apud Isaiam protestatur: Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum; gloriam meam alteri non dabo, et laudem meam sculptilibus. Quod autem secundum hoc nomen suum laudetur Deus in finibus terræ, ostendit Propheta protinus subdens: Cantate Domino canticum novum, laus ejus ab extremis terræ. Et iterum: Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt. Hoc Paulus apostolus impletum esse denuntians, ait, gentibus scribens: Conversi estis ad Deum a simulacris mutis, servire Deo viventi.
paras.en: [[47:11|According to thy name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth|Secundum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ]]: that is, according to thy greatness or the majesty of thy name, the fame of thy sublimity has been spread abroad, and thy dignity made known, and reverence is shown thee in all parts of the world. For to God is paid the worship of latria [that is, the worship of adoration, due to God alone], which is owed to him alone: and so he is honoured everywhere according to his name, though no one can praise, love or honour him as much as he is worthy. And this is what the Lord himself declares in Isaias: [[Is 42:8|I the Lord, this is my name: I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to graven things.|Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum; gloriam meam alteri non dabo, et laudem meam sculptilibus]] And that God is praised according to this name of his in the ends of the earth, the Prophet shows by adding straight away: [[Is 42:10|Sing ye to the Lord a new song, his praise is from the ends of the earth|Cantate Domino canticum novum, laus ejus ab extremis terræ]]. And again: [[Is 42:12|They shall give glory to the Lord, and shall declare his praise in the islands.|Ponent Domino gloriam, et laudem ejus in insulis nuntiabunt]] Paul the apostle, declaring that this has been fulfilled, says, writing to gentiles: [[1 Thess 1:9|you turned to God from idols|Conversi estis ad Deum a simulacris]], dumb idols, [[1 Thess 1:9|to serve the living and true God|servire Deo viventi]].

paras.t: Justitia plena est dextera tua: id est, gratiosa præsentia tua, pia protectio tua, seu propitiatio tua, o Domine, plena est æquitate. Inferius enim scriptum est, Justus Dominus in omnibus viis suis: quia dum impiis miseretur, juste facit ex parte suæ bonitatis, quoniam ipse tam bonus est, ut justum sit ipsum etiam indignis benefacere, ingratisque misereri; dum autem bonis gratiam dat, justum est tam ex parte sui, quam justorum. Vel sic: Justitia plena est dextera tua: id est, tu ipse omnino justus es, quoad illos qui in die judicii erunt ad dexteram tuam, quibus dicturus es, Percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est: in quibus omnia bona etiam minima remunerabis.
paras.en: [[47:11|thy right hand is full of justice|Justitia plena est dextera tua]]: that is, thy gracious presence, thy loving protection, or thy propitiation, O Lord, is full of equity. For it is written further on: [[Ps 144:17|The Lord is just in all his ways|Justus Dominus in omnibus viis suis]]: for when he has mercy on the wicked, he acts justly on the part of his own goodness, since he is so good that it is just for him to do good even to the unworthy and to have mercy on the ungrateful; and when he gives grace to the good, it is just both on his own part and on the part of the just. Or thus: [[47:11|thy right hand is full of justice|Justitia plena est dextera tua]]: that is, thou thyself art altogether just towards those who on the day of judgement shall be at thy right hand, to whom thou wilt say, [[Matt 25:34|possess you the kingdom prepared for you|Percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est]]: in whom thou wilt reward every good deed, even the least.

paras.t: Lætetur mons Sion, id est primitiva Ecclesia in monte Sion instituta et illuminata, sicut jam patuit, et exsultent filiæ Judæ, id est omnes successores primorum fidelium, seu omnes Ecclesiæ filii, qui sunt filiæ Judæ, id est filii confessionis laudis divinæ ac propriæ culpæ. Solent enim sancti Prophetæ nomine filiæ, vel in singulari, vel in plurali, totum populum designare. Unde Isaias ait: Descende, sede in pulvere, filia Babylon; et Zacharias, Exsulta satis, filia Sion; et Sophonias, Exsulta in omni corde tuo, filia Jerusalem. Ita hoc loco nomine filiarum Sion, intelligitur totus fidelium populus. Hi ergo exsultent propter judicia tua, Domine: quibus, cui vis misereris, et quem vis induras; quibus justos salvas, et impios damnas; quibus nihil inordinatum relinquis; quibus in præsenti vita bonos a malis discernis ac separas gratia, voto et merito, in futuro separaturus eosdem loco ac præmio. Hæc autem judicia Dei, sunt ipsemet Deus omnia judicans, vel effectus divinæ justitiæ.
paras.en: [[47:12|Let mount Sion rejoice|Lætetur mons Sion]], that is, the first Church, established and enlightened on mount Sion, as has already been shown, [[47:12|and the daughters of Juda be glad|et exsultent filiæ Judæ]], that is, all the successors of the first faithful, or all the sons of the Church, who are the daughters of Juda, that is, sons of confession, both of the divine praise and of their own guilt [the name Juda was taken to mean "confession", that is, both praise and the owning of sin]. For the holy Prophets are wont to signify the whole people by the name of daughter, either in the singular or in the plural. Hence Isaias says: [[Is 47:1|Come down, sit in the dust|Descende, sede in pulvere]], [[Is 47:1|daughter of Babylon|filia Babylon]]; and Zacharias: [[Zach 9:9|Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion|Exsulta satis, filia Sion]]; and Sophonias: [[Soph 3:14|rejoice with all thy heart, O daughter of Jerusalem|Exsulta in omni corde tuo, filia Jerusalem]]. So in this place by the name of the daughters of Sion is understood the whole people of the faithful. Let these, then, be glad [[47:12|because of thy judgments, O Lord|propter judicia tua, Domine]]: by which thou hast mercy on whom thou wilt and hardenest whom thou wilt; by which thou savest the just and condemnest the wicked; by which thou leavest nothing out of order; by which in the present life thou dost distinguish and separate the good from the wicked in grace, in will and in merit, and in the life to come wilt separate them in place and in reward. And these judgments of God are God himself judging all things, or the effects of the divine justice.

paras.t: Circumdate Sion: id est, Ecclesiam Christi verbo et opere defensate, nullum scandalizantes, pervertentes, aut opprimentes, sed fidem atque fideles totis viribus protegentes, confirmantes ac venerantes, ut vobis conveniat quod Habacuc ait: Super custodiam meam stabo, et figam gradum meum super munitionem, et contemplabor, etc. Hoc modo circumdedit Sion sacratissimus Isaias, qui ait: Super speculam Domini ego sum stans jugiter per diem, et super custodiam meam ego sum stans totis noctibus. Hoc ad prælatos Ecclesiæ potissimum pertinet.
paras.en: [[47:13|Surround Sion|Circumdate Sion]]: that is, defend the Church of Christ by word and deed, scandalizing, perverting or oppressing no one, but protecting, strengthening and reverencing the faith and the faithful with all your strength, so that what Habacuc says may fit you: [[Hab 2:1|I will stand upon my watch, and fix my foot upon the tower|Super custodiam meam stabo, et figam gradum meum super munitionem]], [[Hab 2:1|and I will watch|et contemplabor]], etc. In this way the most holy Isaias surrounded Sion, who says: [[Is 21:8|I am upon the watchtower of the Lord, standing continually by day: and I am upon my ward, standing whole nights|Super speculam Domini ego sum stans jugiter per diem, et super custodiam meam ego sum stans totis noctibus]]. This belongs above all to the prelates of the Church.

paras.t: Et complectimini eam: id est, cordiali affectu amate Ecclesiam, et omnia membra ipsius. Qui enim diligit proximum, legem implevit: quoniam plenitudo legis est dilectio. Propter quod Christus ait: Mandatum novum do vobis, ut diligatis invicem, sicut dilexi vos. Et iterum: In hoc cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem.
paras.en: [[47:13|and encompass her|Et complectimini eam]] [Denis's word *complectimini* means "embrace"]: that is, love the Church and all her members with heartfelt affection. For [[Rom 13:8|he that loveth his neighbour hath fulfilled the law|Qui enim diligit proximum, legem implevit]]: since [[Rom 13:10|Love therefore is the fulfilling of the law|plenitudo legis est dilectio]]. Hence Christ says: [[John 13:34|A new commandment I give unto you: That you love one another, as I have loved you|Mandatum novum do vobis, ut diligatis invicem, sicut dilexi vos]]. And again: [[John 13:35|By this shall all men know that you are my disciples, if you have love one for another.|In hoc cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem]]

paras.t: Narrate in turribus ejus: id est, in Ecclesiis prædicate Evangelium Christi. Vel: Narrate in turribus ejus, id est, principibus atque prælatis fidelium annuntiate Christi doctrinam, o prædicatores verbi Dei, quatenus secundum Christi præcepta vivant, aliosque gubernent. Secundum quod Paulus Ecclesiæ turribus, id est aliorum pastoribus, dicit: Attendite vobis et universo gregi, in quo posuit vos Spiritus Sanctus episcopos, regere Ecclesiam Dei, quam acquisivit sanguine suo. Et Petrus: Seniores (inquit) obsecro, pascite qui in vobis est gregem, forma gregis effecti ex animo.
paras.en: [[47:13|tell ye in her towers|Narrate in turribus ejus]]: that is, preach the Gospel of Christ in the Churches. Or: [[47:13|tell ye in her towers|Narrate in turribus ejus]], that is, proclaim the doctrine of Christ to the princes and prelates of the faithful, O preachers of the word of God, so that they may live according to Christ's precepts and govern others. According as Paul says to the towers of the Church, that is, to the shepherds of others: [[Acts 20:28|Take heed to yourselves and to the whole flock, wherein the Holy Ghost hath placed you bishops, to rule the Church of God which he hath purchased with his own blood.|Attendite vobis et universo gregi, in quo posuit vos Spiritus Sanctus episcopos, regere Ecclesiam Dei, quam acquisivit sanguine suo]] And Peter: [[1 Pet 5:1|The ancients|Seniores]] (he says) [[1 Pet 5:1|I beseech|obsecro]]: [[1 Pet 5:2|Feed the flock of God which is among you|pascite qui in vobis est gregem]], [[1 Pet 5:3|being made a pattern of the flock from the heart|forma gregis effecti ex animo]].

paras.t: Ponite corda vestra in virtute ejus: id est, applicate mentem vestram ad cognoscendum ac imitandum perfectionem, seu caritatem Ecclesiæ, ut sitis viva ac digna Christi membra, et non servi inutiles, ne projiciamini in tenebras exteriores; et distribuite domos ejus, id est, ipsos Ecclesiæ filios ordinate, et unicuique proprium officium deputate: quatenus, sicut ait Apostolus, omnia decenter et secundum ordinem fiant in vobis; sicque unusquisque digne ambulet ea vocatione qua vocatus est. Unde Moyses ait: Non transferes terminos, quos fixerunt priores in possessione tua. Quod planius allegari solet hoc modo: Non transgrediaris terminos antiquos, quos posuerunt patres tui. Et Dionysius sæpe affirmat, quod angeli sancti nequaquam præsumunt aliquid agere, nisi secundum quod eis a lege divina præfixum est. Et nos ergo custodiamus ordinem nostrum, faciatque unusquisque quod sibi incumbit; nec occupet se cum his quæ ad ipsum non pertinent, quia nec aliter veram ac stabilem pacem habere poterimus.
paras.en: [[47:14|Set your hearts on her strength|Ponite corda vestra in virtute ejus]] [*virtus* is both "strength" and "virtue"]: that is, apply your mind to knowing and imitating the perfection, or the charity, of the Church, so that you may be living and worthy members of Christ, and not unprofitable servants, lest you be cast out into the exterior darkness; [[47:14|and distribute her houses|et distribuite domos ejus]], that is, set the sons of the Church themselves in order, and assign to each his proper office: so that, as the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 14:40|let all things be done decently and according to order|omnia decenter et secundum ordinem fiant]] among you; and so each one may walk worthily in the calling in which he is called [an echo of Eph 4:1 and 1 Cor 7:20]. Hence Moses says: [[Deut 19:14|Thou shalt not take nor remove thy neighbour's landmark, which thy predecessors have set in thy possession|Non transferes terminos, quos fixerunt priores in possessione tua]] [Denis leaves out "take nor" and "thy neighbour's"]. Which is more commonly cited in this way: [[Prov 22:28|Pass not beyond the ancient bounds which thy fathers have set.|Non transgrediaris terminos antiquos, quos posuerunt patres tui]] [these words are in fact Prov 22:28]. And Dionysius often affirms that the holy angels never presume to do anything except as it has been laid down for them by the divine law. Let us too, then, keep our order, and let each one do what falls to him; and let him not busy himself with things that do not concern him, for in no other way shall we be able to have true and lasting peace.

paras.t: Hæc itaque agite, o doctores, et aliorum rectores, ut enarretis in progenie altera, id est, quatenus successores vestros instruatis, quum audierint vitam vestram laudabilem salutaremque doctrinam.
paras.en: Do these things, then, O teachers and rulers of others, [[47:14|that ye may relate it in another generation|ut enarretis in progenie altera]], that is, so that you may instruct your successors when they hear of your praiseworthy life and your saving doctrine.

paras.t: Quid autem enarrare posteris debeant, subdit: Quoniam hic, id est Christus qui propter nos incarnatus ac passus est, est Deus omnium, tanquam creator, Deus noster, tanquam noster salvator, in æternum et in sæculum sæculi, id est in præsenti sæculo et in futuro sine fine; ipse reget nos in sæcula, id est, quamdiu fuerimus. Regit enim Christus nos per sacram Scripturam, in qua docemur quid agere debeamus; item per angelorum custodiam, per vicarios quoque suos Ecclesiarum pastores; et etiam per semetipsum, gratiam et dona Sancti Spiritus infundendo, per quæ in omnibus scimus quid Deo sit placitum. Propter quod in libro Sapientiæ dicitur: Justum deduxit Dominus per vias rectas, et ostendit illi regnum Dei. Quod autem in hoc versu jam dictum est, hoc idem Ecclesiæ Christi promittitur alibi: Lauda, filia Sion; jubila, Israel; lætare et exsulta in omni corde, filia Jerusalem. Abstulit Dominus judicium tuum, avertit inimicos tuos; Dominus Deus tuus in medio tui fortis, ipse salvabit te; gaudebit super te Dominus in lætitia, silebit in dilectione tua.
paras.en: And what they ought to relate to those who come after, he goes on to say: [[47:15|For this|Quoniam hic]], that is, Christ, who for our sake became incarnate and suffered, [[47:15|is God|est Deus]] of all, as creator, [[47:15|our God|Deus noster]], as our saviour, [[47:15|unto eternity, and for ever and ever|in æternum et in sæculum sæculi]], that is, in the present age and in the age to come without end; [[47:15|he shall rule us for evermore|ipse reget nos in sæcula]], that is, as long as we shall be. For Christ rules us through holy Scripture, in which we are taught what we ought to do; through the guardianship of the angels too, and through his vicars, the shepherds of the Churches; and also through himself, by pouring in the grace and gifts of the Holy Ghost, through which we know in all things what is pleasing to God. Hence it is said in the book of Wisdom: The Lord [[Wis 10:10|conducted the just|Justum deduxit]] [[Wis 10:10|through the right ways, and shewed him the kingdom of God|per vias rectas, et ostendit illi regnum Dei]] [the Vulgate has *Hæc*, "she", that is, Wisdom, where Denis has *Dominus*]. And what has been said in this verse is promised to the Church of Christ in the same way elsewhere: [[Soph 3:14|Give praise, O daughter of Sion: shout, O Israel: be glad, and rejoice with all thy heart, O daughter of Jerusalem.|Lauda, filia Sion; jubila, Israel; lætare et exsulta in omni corde, filia Jerusalem]] [[Soph 3:15|The Lord hath taken away thy judgment, he hath turned away thy enemies|Abstulit Dominus judicium tuum, avertit inimicos tuos]]: [[Soph 3:17|The Lord thy God in the midst of thee is mighty, he will save: he will rejoice over thee with gladness, he will be silent in his love|Dominus Deus tuus in medio tui fortis, ipse salvabit te; gaudebit super te Dominus in lætitia, silebit in dilectione tua]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmus iste, in profunditate sensuum plenus, quam copiose ac splendide describit mysteria Christi, exordiumque Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: See how richly and splendidly this psalm, full of depth of meaning, describes the mysteries of Christ and the beginning of the Church.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Qui es magnus Dominus et laudabilis nimis in omnibus creaturis tuis, suscipe nos ad te respirantes in misericordia tua; pone corda nostra in virtute tua: et tu, Deus noster, rege nos in æterna sæcula, qui in Trinitate perfecta vivis et regnas Deus.
paras.en: Prayer. O thou who art the great Lord and [[47:2|exceedingly to be praised|laudabilis nimis]] in all thy creatures, receive us, who sigh after thee, in thy mercy; set our hearts on thy strength: and do thou, our God, rule us for ever and ever, who in perfect Trinity livest and reignest God.

48.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI QUADRAGESIMI OCTAVI : AUDITE HÆC, OMNES GENTES.
48.title_en: Exposition of the forty-eighth psalm: Hear these things, all ye nations.

paras.t: Elucidandi nunc psalmi titulus talis est: In finem, filiis Core, psalmus: id est, psalmus præsens, in finem, id est in Christum et veram felicitatem nos dirigens, convenit filiis Core, id est, imitatoribus Christi occisi, qui Christum sequentes, temporalem prosperitatem contemnunt, et veram beatitudinem patriæ quærunt. Loquitur namque hic psalmus contra eos, qui tunc scandalizantur et cadunt, dum aliquid adversitatis eis occurrit; dum vero omnia prospera sibi succedunt, Deum glorificant.
paras.en: The title of the psalm now to be explained is this: [[48:1|Unto the end, a psalm for the sons of Core|In finem, filiis Core, psalmus]]: that is, the present psalm, [[48:1|Unto the end|in finem]], that is, directing us to Christ and to true happiness, befits [[48:1|the sons of Core|filiis Core]], that is, the imitators of Christ who was slain, who, following Christ, despise temporal prosperity and seek the true beatitude of the fatherland. For this psalm speaks against those who are scandalized and fall whenever some adversity befalls them, but glorify God while all things go prosperously for them.

paras.t: De quibus ait Salvator: Quum audierint verbum Dei, cum gaudio suscipiunt illud: et hi radices non habent, quia ad tempus credunt, et in tempore tentationis recedunt. Cujus recessionis causam Christus assignans, alibi ait: Ærumnæ sæculi et deceptio divitiarum et circa reliqua concupiscentiæ, introeuntes in cor, suffocant verbum Dei, et sine fructu efficitur. De prædictis quoque per Malachiam scriptum est: Dixistis: Vanus est qui servit Domino; et quod emolumentum, quia custodivimus præcepta ejus, et quia ambulavimus tristes coram Domino? Ergo beatos nunc dicimus arrogantes: siquidem ædificati sunt, facientes impietatem.
paras.en: Of these the Saviour says: [[Luke 8:13|when they hear receive the word with joy: and these have no roots: for they believe for a while and in time of temptation they fall away|Quum audierint verbum Dei, cum gaudio suscipiunt illud: et hi radices non habent, quia ad tempus credunt, et in tempore tentationis recedunt]]. Assigning the cause of this falling away, Christ says elsewhere: [[Mark 4:19|the cares of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts after other things entering in choke the word, and it is made fruitless|Ærumnæ sæculi et deceptio divitiarum et circa reliqua concupiscentiæ, introeuntes in cor, suffocant verbum Dei, et sine fructu efficitur]]. Of the same it is also written by Malachias: You have said: [[Mal 3:14|He laboureth in vain that serveth God, and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinances, and that we have walked sorrowful before the Lord|Vanus est qui servit Domino; et quod emolumentum, quia custodivimus præcepta ejus, et quia ambulavimus tristes coram Domino?]]? [[Mal 3:15|Wherefore now we call the proud people happy, for they that work wickedness are built up|Ergo beatos nunc dicimus arrogantes: siquidem ædificati sunt, facientes impietatem]].

paras.t: Contra hos igitur locuturus Propheta, præmittit proœmium, quatenus attentos nos reddat, et dicit: Audite hæc, quæ sequuntur, omnes gentes, quia ad omnium vestrum salutem respiciunt, nec ignorantia horum vos excusat; auribus cordis et corporis percipite, omnes qui habitatis orbem, id est homines universi. Quique terrigenæ et filii hominum. Idem frequenter resumit, ut omnino nos sollicitos efficiat. Simul in unum dives et pauper, quia commune bonum vobis proponam.
paras.en: Against these, then, the Prophet, being about to speak, first sets down a proem, so as to make us attentive, and says: [[48:2|Hear these things|Audite hæc]], which follow, [[48:2|all ye nations|omnes gentes]], because they concern the salvation of all of you, and ignorance of them does not excuse you; [[48:2|give ear|percipite]] with the ears of heart and of body, [[48:2|all ye inhabitants of the world|omnes qui habitatis orbem]], that is, all men without exception. [[48:3|All you that are earthborn, and you sons of men|Quique terrigenæ et filii hominum]]. He takes up the same thing again and again, so as to make us altogether attentive.
