[[48:3|both rich and poor together|Simul in unum dives et pauper]], because I will set before you a good common to all.

paras.t: Os meum loquetur in psalmo isto sapientiam, id est notitiam de rebus divinis. Tractat enim in psalmo isto quædam de Deo et beatitudine vera, quæ est vita æterna. Et meditatio cordis mei loquetur per os corporis prudentiam, id est moralem scientiam. Aliqua namque in psalmo præsenti tractantur ad formationem morum spectantia, sicut patebit.
paras.en: [[48:4|My mouth shall speak|Os meum loquetur]] in this psalm [[48:4|wisdom|sapientiam]], that is, knowledge of divine things. For in this psalm he treats certain things concerning God and true beatitude, which is life everlasting. [[48:4|and the meditation of my heart|Et meditatio cordis mei]] shall speak through the mouth of the body [[48:4|understanding|prudentiam]] [Latin prudentia, prudence, the virtue that directs action], that is, moral knowledge. For some things are treated in the present psalm that bear on the forming of morals, as will appear.

paras.t: Inclinabo in parabolam aurem meam: id est, ad intelligendum occultas seu mysticas inspirationes atque aliorum Sanctorum scripturas parabolice traditas, applicabo ingenium meum. Unde in Ecclesiastico habetur: Sapientiam omnium antiquorum exquiret sapiens, et in Prophetis vacabit. Aperiam in psalterio, id est in præsenti psalmo hujus libri, qui Psalterium nuncupatur, propositionem meam, id est cordis mei conceptum. Vel, In psalterio, id est in bona operatione, ita quod non solum dicam, quæ dicturus sum, ore et lingua, sed opere et veritate. Hoc enim necesse est, ut vita concordet doctrinæ. Nam cujus vita despicitur, ejus quoque instructio vilipenditur.
paras.en: [[48:5|I will incline my ear to a parable|Inclinabo in parabolam aurem meam]]: that is, I will apply my mind to understanding hidden or mystical inspirations, and the writings of the other Saints handed down in parables. Whence it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 39:1|The wise man will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients, and will be occupied in the prophets|Sapientiam omnium antiquorum exquiret sapiens, et in Prophetis vacabit]]. [[48:5|I will open|Aperiam]] [[48:5|on the psaltery|in psalterio]], that is, in the present psalm of this book, which is called the Psalter, [[48:5|my proposition|propositionem meam]], that is, the conception of my heart. Or, [[48:5|on the psaltery|In psalterio]], that is, in good works [the psaltery, an instrument played with the hands, stands for the work of the hands], so that I shall say what I am to say not only with mouth and tongue, but in deed and in truth. For this is necessary, that the life agree with the teaching; for when a man's life is despised, his instruction too is held cheap.

paras.t: Hucusque proœmium: et utique nisi quæ sequuntur valde notabilia essent, nequaquam Propheta tam præclarum prologum induxisset. Narrationem ergo incipiens, quæstionem proponit: Cur timebo in die malo? id est, quid poterit mihi in die judicii esse causa timoris? vel, cur tunc timebo, si pœnitentiam modo non egero? Et hanc quæstionem proponit in persona universorum, maxime peccatorum. Et respondet: Iniquitas calcanei mei, id est operationis meæ (per calcaneum enim seu pedem, gressus et conversatio seu operatio designatur), circumdabit me, id est, undique objicietur mihi, et redundabit in me. In die namque judicii accusabitur homo a dæmonibus, ab angelis, a conscientia propria: imo et a Judice ipso, quemadmodum Dominus ait per Malachiam: Accedam ad vos in judicio, et ero testis velox maleficis et adulteris, et qui calumniantur et opprimunt pauperem, et non timuerunt me. Et Isaias ait: Ecce nomen Domini venit de longinquo; ardens furor ejus et gravis ad portandum. Labia ejus repleta sunt indignatione, et lingua ejus quasi ignis devorans; spiritus ejus velut torrens inundans usque ad medium colli, ad perdendas gentes in nihilum. Hæc ergo est causa timendi futurum judicium, quia operationum nostrarum iniquitas tunc circumdabit nos. Propter quod in Apocalypsi dicitur: Opera illorum sequuntur illos. Et Salvator ait: Amen dico vobis, nisi pœnitentiam egeritis, omnes similiter peribitis. Dicitur autem dies judicii mala, non a malitia culpæ, quum sit dies justissimæ remunerationis, prudentissimæ discretionis, et districtissimæ examinationis; sed a malitia pœnæ, quia multa mala pœnalia erunt in eo, quemadmodum Sophonias testatur: Dies iræ dies illa, dies tribulationis et angustiæ, dies calamitatis et miseriæ, dies tenebrarum et caliginis, dies nebulæ et turbinis, dies tubæ et clangoris. Ecce quam horrenda ac horribilissima dies, cujus horrorem tot nominibus Propheta explicare curavit.
paras.en: So far the proem: and surely, were not what follows very notable, the Prophet would never have brought in so splendid a prologue. Beginning the narration, then, he puts a question: [[48:6|Why shall I fear in the evil day?|Cur timebo in die malo?]] that is, what can be a cause of fear to me in the day of judgment? or, why shall I fear then, if I do not do penance now? And he puts this question in the person of all men, above all of sinners. And he answers: [[48:6|the iniquity of my heel|Iniquitas calcanei mei]], that is, of my working (for by the heel, or foot, are signified a man's steps and conduct, or working), [[48:6|shall encompass me|circumdabit me]], that is, it shall be cast up against me on every side, and shall redound upon me. For in the day of judgment a man will be accused by the demons, by the angels, by his own conscience: nay, by the Judge himself, as the Lord says by Malachias: [[Mal 3:5|I will come to you in judgment, and will be a speedy witness against sorcerers, and adulterers|Accedam ad vos in judicio, et ero testis velox maleficis et adulteris]], and against them that calumniate and oppress the poor, and [[Mal 3:5|have not feared me|non timuerunt me]]. And Isaias says: [[Is 30:27|Behold the name of the Lord cometh from afar, his wrath burneth, and is heavy to bear: his lips are filled with indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire|Ecce nomen Domini venit de longinquo; ardens furor ejus et gravis ad portandum. Labia ejus repleta sunt indignatione, et lingua ejus quasi ignis devorans]]; [[Is 30:28|His breath as a torrent overflowing even to the midst of the neck, to destroy the nations unto nothing|spiritus ejus velut torrens inundans usque ad medium colli, ad perdendas gentes in nihilum]]. This, then, is the cause for fearing the judgment to come: that the iniquity of our works will then encompass us. For which reason it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 14:13|their works follow them|Opera illorum sequuntur illos]]. And the Saviour says: Amen I say to you, [[Luke 13:5|except you do penance, you shall all likewise perish|nisi pœnitentiam egeritis, omnes similiter peribitis]]. Now the day of judgment is called evil not from the evil of guilt, since it will be a day of most just requital, most prudent discernment, and most strict examination; but from the evil of punishment [the schoolmen's distinction between the evil of guilt, that is, sin, and the evil of punishment, that is, the suffering that is its penalty], because many penal evils will be in it, as Sophonias testifies: [[Soph 1:15|That day is a day of wrath, a day of tribulation and distress, a day of calamity and misery, a day of darkness and obscurity, a day of clouds and whirlwinds|Dies iræ dies illa, dies tribulationis et angustiæ, dies calamitatis et miseriæ, dies tenebrarum et caliginis, dies nebulæ et turbinis]], [[Soph 1:16|A day of the trumpet and alarm|dies tubæ et clangoris]]. Behold how dreadful and most horrible a day, whose horror the Prophet has taken care to set forth under so many names.

paras.t: Qui in virtute sua confidunt, id est, qui propriis viribus se posse salvari præsumunt, et in sæculari, naturali, seu corporali potentia sperant, non in misericordia et gratia Creatoris, et in multitudine divitiarum suarum gloriantur, id est, in possessionibus seu propriis meritis atque justitiis inordinate lætantur, non omnium largitori gratias referendo, sed in se ipsis quasi non acceperint, jucundando, aut alios contemnendo. Hi tales timeant, quia in die mala evadere non valebunt: quod consequenter ostendit.
paras.en: [[48:7|They that trust in their own strength|Qui in virtute sua confidunt]], that is, who presume that they can be saved by their own powers, and hope in worldly, natural or bodily might, not in the mercy and grace of the Creator, [[48:7|and glory in the multitude of their riches|et in multitudine divitiarum suarum gloriantur]], that is, who rejoice inordinately in their possessions, or in their own merits and righteous deeds, not returning thanks to the giver of all things, but delighting in themselves as though they had not received them, or despising others. Let such as these fear, for they will not be able to escape in the evil day: which he goes on to show.

paras.t: Frater non redimit, id est, nullus consanguineus seu propinquus alium liberare poterit in die judicii, secundum quod apud Ezechielem Dominus protestatur: Terra quum peccaverit, interficiam de ea hominem et jumentum. Et si fuerint tres viri isti in medio ejus, Noe, Daniel et Job, ipsi in justitia sua liberabunt animas suas, filium autem et filiam non liberabunt. Et rursus ait idem Propheta: Justitia justi erit super eum, et impietas impii erit super eum. Quum ergo sit ita, redimet homo? Quod interrogative legendum est, ut sit sensus: Si propinquus et frater non redimet peccatorem, multo minus homo, id est alius quicumque extraneus, seu remotus et minus propinquus, redimere poterit alium. Unde et alibi Dominus ait: Si steterint Moyses et Samuel coram me, non est anima mea ad populum istum. Non dabit Deo placationem suam: id est, peccator in die judicii Deum placare non poterit, quia post mortem non patet precum meritorumve locus, nec est tunc pœnitentia fructuosa: secundum quod Christus innuit de virginibus fatuis sero venientibus atque dicentibus, Domine, Domine, aperi nobis: quibus ipse respondet, Amen dico vobis, nescio vos. Hæc quippe vita est via ad vitam futuram: idcirco hac vita finita, cessat modus merendi ac demerendi, sicque ad aliam vitam pertingendi; sed per mortem ponitur homo in termino motus. Unde Damascenus: Quod angelo, inquit, est casus, hoc hominibus est mors.
paras.en: [[48:8|No brother can redeem|Frater non redimit]], that is, no kinsman or relative will be able to set another free in the day of judgment, according to what the Lord declares in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 14:13|when a land shall sin|Terra quum peccaverit]], I [[Ezech 14:13|will destroy man and beast out of it|interficiam de ea hominem et jumentum]]. [[Ezech 14:14|And if these three men, Noe, Daniel, and Job, shall be in it: they shall deliver their own souls by their justice|Et si fuerint tres viri isti in medio ejus, Noe, Daniel et Job, ipsi in justitia sua liberabunt animas suas]]: but [[Ezech 14:20|they shall deliver neither son nor daughter|filium autem et filiam non liberabunt]] [the margin gives Ezech. xiv, 13, 14, 16; these last words are closer to Ezech 14:20]. And again the same Prophet says: [[Ezech 18:20|the justice of the just shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him|Justitia justi erit super eum, et impietas impii erit super eum]] [the margin gives Ezech. xiv, 20; the words are those of Ezech 18:20]. Since, then, it is so, [[48:8|nor shall man redeem|redimet homo]]? This is to be read as a question [Denis reads redimet homo as "shall man redeem?", where the Douay-Rheims has "nor shall man redeem"], so that the sense is: if a kinsman and brother will not redeem the sinner, much less will a man, that is, any other, a stranger, or one far off and less near, be able to redeem another. Whence the Lord says elsewhere too: [[Jer 15:1|If Moses and Samuel shall stand before me, my soul is not towards this people|Si steterint Moyses et Samuel coram me, non est anima mea ad populum istum]]. [[48:8|he shall not give to God his ransom|Non dabit Deo placationem suam]]: that is, the sinner will not be able to appease God in the day of judgment, because after death there is no room left for prayers or merits, nor is penance then fruitful: as Christ indicates of the foolish virgins, who come late and say, [[Matt 25:11|Lord, Lord, open to us|Domine, Domine, aperi nobis]]; to whom he answers, [[Matt 25:12|Amen I say to you, I know you not|Amen dico vobis, nescio vos]]. For this life is the way to the life to come: and so, when this life is ended, the means of meriting and demeriting, and so of reaching the other life, ceases; and by death a man is set at the term of his movement [in termino motus, a scholastic phrase: at the end where his course stops, so that his state can no longer change]. Whence Damascene: What the fall is to the angel, he says, that death is to men.

paras.t: Et pretium redemptionis animæ suæ: id est, peccator post mortem nullo genere satisfaciendi poterit animam suam a debita pœna eruere.
paras.en: [[48:9|Nor the price of the redemption of his soul|Et pretium redemptionis animæ suæ]]: that is, after death the sinner will not be able by any kind of satisfaction to rescue his soul from the punishment due.

paras.t: Ecce quam terribilis Deus post mortem, qui ante mortem tam misericordissime præstolatur, sicut et Isaias ait: Propterea exspectat Dominus, ut misereatur vestri. Nemo igitur nostrum in sua virtute confidat, nemo in sua sapientia, nemo in suis meritis glorietur, ne sibi conveniat quod ait Jeremias propheta: Arrogantia tua et superbia cordis tui decepit te. Illud quoque Isaiæ: Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris. Qui iterum ait: Sapientia tua et scientia tua deceperunt te. Sed et in spiritualibus divitiis glorianti, Joannes ait in Apocalypsi: Dicis, Quia dives sum, et nullius egeo; et nescis quia tu es miser, et miserabilis, et pauper, et cæcus, et nudus. Divitibus vero, in corporalibus divitiis gloriantibus, apud Lucam dicitur: Væ vobis divitibus qui habetis consolationem vestram.
paras.en: Behold how terrible God is after death, who before death waits for us so most mercifully, as Isaias also says: [[Is 30:18|Therefore the Lord waiteth that he may have mercy on you|Propterea exspectat Dominus, ut misereatur vestri]] [the margin gives Is. xxx, 16; the words are Is 30:18]. Let none of us, then, trust in his own strength, none in his own wisdom, let none glory in his own merits, lest there apply to him what Jeremias the prophet says: [[Jer 49:16|Thy arrogancy hath deceived thee, and the pride of thy heart|Arrogantia tua et superbia cordis tui decepit te]]. And that too of Isaias: [[Is 5:21|Woe to you that are wise in your own eyes|Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris]]. Who says again: [[Is 47:10|Thy wisdom, and, thy knowledge, this hath deceived thee|Sapientia tua et scientia tua deceperunt te]]. And to him who glories in spiritual riches John says in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:17|thou sayest: I am rich|Dicis, Quia dives sum]] [[Apoc 3:17|and have need of nothing: and knowest not that thou art wretched and miserable and poor and blind and naked|et nullius egeo; et nescis quia tu es miser, et miserabilis, et pauper, et cæcus, et nudus]]. But to the rich, who glory in bodily riches, it is said in Luke: [[Luke 6:24|woe to you that are rich: for you have your consolation|Væ vobis divitibus qui habetis consolationem vestram]].

paras.t: Deinceps ponitur pœna malorum, qui in finali judicio damnabuntur. Et laborabit in æternum: id est, impius æternaliter affligetur, et laboriosissima pœna torquebitur, quemadmodum scriptum est: Cruciabitur iniquus igne et sulfure in conspectu angelorum sanctorum; et fumus tormentorum ejus ascendet in sæcula sæculorum, et requiem non habebit die ac nocte.
paras.en: Next is set down the punishment of the wicked who will be damned at the final judgment. [[48:9|and shall labour for ever|Et laborabit in æternum]]: that is, the wicked man will be afflicted eternally, and tormented with a most toilsome punishment, as it is written: The wicked man [[Apoc 14:10|shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the sight of the holy angels|Cruciabitur iniquus igne et sulfure in conspectu angelorum sanctorum]]; [[Apoc 14:11|And the smoke of their torments, shall ascend up for ever and ever|et fumus tormentorum ejus ascendet in sæcula sæculorum]], and, [[Apoc 14:11|neither have they rest day nor night|requiem non habebit die ac nocte]].

paras.t: Et vivet adhuc in finem, id est, naturalem vitam nunquam amittet, quamvis eam amittere cupiet, sed æternaliter vivet in natura, ut incessabiliter perseveret in pœna. Propter quod Joannes ait: In diebus illis quærent homines mortem, et non invenient eam: et desiderabunt mori, et fugiet mors ab eis. Nec dissonat quod alibi legitur: Eligent magis mortem quam vitam, omnes qui residui fuerint de generatione hac pessima. Quamvis enim, secundum philosophos, omne ens naturaliter appetat esse, omneque vivens naturaliter appetat vivere, tamen reprobi in inferno appetent non esse, et non vivere: quoniam propter miseriæ vehementiam superabitur appetitus naturalis ab appetitu sensitivo seu intellectivo. Quod vero de peccatore jam dictum est, Laborabit in æternum, et vivet adhuc in finem, consonat ei quod de reprobis in Daniele scriptum est, Evigilabunt de pulvere in opprobrium ut videant semper. O quanta miseria, et quam odibile esse, semper esse, et nunquam bene esse, æternaliter permanere, et non ob aliud nisi ut æternaliter compellatur tormenta sentire! Unde ob tam infelicem ac pœnalissimum statum maledicti in inferno Deum verum et sanctum incessanter blasphemant, sicut in Apocalypsi legitur: Commanducaverunt linguas suas præ dolore, et blasphemaverunt Deum cœli præ doloribus et vulneribus suis.
paras.en: [[48:10|And shall still live unto the end|Et vivet adhuc in finem]], that is, he will never lose his natural life, though he will long to lose it, but will live eternally in his nature, so as to remain unceasingly in punishment. For which reason John says: [[Apoc 9:6|in those days, men shall seek death and shall not find it. And they shall desire to die: and death shall fly from them|In diebus illis quærent homines mortem, et non invenient eam: et desiderabunt mori, et fugiet mors ab eis]]. Nor is that out of tune with it which is read elsewhere: [[Jer 8:3|death shall be chosen rather than life by all that shall remain of this wicked kindred|Eligent magis mortem quam vitam, omnes qui residui fuerint de generatione hac pessima]]. For although, according to the philosophers, every being naturally desires to be, and every living thing naturally desires to live, yet the reprobate in hell will desire not to be and not to live: since, through the vehemence of their misery, the natural appetite will be overcome by the sensitive or intellective appetite. And what has just been said of the sinner, [[48:9|and shall labour for ever|Laborabit in æternum]], [[48:10|And shall still live unto the end|et vivet adhuc in finem]], agrees with what is written of the reprobate in Daniel: They [[Dan 12:2|shall awake|Evigilabunt]] from the dust [[Dan 12:2|unto reproach, to see it always|in opprobrium ut videant semper]]. O how great a misery, and how hateful a being: always to be, and never to be well; to endure eternally, and for no other end than to be forced eternally to feel torments! Whence, because of so unhappy and most penal a state, the accursed in hell unceasingly blaspheme the true and holy God, as is read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 16:10|they gnawed their tongues for pain|Commanducaverunt linguas suas præ dolore]], [[Apoc 16:11|And they blasphemed the God of heaven, because of their pains and wounds|et blasphemaverunt Deum cœli præ doloribus et vulneribus suis]].

paras.t: Non videbit interitum, id est, peccator non considerabit post mortem temporalem instare et esse mortem æternam malignis, quum viderit sapientes, id est homines doctos et virtuosos, morientes corporaliter, sicut et ceteri moriuntur. Multi enim, ex hoc quod vident bonos et malos, sapientes et insipientes, quoad præsentem statum corporalemque vitam, æqualiter pertransire ac mori, putant non esse vitam aliam quam præsentem. Ex quorum persona in libro Sapientiæ scriptum est: Non est qui agnitus sit reversus ab inferis. Quia ex nihilo nati sumus, et post hæc erimus quasi non fuerimus. Venite ergo, fruamur bonis quæ sunt, etc. Et alibi: Manducemus et bibamus, cras enim moriemur.
paras.en: [[48:11|He shall not see destruction|Non videbit interitum]], that is, the sinner will not consider that after temporal death there awaits the wicked, and there is, an eternal death, [[48:11|when he shall see the wise|quum viderit sapientes]], that is, learned and virtuous men, [[48:11|dying|morientes]] in the body, just as the rest die. For many, from seeing that the good and the wicked, the wise and the unwise, pass away and die alike as far as the present state and bodily life go, think there is no other life than the present. In whose person it is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 2:1|no man hath been known to have returned from hell|Non est qui agnitus sit reversus ab inferis]]. [[Wis 2:2|For we are born of nothing, and after this we shall be as if we had not been|Quia ex nihilo nati sumus, et post hæc erimus quasi non fuerimus]]. [[Wis 2:6|Come, therefore, and let us enjoy the good things that are present|Venite ergo, fruamur bonis quæ sunt]], etc. [the margin gives Sap. vii, 1, 2, 6; the passage is Wis 2:1, 2, 6] And elsewhere: [[1 Cor 15:32|Let us eat and drink, for to morrow we shall die|Manducemus et bibamus, cras enim moriemur]] [no margin reference; the words stand in Is 22:13 and, as Denis gives them, in 1 Cor 15:32].

paras.t: Simul insipiens, id est divina non cognoscens, sed diabolice vivens, et stultus, id est nec sciens, nec operans bona, peribunt morte perpetua, sicut Apostolus ait: Qui ignorat, ignorabitur. Et relinquent alienis divitias suas, id est, insipiens et stultus dimittent possessiones suas extraneis. Unde de peccatore superius dictum est: Thesaurizat, et ignorat cui congregabit ea.
paras.en: [[48:11|the senseless|Simul insipiens]], that is, one who does not know divine things but lives devilishly, [[48:11|and the fool|et stultus]], that is, one who neither knows nor does good things, [[48:11|shall perish together|peribunt]] by everlasting death, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 14:38|if any man know not, he shall not be known|Qui ignorat, ignorabitur]] [the margin gives 1 Cor. xv, 3 (number partly unread); the words are 1 Cor 14:38]. [[48:11|And they shall leave their riches to strangers|Et relinquent alienis divitias suas]], that is, the senseless and the fool will leave their possessions to outsiders. Whence it was said above of the sinner: [[Ps 38:7|He storeth up: and he knoweth not for whom he shall gather these things|Thesaurizat, et ignorat cui congregabit ea]].

paras.t: Et sepulcra eorum, domus illorum in æternum: id est, impii secundum suam perfidiam æstimabunt se nunquam de terra surrecturos, sed in terra penitus relinquendos: quia non credunt quod apud Danielem legitur, Qui in pulvere dormiunt, evigilabunt; et quod sanctus Job profitetur, Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum.
paras.en: [[48:12|And their sepulchres shall be their houses for ever|Et sepulcra eorum, domus illorum in æternum]]: that is, the wicked, in keeping with their unbelief, will suppose that they will never rise again from the earth, but be left wholly in the earth: because they do not believe what is read in Daniel, [[Dan 12:2|those that sleep in the dust of the earth, shall awake|Qui in pulvere dormiunt, evigilabunt]]; and what holy Job professes, [[Job 19:25|I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]].

paras.t: Tabernacula eorum in progenie et progenie: id est, domus ab impiis ædificatæ, manent per generationes successorum suorum. Construunt enim sibi nonnunquam magna palatia, quatenus tamdiu maneant in memoriis hominum, quamdiu durant eorum structuræ. Quoniam enim non ponunt vitam futuram post istam, desiderant saltem in memoria hominum permanere. Ideo subditur, vocaverunt nomina sua in terris suis, id est, memorialia aliqua studuerunt relinquere posteris, ne oblivioni tradantur. Unde in Genesi filii hominum dixisse leguntur: Venite, construamus turrem, cujus altitudo usque ad cœlos pertingat, et celebremus nomen nostrum super terram.
paras.en: [[48:12|Their dwelling places to all generations|Tabernacula eorum in progenie et progenie]]: that is, the houses built by the wicked remain through the generations of their successors. For they sometimes build themselves great palaces, so that they may remain in men's memories as long as their buildings last. For since they do not hold that there is a life to come after this one, they desire at least to remain in the memory of men. Therefore it is added, [[48:12|they have called their lands by their names|vocaverunt nomina sua in terris suis]], that is, they have been eager to leave some memorials to posterity, lest they be given over to oblivion. Whence in Genesis the sons of men are read to have said: [[Gen 11:4|Come, let us make|Venite, construamus]] [[Gen 11:4|a tower, the top whereof may reach to heaven|turrem, cujus altitudo usque ad cœlos pertingat]], [[Gen 11:4|and let us make our name famous|et celebremus nomen nostrum]] upon the earth [the margin gives Gen. xi, 3; the words, freely given, are those of Gen 11:4].

paras.t: Et homo quum in honore esset, non intellexit: id est, peccator quum ad Creatoris sui imaginem factus esset, propriam dignitatem non advertit, nec rationaliter vixit, nec cœlestem atque angelicam beatitudinem concupivit, sed in rebus temporalibus atque carnalibus se immersit, nec per rationem passionibus suis prævaluit: idcirco comparatus est jumentis insipientibus, factus sicut equus et mulus, in quibus non est intellectus, et similis factus est illis, sequendo concupiscentiæ impetum et vitiorum impulsum, non rectæ rationis imperium, neque divinæ legis censuram. De tali homine in Genesi ait Dominus: Non permanebit spiritus meus in homine in æternum, quia caro est. Non enim adimplet quod Dominus ait: Sub te erit appetitus ejus, id est concupiscentia mala, et tu dominaberis illius. O quam multi sunt hodierna die prælati et doctores, ac alii multi, qui proprium honorem non intelligunt, sed inhonestissime coram Deo et turpiter atque carnaliter vivunt, et Deo ingrati rebellesque sunt!
paras.en: [[48:13|And man when he was in honour did not understand|Et homo quum in honore esset, non intellexit]]: that is, the sinner, though he had been made to the image of his Creator, did not heed his own dignity, nor live according to reason, nor desire the heavenly and angelic beatitude, but sank himself in temporal and carnal things, nor did he by reason prevail over his passions: therefore [[48:13|he is compared to senseless beasts|comparatus est jumentis insipientibus]], made [[Ps 31:9|like the horse and the mule, who have no understanding|sicut equus et mulus, in quibus non est intellectus]], [[48:13|and is become like to them|et similis factus est illis]], by following the onset of concupiscence and the drive of the vices, not the command of right reason, nor the judgment of the divine law. Of such a man the Lord says in Genesis: [[Gen 6:3|My spirit shall not remain in man for ever, because he is flesh|Non permanebit spiritus meus in homine in æternum, quia caro est]]. For he does not fulfil what the Lord says: [[Gen 4:7|the lust thereof shall be under thee|Sub te erit appetitus ejus]], that is, evil concupiscence, [[Gen 4:7|and thou shalt have dominion over it|et tu dominaberis illius]]. O how many there are today, prelates and doctors, and many others besides, who do not understand their own honour, but live most dishonourably before God, shamefully and carnally, and are ungrateful and rebellious toward God!

paras.t: Hæc via illorum, id est, prædicta opinio et mala conversatio, est via seu operatio impiorum, scandalum ipsis, id est, ad casum et mortem æternam eos perducens. Est enim eis talis via, ruinæ ac damnationis occasio. Unde Salomon dicit: Via impiorum tenebrosa; nesciunt ubi corruunt. Et postea in ore suo complacebunt: id est, peccatores postquam divitias congregaverint, et temporalia fuerint bona sortiti, sibi invicem complacebunt, se mutuo beatificantes, collaudantes, et blandientes; sicut superius dictum est, Quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ; et infra, Beatum dixerunt populum cui hæc sunt. Hi enim gloriantur, quum malefecerint, et exsultant in rebus pessimis. Verumtamen ipsi miserrimi sunt, et se mutuo fallunt, sicut Dominus per Isaiam contestatur: Popule meus, qui te beatum dicunt, ipsi te decipiunt, et viam gressuum tuorum dissipant.
paras.en: [[48:14|This way of theirs|Hæc via illorum]], that is, the opinion and evil conduct just described, is the way, or working, of the wicked, [[48:14|is a stumblingblock to them|scandalum ipsis]], that is, it leads them to a fall and to eternal death. For such a way is to them an occasion of ruin and damnation. Whence Solomon says: [[Prov 4:19|The way of the wicked is darksome: they know not where they fall|Via impiorum tenebrosa; nesciunt ubi corruunt]]. [[48:14|and afterwards they shall delight in their mouth|Et postea in ore suo complacebunt]]: that is, sinners, after they have gathered riches and obtained temporal goods, will be pleased with one another, calling one another blessed, praising and flattering one another; as was said above, [[Ps 9:24|For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul|Quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ]] [the margin gives Ps. x, 3, according to the Hebrew: Ps 9:24 in the Vulgate numbering]; and below, [[Ps 143:15|They have called the people happy, that hath these things|Beatum dixerunt populum cui hæc sunt]] [the margin gives Ps. cxlvii, 15; the verse is Ps 143:15]. For these glory [[Prov 2:14|when they have done evil, and rejoice in the most wicked things|quum malefecerint, et exsultant in rebus pessimis]]. Yet they are most wretched, and deceive one another, as the Lord testifies by Isaias: [[Is 3:12|O my people, they that call thee blessed, the same deceive thee, and destroy the way of thy steps|Popule meus, qui te beatum dicunt, ipsi te decipiunt, et viam gressuum tuorum dissipant]].

paras.t: Sicut oves in inferno positi sunt: id est, quemadmodum oves repente et improvise ad mortem ducuntur, et occiduntur, ita maligni subito et inopinate condemnabuntur. Quum enim (ut Paulus ait) dixerint, Pax et securitas, tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus. Propter quod Christus hortatur: Vigilate; nescitis enim quando Dominus veniet, sero an media nocte, an galli cantu, an mane: ne, quum venerit repente, inveniat vos dormientes. Et, Vigilate, inquit, omni tempore orantes, ut digni habeamini fugere omnia quæ ventura sunt, et stare ante Filium hominis. Mors depascet eos: id est, ipsa pœna inferni, quæ morte amarior est, erit cibus impiorum ac damnatorum: ita quod sicut esuriens cibo impletur, sic ipsi pœnis perpetuis implebuntur; et sicut per cibum conservatur anima in esse, sic pœna infernalis servabit injustos in esse, semper eos torquendo, et nunquam consumendo. Unde apud Jeremiam Dominus ait: Ecce ego cibabo eos absinthio, et potabo eos felle.
paras.en: [[48:15|They are laid in hell like sheep|Sicut oves in inferno positi sunt]]: that is, as sheep are led suddenly and without warning to death, and slain, so the wicked will be condemned suddenly and unexpectedly. For when (as Paul says) [[1 Thess 5:3|they shall say: Peace and security|dixerint, Pax et securitas]], [[1 Thess 5:3|then shall sudden destruction come upon them|tunc repentinus eis superveniet interitus]]. For which reason Christ exhorts us: [[Mark 13:35|Watch ye therefore (for you know not when the lord of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cock crowing, or in the morning|Vigilate; nescitis enim quando Dominus veniet, sero an media nocte, an galli cantu, an mane]]: [[Mark 13:36|Lest coming on a sudden, he find you sleeping|ne, quum venerit repente, inveniat vos dormientes]]. And: [[Luke 21:36|Watch ye|Vigilate]], he says, [[Luke 21:36|praying at all times, that you may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that are to come and to stand before the Son of man|omni tempore orantes, ut digni habeamini fugere omnia quæ ventura sunt, et stare ante Filium hominis]]. [[48:15|death shall feed upon them|Mors depascet eos]]: that is, the very punishment of hell, which is more bitter than death, will be the food of the wicked and the damned: so that, as a hungry man is filled with food, so they will be filled with everlasting punishments; and as by food the soul is kept in being, so the punishment of hell will keep the unjust in being, ever tormenting them and never consuming them. Whence the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 23:15|Behold I will feed them with wormwood, and will give them gall to drink|Ecce ego cibabo eos absinthio, et potabo eos felle]].

paras.t: Et dominabuntur eorum justi in matutino: id est, electi in resurrectione beata prævalebunt injustis. Stabunt enim in magna constantia adversus eos; et, Judicabunt Sancti nationes, et dominabuntur populis. Tunc namque maligni in nullo resistere Sanctis, aut eorum felicitatem minuere poterunt, nec ad eos ascendere, aut eorum gloriam intueri. Justi vero, si eis placuerit, ad damnatos descendere poterunt, et eorum miseriam cernere, eisque justissime insultare. Et auxilium eorum veterascet in inferno a gloria eorum: id est, fortitudo et spes ac omne subsidium, quæ impii habent in vita præsenti in rebus caducis ac transitoriis, omnino peribunt, cessabunt, et ad instar veteris panni deficient in inferno, a præsumptione et vana exsultatione quas habuerunt in hoc mundo: quia tunc nihil proderunt eis, quemadmodum in libro Sapientiæ ipsi protestantur: Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut quid divitiarum jactantia contulit nobis? Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra. Et hoc est quod Dominus ad peccatores per Ezechielem terribiliter ait: Ecce complosi manus meas super malitias tuas. Numquid sustinebit cor tuum, aut prævalebunt manus tuæ in diebus quos ego faciam tibi? Et conflabo et succendam vos in igne furoris mei.
paras.en: [[48:15|And the just shall have dominion over them in the morning|Et dominabuntur eorum justi in matutino]]: that is, the elect, in the blessed resurrection, will prevail over the unjust. For they will [[Wis 5:1|stand with great constancy against those|Stabunt enim in magna constantia adversus eos]]; and, The Saints [[Wis 3:8|shall judge nations, and rule over people|Judicabunt Sancti nationes, et dominabuntur populis]]. For then the wicked will in no way be able to resist the Saints, or lessen their happiness, nor to go up to them, or look upon their glory. But the just, if it please them, will be able to go down to the damned, and see their misery, and most justly mock them. [[48:15|and their help shall decay in hell from their glory|Et auxilium eorum veterascet in inferno a gloria eorum]] [veterascet, "shall grow old": hence the old garment that follows]: that is, the strength and hope and every support which the wicked have in the present life, in perishable and passing things, will wholly perish, cease, and wear out like an old garment in hell, away from the presumption and vain exultation which they had in this world: for then they will profit them nothing, as they themselves declare in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:8|What hath pride profited us? or what advantage hath the boasting of riches brought us?|Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut quid divitiarum jactantia contulit nobis?]] [[Wis 5:9|All those things are passed away like a shadow|Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra]]. And this is what the Lord says so terribly to sinners by Ezechiel: [[Ezech 22:13|Behold, I have clapped my hands|Ecce complosi manus meas]] at thy wickednesses. [[Ezech 22:14|Shall thy heart endure, or shall thy hands prevail in the days which I will bring upon thee|Numquid sustinebit cor tuum, aut prævalebunt manus tuæ in diebus quos ego faciam tibi?]]? And I will melt you, and [[Ezech 22:21|will burn you in the fire of my wrath|succendam vos in igne furoris mei]].

paras.t: Verumtamen Deus redimet animam meam de manu inferi, id est de causa ac merito cadendi in pœnas inferni, id est de peccato mortali ac servitute diaboli, quum acceperit me, id est, quum gratiose ac misericorditer egerit mecum, vitia ignoscendo, et gratiam infundendo. Vel: Redimet de manu inferi, id est de omni potestate diaboli ac pœnis inferni, quum acceperit me ad immortalem ac impassibilem statum, videlicet in die judicii, quando dicturus est justis: Venite, benedicti Patris mei.
paras.en: [[48:16|But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell|Verumtamen Deus redimet animam meam de manu inferi]], that is, from the cause and desert of falling into the pains of hell, that is, from mortal sin and the servitude of the devil, [[48:16|when he shall receive me|quum acceperit me]], that is, when he deals with me graciously and mercifully, pardoning my vices and pouring in grace. Or: [[48:16|will redeem|Redimet]] [[48:16|from the hand of hell|de manu inferi]], that is, from all the power of the devil and from the pains of hell, [[48:16|when he shall receive me|quum acceperit me]] into the immortal and impassible state, namely on the day of judgment, when he will say to the just: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father|Venite, benedicti Patris mei]].

paras.t: Ne timueris, timore humano et turbulento, quum dives factus fuerit homo in temporalibus ac sensibilibus bonis, et quum multiplicata fuerit gloria domus ejus, id est fama, honor, voluptas, fortitudo, prosperitas, atque similia, quæ sæpe in hoc mundo reprobis conceduntur.
paras.en: [[48:17|Be not thou afraid|Ne timueris]], with a human and troubled fear, [[48:17|when a man shall be made rich|quum dives factus fuerit homo]] in temporal and sensible goods, [[48:17|and when the glory of his house shall be increased|et quum multiplicata fuerit gloria domus ejus]], that is, fame, honour, pleasure, strength, prosperity, and the like, which in this world are often granted to the reprobate.

paras.t: Quoniam quum interierit, non sumet omnia, id est, nihil horum secum portabit; neque descendet ad pœnas inferni, cum eo jam mortuo et judicato, gloria ejus, id est temporalis atque mundana prosperitas. Unde ait Apostolus: Nihil intulimus in hunc mundum; haud dubium quia nec auferre quid possumus. Et sanctus Job dicit: Dives quum dormierit, nihil secum auferet; aperiet oculos suos, et nihil inveniet; apprehendet eum quasi aqua inopia. Nihil ergo sequitur morientem, nisi merita aut demerita ejus. Propterea Salomon jubet: Quodcumque potest facere manus tua, instanter operare: quia nec opes, nec ratio, nec sapientia, nec scientia erunt apud inferos, quo tu properas. Et rursum: Mortuo homine impio, nulla erit ultra spes.
paras.en: [[48:18|For when he shall die he shall take nothing away|Quoniam quum interierit, non sumet omnia]], that is, he will carry none of these things with him; [[48:18|nor shall|neque]] [[48:18|his glory|gloria ejus]], that is, temporal and worldly prosperity, [[48:18|descend|descendet]] to the pains of hell [[48:18|with him|cum eo]], when he is now dead and judged. Whence the Apostle says: [[1 Tim 6:7|we brought nothing into this world: and certainly we can carry nothing out|Nihil intulimus in hunc mundum; haud dubium quia nec auferre quid possumus]]. And holy Job says: [[Job 27:19|The rich man when he shall sleep shall take away nothing with him: he shall open his eyes and find nothing.|Dives quum dormierit, nihil secum auferet; aperiet oculos suos, et nihil inveniet]] [[Job 27:20|Poverty like water shall take hold on him|apprehendet eum quasi aqua inopia]]. Nothing, then, follows the dying man but his merits or demerits. Therefore Solomon bids: [[Eccles 9:10|Whatsoever thy hand is able to do, do it earnestly|Quodcumque potest facere manus tua, instanter operare]]: for neither riches [Denis reads opes, riches, where the Vulgate has opus, work], [[Eccles 9:10|nor reason, nor wisdom, nor knowledge shall be in hell, whither thou art hastening|nec ratio, nec sapientia, nec scientia erunt apud inferos, quo tu properas]]. And again: [[Prov 11:7|When the wicked man is dead, there shall be no hope any more|Mortuo homine impio, nulla erit ultra spes]] [the margin gives Prov. vi, 7; the verse is Prov 11:7].

paras.t: Quia anima ejus in vita ipsius benedicetur: id est, ideo non debes timere quum dives factus fuerit homo, quia anima non benedicetur a Deo propter divitias, sed propter justitiam suam: quam si non habuerit, non benedicetur divinitus. Vel sic: Anima ejus in vita ipsius benedicetur, id est, peccator in præsenti vita ab adulatoribus et vanis hominibus beatificabitur atque laudabitur, sicut prædictum est, Quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ, et iniquus benedicitur. Ponit enim partem pro toto, videlicet animam pro homine. Confitebitur tibi, id est, gratias tibi, Domine, aget, teque laudabit, quum benefeceris ei, id est, quum omnia ei ad nutum succedunt, quum adversa non sustinet, quum temporaliter prosperatur.
paras.en: [[48:19|For in his lifetime his soul will be blessed|Quia anima ejus in vita ipsius benedicetur]]: that is, you ought not to fear [[48:17|when a man shall be made rich|quum dives factus fuerit homo]], for the soul will not be blessed by God because of riches, but because of its justice: and if it has not this, it will not be blessed by God. Or thus: [[48:19|in his lifetime his soul will be blessed|Anima ejus in vita ipsius benedicetur]], that is, the sinner in the present life will be called blessed and praised by flatterers and vain men, as was said before: [[Ps 9:24|For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul: and the unjust man is blessed|Quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ, et iniquus benedicitur]] [again the margin gives Ps. x, 3, according to the Hebrew: Ps 9:24 in the Vulgate]. For he puts the part for the whole, namely the soul for the man. [[48:19|he will praise thee|Confitebitur tibi]] [confitebitur: literally "will confess to thee", that is, give thanks and praise], that is, he will give thanks to thee, O Lord, and praise thee, [[48:19|when thou shalt do well to him|quum benefeceris ei]], that is, when all things go as he would have them, when he suffers no adversity, when he prospers in temporal things.

paras.t: Sed numquid peccatum est, in prosperis Domino confiteri? Nonne Apostolus ait, Gratias ago Deo super inenarrabili dono ejus? Et iterum: Benedictus Deus qui consolatur nos. Et Isaias: Miserationum, inquit, Domini recordabor; laudem Domini super omnibus quæ reddidit nobis. Cur ergo opus justi gratique hominis appropriatur nunc impio, nisi quod justus in prosperis et adversis Domino confitetur, malus autem in prosperis tantum? Et ideo confessio seu gratiarum actio hominis mali, non oritur ex caritate divina, sed ex amore privato aut naturali, videlicet quia naturaliter amat homo se ipsum. Naturale est enim benefactorem laudare atque diligere. Si autem amaret se homo in Deo ordinato amore, tunc in omni eventu gratias ageret dispensationi divinæ, gloriareturque in adversis, in quantum per talia a peccatis purgatur, ad gratiam coaptatur, Christo conformatur, atque ad æternam felicitatem perducitur. Quidquid ergo nobis acciderit, maneamus fixi in Domino. Si spiritualis consolatio subtrahitur, si gratia secundum desiderium nostrum non augmentatur, si tentationes gravantur et multiplicantur, perseveret spes nostra in Domino stabilita, et faciamus quod in nobis est, sine intermissione ad Deum gementes, clamantes et obsecrantes.
paras.en: But is it a sin to praise the Lord in prosperity? Does not the Apostle say, [[2 Cor 9:15|Thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift|Gratias ago Deo super inenarrabili dono ejus]]? And again: [[2 Cor 1:3|Blessed be the God|Benedictus Deus]] [[2 Cor 1:4|who comforteth us|qui consolatur nos]]. And Isaias: [[Is 63:7|I will remember the tender mercies of the Lord|Miserationum, inquit, Domini recordabor]], he says; [[Is 63:7|the praise of the Lord for all the things that the Lord hath bestowed upon us|laudem Domini super omnibus quæ reddidit nobis]]. Why, then, is the work of the just and grateful man here ascribed to the wicked, unless because the just man praises the Lord in prosperity and in adversity, but the wicked man in prosperity only? And so the praise, or thanksgiving, of the wicked man does not spring from divine charity, but from a private or natural love, namely because man naturally loves himself. For it is natural to praise and love a benefactor. But if a man loved himself in God with an ordered love, then in every event he would give thanks to the divine dispensation, and would glory in adversities, inasmuch as by such things he is purged of sins, fitted for grace, conformed to Christ, and brought to eternal happiness. Whatever befalls us, then, let us remain fixed in the Lord. If spiritual consolation is withdrawn, if grace is not increased as we desire, if temptations grow heavier and more numerous, let our hope persevere, established in the Lord, and let us do what is in us, groaning, crying and beseeching to God without ceasing.

paras.t: Introibit usque in progenies patrum suorum: id est, peccator dum moritur, colligetur ad reprobos in inferno: qui sunt patres ejus, quoniam opera eorum ipse secutus est. Duæ enim sunt generationes: una bonorum, alia malorum. Quemadmodum itaque frequenter in sacra Scriptura justi dicuntur collecti ad patres, seu ad populum suum, id est additi societati electorum; sic mali, dum moriuntur, generationem seu societatem damnatorum ingrediuntur. Sic quippe scriptum est: Venerunt filii Israel in montem Hor, et dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Pergat, inquit, Aaron ad populos suos. Usque in æternum non videbit lumen, id est, nunquam visurus est gloriam Beatorum: juxta illud, Tollatur impius ne videat gloriam Dei. Et sanctus Job de tali homine ait: Obliviscatur ejus misericordia, et dulcedo illius vermis. Dedit enim illi Deus locum pœnitentiæ, et ipse abutitur eo in superbiam. In inferno enim nulla redemptio est, sed fletus et stridor dentium atque palpabiles tenebræ; nec unquam assurgere poterunt condemnati ad lumen gratiæ, claritatemque gloriæ.
paras.en: [[48:20|He shall go in to the generations of his fathers|Introibit usque in progenies patrum suorum]]: that is, the sinner, when he dies, will be gathered to the reprobate in hell, who are his fathers, since he has followed their works. For there are two generations: one of the good, the other of the wicked. As, then, the just are often said in sacred Scripture to be gathered to their fathers, or to their people, that is, added to the company of the elect; so the wicked, when they die, enter the generation, or company, of the damned. For so it is written: The children of Israel came to mount Hor[[Num 20:22||]], and [[Num 20:23|the Lord spoke to Moses|dixit Dominus ad Moysen]]: [[Num 20:24|Let Aaron, saith he, go to his people|Pergat, inquit, Aaron ad populos suos]]. [[48:20|and he shall never see light|Usque in æternum non videbit lumen]], that is, he will never see the glory of the Blessed: according to that saying, Let the wicked be taken away, that he may not see the glory of God[[Is 26:10||]] [the margin gives Is. xxvi, 10, according to the Septuagint; the Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims read: he shall not see the glory of the Lord]. And holy Job says of such a man: [[Job 24:20|Let mercy forget him: may worms be his sweetness|Obliviscatur ejus misericordia, et dulcedo illius vermis]]. [[Job 24:23|God hath given him place for penance, and he abuseth it unto pride|Dedit enim illi Deus locum pœnitentiæ, et ipse abutitur eo in superbiam]]. For in hell there is no redemption, but [[Matt 22:13|weeping and gnashing of teeth|fletus et stridor dentium]][[Matt 25:30||]] [the margin gives Matt. xxii, 13; xxv, 13, etc.: the second is Matt 25:30], and darkness that can be felt; nor will the condemned ever be able to rise to the light of grace and the brightness of glory.

paras.t: Homo quum in honore esset, non intellexit, etc. Versus iste propter sententiæ suæ decorem ac utilitatem repetitur: qui jam satis elucidatus videtur.
paras.en: [[48:21|Man when he was in honour did not understand|Homo quum in honore esset, non intellexit]], etc. This verse is repeated because of the beauty and usefulness of its meaning: and it seems already to have been sufficiently explained.

paras.t: Ecce psalmus iste, quam pulchre temporalem prosperitatem et gloriam reprobat, atque futura impiorum tormenta demonstrat; quam pulchre peccatricis animæ ignobilitatem et cæcitatem ostendit, justorumque futurum dominium pandit. Conemur ergo temporalia cuncta despicere, florentem mundum cum omni sua voluptate ac vanitate respuere, quoniam mundus transit et concupiscentia ejus. Et, sicut Isaias asserit, Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos fœni; exsiccatum est fœnum, et cecidit flos. Paremusque nos indesinenter ad lætam mortis susceptionem: quam secure exspectat, atque lætanter recipere potest, qui nil carnale, sæculare, aut transitorium diligit, sed toto affectu cœlestia quærit, et Deum sanctum ac benedictum, omnis sanctæ lætitiæ fontem dulcissimum, summe desiderat, illud sapientissimi Salomonis efficaciter pensans: Nescit homo finem suum; sed sicut pisces capiuntur hamo et aves laqueo, sic capiuntur homines tempore malo, quum eis extemplo supervenerit.
paras.en: Behold how beautifully this psalm condemns temporal prosperity and glory, and shows forth the future torments of the wicked; how beautifully it displays the baseness and blindness of the sinful soul, and makes known the future dominion of the just. Let us strive, then, to despise all temporal things, and to spurn the flourishing world with all its pleasure and vanity, since [[1 John 2:17|the world passeth away and the concupiscence thereof|mundus transit et concupiscentia ejus]]. And, as Isaias declares, [[Is 40:6|All flesh is grass, and all the glory thereof as the flower of the field|Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos fœni]] [Denis has "the flower of the grass"]; [[Is 40:7|The grass is withered, and the flower is fallen|exsiccatum est fœnum, et cecidit flos]]. And let us prepare ourselves unceasingly to welcome death gladly: which he awaits securely, and can receive gladly, who loves nothing carnal, worldly or passing, but seeks heavenly things with his whole affection, and desires above all the holy and blessed God, the sweetest fountain of all holy gladness, weighing to good effect that saying of the most wise Solomon: [[Eccles 9:12|Man knoweth not his own end: but as fishes are taken with the hook, and as birds are caught with the snare, so men are taken in the evil time, when it shall suddenly come upon them|Nescit homo finem suum; sed sicut pisces capiuntur hamo et aves laqueo, sic capiuntur homines tempore malo, quum eis extemplo supervenerit]].

paras.t: PRECATIO. Pie redemptor Christe, qui pro salute mundi in ligno crucis innocens pependisti, et moriendo populum Sanctorum ad imperium revocasti cœlorum: tuæ, quæsumus, miserationis operatione, quum nos acceperis, animas nostras de manu inferi redime, atque eas partem beatæ resurrectionis fac obtinere.
paras.en: Prayer. O loving Redeemer, Christ, who for the salvation of the world didst hang innocent on the wood of the cross, and by dying didst call back the people of the Saints to the kingdom of heaven: by the working of thy mercy, we beseech thee, when thou shalt receive us, redeem our souls [[48:16|from the hand of hell|de manu inferi]], and make them obtain a share in the blessed resurrection.

49.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI QUADRAGESIMI NONI : DEUS DEORUM DOMINUS LOCUTUS EST.
49.title_en: Exposition of the forty-ninth psalm: The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken.

paras.t: Brevis autem est titulus psalmi præsentis, videlicet: Psalmus Asaph. Secundum Hieronymum vero et Hebræorum doctores, Asaph erat propheta, et auctor psalmi istius. Secundum Augustinum autem, David est auctor psalmi hujus, et adscribitur Asaph sicut cantori, quoniam erat unus de principalibus cantoribus a David in templo dispositis. Secundum Cassiodorum quoque, Asaph ponitur hic pro titulo propter nominis sui interpretationem: interpretatur enim congregatio. De congregatione autem fidelium tractat hic psalmus. Denique psalmus iste mysteriis Christi plenus est, de novæ legis institutione ac veteris Testamenti cessatione, et duplici Christi adventu, multisque aliis loquens.
paras.en: The title of the present psalm is short, namely: [[49:1|A psalm for Asaph|Psalmus Asaph]]. According to Jerome and the doctors of the Hebrews, Asaph was a prophet, and the author of this psalm. But according to Augustine, David is the author of this psalm, and it is ascribed to Asaph as to its singer, since he was one of the chief singers appointed by David in the temple[[1 Par 25:1||]][[1 Par 25:2||]]. According to Cassiodorus too, Asaph is put here in the title because of the meaning of his name: for it is interpreted *congregation*. And this psalm treats of the congregation of the faithful. Lastly, this psalm is full of the mysteries of Christ, speaking of the institution of the new law and the ceasing of the old Testament, of the twofold coming of Christ, and of many other things.

paras.t: Ait ergo Propheta: Deus deorum Dominus, id est Christus Unigenitus Dei, Deus verus angelorum, hominumque sanctorum Dominus, locutus est nobis in carne assumpta per se ipsum, sicut ait Apostolus: Novissime diebus istis locutus est nobis in Filio. Quemadmodum Filius Dei per Isaiam promisit: Propter hoc sciet populus meus nomen meum in die illa, quia ego ipse qui loquebar, ecce adsum. Dicuntur autem angeli sancti et homines virtuosi, dii, quoniam excellentius divinæ naturæ perfectionem participant, et de talibus diis Moyses ait: Diis non detrahes. Et Salvator, Illos (inquit) dixit deos, ad quos sermo Dei factus est. Et vocavit terram, id est, Christus per se ipsum atque discipulos, homines vocavit ad fidem et cultum suum. Et hoc, A solis ortu usque ad occasum, id est ex omnibus partibus mundi: sicut prædictum est, quia in omnem terram exivit sonus eorum. Et Christus alibi ait: Convertimini ad me, et salvi eritis, omnes fines terræ. Et: Euntes docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris, et Filii, et Spiritus Sancti. Quod alibi clarius dicitur: Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ.
paras.en: The Prophet says, then: [[49:1|The God of gods, the Lord|Deus deorum Dominus]], that is, Christ the Only-begotten of God, true God of the angels and Lord of holy men, [[49:1|hath spoken|locutus est]] to us by himself in the flesh he had taken, as the Apostle says: Last of all, [[Heb 1:2|In these days, hath spoken to us by his Son|Novissime diebus istis locutus est nobis in Filio]][[Heb 1:1||]]. Even as the Son of God promised through Isaias: [[Is 52:6|Therefore my people shall know my name in that day: for I myself that spoke, behold I am here|Propter hoc sciet populus meus nomen meum in die illa, quia ego ipse qui loquebar, ecce adsum]]. Now holy angels and virtuous men are called gods, because they share more excellently in the perfection of the divine nature; and of such gods Moses says: [[Ex 22:28|Thou shalt not speak ill of the gods|Diis non detrahes]]. And the Saviour: [[John 10:35|he called them gods|Illos]], he says, [[John 10:35|to whom the word of God was spoken|dixit deos, ad quos sermo Dei factus est]]. [[49:1|and he hath called the earth|Et vocavit terram]], that is, Christ, by himself and by his disciples, called men to faith and to his worship. And this [[49:1|From the rising of the sun, to the going down thereof|A solis ortu usque ad occasum]], that is, from all parts of the world: as was foretold, that [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|in omnem terram exivit sonus eorum]]. And Christ says elsewhere: [[Is 45:22|Be converted to me, and you shall be saved, all ye ends of the earth|Convertimini ad me, et salvi eritis, omnes fines terræ]]. And: [[Matt 28:19|Going therefore, teach ye all nations: baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost|Euntes docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris, et Filii, et Spiritus Sancti]]. Which is said more clearly elsewhere: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]].

paras.t: Ex Sion species decoris ejus: id est, ex monte Sion et civitate sancta Jerusalem prædicata ac publicata est primo pulchritudo seu claritas evangelicæ legis, seu humanæ naturæ Christi, divinitatisque ejus. Jam enim in præcedentium psalmorum explanatione ostensum est, quomodo evangelica lex instituta est a Christo in die Cœnæ et Pentecostes, seu aliis certis temporibus, in monte Sion; et quomodo in Jerusalem primo prædicata est resurrectio atque Evangelium Christi, quemadmodum ab Isaia prædictum est, De Sion exibit lex, et verbum Domini de Jerusalem. De hac autem datione ac institutione novæ legis, Jeremias apertissime prophetavit: Ecce, inquiens, dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et feriam domui Israel et domui Juda pactum novum; et scribam leges meas in corde eorum.
paras.en: [[49:2|Out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty|Ex Sion species decoris ejus]]: that is, from mount Sion and the holy city Jerusalem was first preached and published the beauty or brightness of the Gospel law, or of the human nature of Christ and of his divinity. For it has already been shown, in explaining the preceding psalms, how the Gospel law was instituted by Christ on mount Sion, on the day of the Supper and of Pentecost, or at other set times; and how the resurrection and the Gospel of Christ were first preached in Jerusalem, as was foretold by Isaias: [[Is 2:3|the law shall come forth from Sion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem|De Sion exibit lex, et verbum Domini de Jerusalem]]. And of this giving and institution of the new law Jeremias prophesied most plainly: [[Jer 31:31|Behold|Ecce]], he says, [[Jer 31:31|the days shall come, saith the Lord, and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Juda|dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et feriam domui Israel et domui Juda pactum novum]]; and [[Jer 31:33|I will write it in their heart|et scribam leges meas in corde eorum]] [Denis reads *scribam leges meas*, "I will write my laws"].

paras.t: Deus manifeste veniet. Hic tractat Propheta de secundo Christi adventu, qui erit in majestate et gloria, sicut primus erat in humilitate et pœna. Quia enim primo Christus venit ut judicaretur ac pateretur, oportuit primum suum adventum quodammodo esse occultum: quoniam si cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent. Quia vero secundo Christus venturus est ut judicet mundum, idcirco secundus ejus adventus erit omnibus manifestus. Propter quod Christus Judæis dixit: Amodo videbitis Filium hominis sedentem a dextris virtutis Dei, et venientem in nubibus cœli cum potestate magna et majestate. Et: Sicut fulgur coruscans de cœlo, in ea quæ sub cœlo sunt fulget; ita erit adventus Filii hominis. Deus noster, videlicet Jesus Christus, qui est verus Deus, æternus, immensus et supersubstantialis; et non silebit in secundo adventu sicut in primo. In secundo enim adventu cuncta discutiet, sententiam proferet, et pœnas infliget. Sic autem in primo adventu non habuit se, secundum quod ipse in Evangelio asserit: Non misit Deus Filium suum in mundum ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum. Et hoc est quod ipse per Isaiam testatur: Tacui, semper silui, patiens fui; sicut parturiens loquar; dissipabo et absorbebo simul. Et per Amos: Ecce ego stridebo subter vos, sicut stridet plaustrum onustum fœno; et peribit fuga a veloce, et fortis non salvabit animam suam.
paras.en: [[49:3|God shall come manifestly|Deus manifeste veniet]]. Here the Prophet treats of the second coming of Christ, which will be in majesty and glory, as the first was in humility and suffering. For since Christ came the first time to be judged and to suffer, his first coming had to be in a manner hidden: since [[1 Cor 2:8|if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory|si cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent]]. But since Christ will come the second time to judge the world, his second coming will therefore be manifest to all. For this reason Christ said to the Jews: [[Matt 26:64|hereafter you shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of the power of God and coming in the clouds of heaven|Amodo videbitis Filium hominis sedentem a dextris virtutis Dei, et venientem in nubibus cœli]] [[Luke 21:27|with great power and majesty|cum potestate magna et majestate]][[Matt 24:30||]] [the margin gives Matt. xxiv, 30 and Luke xxi, 27; the first words are those of Matt 26:64]. And: [[Luke 17:24|as the lightning that lighteneth from under heaven shineth unto the parts that are under heaven, so shall the Son of man be|Sicut fulgur coruscans de cœlo, in ea quæ sub cœlo sunt fulget; ita erit adventus Filii hominis]] [Denis's last words, *adventus Filii hominis*, "the coming of the Son of man", are those of Matt 24:27]. [[49:3|our God|Deus noster]], namely Jesus Christ, who is true God, eternal, immeasurable and supersubstantial; [[49:3|and shall not keep silence|et non silebit]] in the second coming as in the first. For in the second coming he will examine all things, pronounce sentence, and inflict punishment. But in the first coming he did not behave so, as he himself declares in the Gospel: [[John 3:17|God sent not his Son into the world, to judge the world: but that the world may be saved by him|Non misit Deus Filium suum in mundum ut judicet mundum, sed ut salvetur mundus per ipsum]]. And this is what he testifies through Isaias: [[Is 42:14|I have always held my peace, I have kept silence, I have been patient, I will speak now as a woman in labour: I will destroy, and swallow up at once|Tacui, semper silui, patiens fui; sicut parturiens loquar; dissipabo et absorbebo simul]]. And through Amos: [[Amos 2:13|Behold, I will screak under you as a wain screaketh that is laden with hay|Ecce ego stridebo subter vos, sicut stridet plaustrum onustum fœno]]; [[Amos 2:14|And flight shall perish from the swift|et peribit fuga a veloce]], and [[Amos 2:14|neither shall the strong save his life|et fortis non salvabit animam suam]].

paras.t: Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet. Sicut mundus primo per diluvium periit, sic ultimo peribit per ignem conflagrationis: qui terram et mare exuret, aeremque purgabit, ac peccatores durante judicio inflammabit, et eos prolata sententia simul involvet, atque cum eis in infernum descendet, quantum ad id quod caliditatis fumositatisque habebit; quod vero claritatis ac lucis in ipso exstiterit, ad superiora ascendet. Secundum Basilium, tam alte quoque ascendet ignis conflagrationis ut aqua diluvii, scilicet quindecim cubitis super omnes montes, ut creditur. De isto itaque igne nunc ait: Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet. Præcedet enim Christi descensum, et durabit usque ad finem judicii. Et in circuitu ejus, scilicet Christi judicis, erit tempestas valida, id est strepitus ingens, gemitus vehemens, ululatus atque ploratus. Videntes enim impii Judicem venientem ac discutientem, turbabuntur timore horribili, dicentes: Montes, operite nos; et, colles, cadite super nos, et abscondite nos a facie sedentis super thronum, et ab ira Agni. De hujus diei tempestate horrenda apud Joelem scriptum est: Conturbentur omnes habitatores terræ, quia veniet dies Domini, dies tenebrarum et caliginis. Similis ei non fuit a principio, et post eum non erit. Ante faciem ejus ignis vorans, et post eum exurens flamma. Omnes vultus redigentur in ollam. A facie ejus contremuit terra, moti sunt cœli, sol et luna obtenebrati sunt, et stellæ retraxerunt splendorem suum.
paras.en: [[49:3|A fire shall burn before him|Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet]]. As the world perished first by the flood, so at the last it will perish by the fire of the conflagration: which will burn up earth and sea, purge the air, and set sinners ablaze while the judgment lasts; and when sentence has been pronounced it will wrap them all together and go down with them into hell, as to whatever heat and smoke it holds; but whatever brightness and light is in it will rise to the higher regions. According to Basil, the fire of the conflagration will also rise as high as the water of the flood, namely fifteen cubits above all the mountains[[Gen 7:20||]], as is believed. Of this fire, then, he now says: [[49:3|A fire shall burn before him|Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet]]. For it will go before Christ's descent, and will last until the end of the judgment. [[49:3|round about him|Et in circuitu ejus]], that is, of Christ the judge, there will be [[49:3|a mighty tempest|tempestas valida]], that is, a huge din, vehement groaning, howling and wailing. For the wicked, seeing the Judge coming and examining, will be troubled with a horrible fear, saying: [[Osee 10:8|to the mountains Cover us; and to the hills: Fall upon us|Montes, operite nos; et, colles, cadite super nos]], and [[Apoc 6:16|hide us from the face of him that sitteth upon the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb|abscondite nos a facie sedentis super thronum, et ab ira Agni]][[Luke 23:30||]]. Of the dreadful tempest of this day it is written in Joel: [[Joel 2:1|let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: because the day of the Lord cometh|Conturbentur omnes habitatores terræ, quia veniet dies Domini]], [[Joel 2:2|A day of darkness, and of gloominess|dies tenebrarum et caliginis]]. [[Joel 2:2|the like to it hath not been from the beginning, nor shall be after it|Similis ei non fuit a principio, et post eum non erit]]. [[Joel 2:3|Before the face thereof a devouring fire, and behind it a burning flame|Ante faciem ejus ignis vorans, et post eum exurens flamma]]. [[Joel 2:6|all faces shall be made like a kettle|Omnes vultus redigentur in ollam]]. [[Joel 2:10|At their presence the earth hath trembled, the heavens are moved: the sun and moon are darkened, and the stars have withdrawn their shining.|A facie ejus contremuit terra, moti sunt cœli, sol et luna obtenebrati sunt, et stellæ retraxerunt splendorem suum]]

paras.t: Advocabit cœlum desursum: id est, Christus ad judicium veniens, convocabit et secum adducet omnes cœlestis patriæ cives, scilicet angelos sanctos, omnesque Beatos, qui etiam visibiliter tunc omnibus apparebunt, secundum Gregorium. Unde in Zacharia legitur: Veniet Dominus Deus meus, omnesque Sancti ejus cum eo. Et erit in die illa: non erit lux, sed frigus et gelu, id est tempestas (ut dictum est) valida. Nam et Christus in nocte venturus est. Hinc per Isaiam dicitur: Dominus ad judicium veniet cum senibus populi sui et principibus ejus. Unde et Judas ait: Prophetavit autem de his septimus ab Adam Enoch, dicens: Ecce veniet Dominus in sanctis millibus suis facere judicium, et arguere omnes impios de omnibus operibus impietatis eorum, et de omnibus duris quæ locuti sunt contra Dominum. Et terram: id est, Christus ad judicium vocabit habitatores terræ, videlicet omnes homines, eos potissimum qui per ignem conflagrationis consumpti erunt, et omnes quorum corpora suscitabit. Propter quod in Evangelio testatus est: Veniet hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem ejus. Discernere populum suum: id est, Christus ideo cœlum et terram advocabit, quatenus ipse eis præsentibus populum suum discernat, id est, electos a reprobis dividat, et agnos ab hœdis loco ac præmio separet, congregans triticum in horreum suum, paleas vero comburens igne inexstinguibili. Unde Dominus ait: Congregabo omnes gentes, et deducam eas in vallem Josaphat, et disceptabo ibi cum eis, quia sedebo ut judicem omnes gentes in circuitu.
paras.en: [[49:4|He shall call heaven from above|Advocabit cœlum desursum]]: that is, Christ, coming to judgment, will call together and bring with him all the citizens of the heavenly fatherland, namely the holy angels and all the Blessed, who will then also appear visibly to all, according to Gregory. Hence we read in Zacharias: [[Zach 14:5|the Lord my God shall come, and all the saints with him|Veniet Dominus Deus meus, omnesque Sancti ejus cum eo]]. [[Zach 14:6|And it shall come to pass in that day, that there shall be no light, but cold and frost|Et erit in die illa: non erit lux, sed frigus et gelu]], that is, a mighty tempest (as has been said). For Christ too is to come in the night. Hence it is said through Isaias: [[Is 3:14|The Lord will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and its princes|Dominus ad judicium veniet cum senibus populi sui et principibus ejus]]. Hence Jude too says: [[Jude 1:14|Now of these Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying: Behold, the Lord cometh with thousands of his saints:|Prophetavit autem de his septimus ab Adam Enoch, dicens: Ecce veniet Dominus in sanctis millibus suis]] [[Jude 1:15|To execute judgment upon all and to reprove all the ungodly for all the works of their ungodliness, whereby they have done ungodly: and for all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against God|facere judicium, et arguere omnes impios de omnibus operibus impietatis eorum, et de omnibus duris quæ locuti sunt contra Dominum]]. [[49:4|and the earth|Et terram]]: that is, Christ will call to judgment the dwellers on earth, namely all men, above all those who will have been consumed by the fire of the conflagration, and all whose bodies he will raise. For this reason he declared in the Gospel: [[John 5:28|the hour cometh wherein all that are in the graves shall hear the voice|Veniet hora, in qua omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem ejus]]. [[49:4|to judge his people|Discernere populum suum]] [*discernere*, "to sort out, to tell apart"]: that is, Christ will call heaven and earth for this reason, that in their presence he may sort out his people, that is, divide the elect from the reprobate, and separate the lambs from the kids in place and in reward[[Matt 25:32||]][[Matt 25:33||]], gathering the wheat into his barn, but burning the chaff with unquenchable fire[[Matt 3:12||]]. Hence the Lord says: [[Joel 3:2|I will gather together all nations and will bring them down into the valley of Josaphat: and I will plead with them there|Congregabo omnes gentes, et deducam eas in vallem Josaphat, et disceptabo ibi cum eis]], [[Joel 3:12|for there I will sit to judge all nations round about|quia sedebo ut judicem omnes gentes in circuitu]].

paras.t: Sed quia adductio ista fiet ministerio angelorum (ipsi enim cineres corporum resuscitandorum colligent, resuscitatosque ad judicium deferent), idcirco consequenter ad angelos dicitur: Congregate illi, id est Christo judici, Sanctos ejus, qui ei in hac vita sancte servierunt, quatenus mercedem dignam ac plenam recipiant, suoque Capiti in æternum adhærentes. Unde Christus de se ipso professus est: Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos, et colligent de regno ejus omnia scandala, et eos qui faciunt iniquitatem, et mittent eos in caminum ignis. Et iterum: In consummatione sæculi exibunt angeli, et separabunt malos de medio justorum. Itaque, Congregate illi Sanctos ejus, qui ordinant testamentum ejus super sacrificia, id est, qui in militanti Ecclesia disponunt quemadmodum exsequenda sint mandata divinæ legis circa oblationes et sacrificia. Quamvis enim Christus præceperit sibi offerri sacrificia aliqua tam in novo quam in veteri Testamento: non tamen determinavit omnem modum ac ritum quibus hoc fieri debeat; sed hoc ordinationi Sanctorum, quos Spiritu Sancto implere decrevit, reliquit, sicut circa Missæ officium multa a sanctis sunt Patribus ordinata.
paras.en: But since this bringing will be done by the ministry of the angels (for they will gather the ashes of the bodies to be raised, and carry those raised to the judgment), it is therefore next said to the angels: [[49:5|Gather ye together|Congregate]] [[49:5|to him|illi]], that is, to Christ the judge, [[49:5|his saints|Sanctos ejus]], who served him holily in this life, so that they may receive a worthy and full reward, cleaving for ever to their Head. Hence Christ declared of himself: [[Matt 13:41|The Son of man shall send his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all scandals, and them that work iniquity|Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos, et colligent de regno ejus omnia scandala, et eos qui faciunt iniquitatem]], [[Matt 13:42|And shall cast them into the furnace of fire|et mittent eos in caminum ignis]]. And again: [[Matt 13:49|at the end of the world. The angels shall go out, and shall separate the wicked from among the just|In consummatione sæculi exibunt angeli, et separabunt malos de medio justorum]]. So, then: [[49:5|Gather ye together his saints to him: who set his covenant before sacrifices|Congregate illi Sanctos ejus, qui ordinant testamentum ejus super sacrificia]] [literally "who order his covenant over the sacrifices", which is how Denis takes it], that is, those who in the Church militant set in order how the commandments of the divine law concerning oblations and sacrifices are to be carried out. For although Christ commanded that certain sacrifices be offered to him, in the new Testament as in the old, yet he did not determine every manner and rite in which this should be done; but he left this to the ordering of the Saints, whom he decreed to fill with the Holy Ghost, as many things concerning the office of the Mass have been ordered by the holy Fathers.

paras.t: Et annuntiabunt cœli justitiam ejus: id est, angeli sancti, hominesque perfecti, qui in die judicii cum Christo judicabunt tanquam assessores ipsius, approbabunt atque laudabunt sententiam Judicis et remunerationem quam unicuique faciet. Et hoc agent, quoniam Deus judex est, id est, quoniam scient quod ille qui judicat, nec falli, nec fallere potest, nec personas accipere, nec aliquid dissimulare, quum ipse sit Deus, in quem error et injustitia cadere nequeunt. Si vero judex iste esset pura creatura, non videretur adeo tutum, approbare judicium ejus, quoniam creatura errare potest ac falli. Vel sic: Et annuntiabunt cœli, id est Apostoli ac alii prædicatores sancti cœlestem vitam in terra ducentes, justitiam ejus, id est præcepta atque consilia Christi, per universum orbem terrarum. Ad utramque autem expositionem referri potest quod in Apocalypsi Sancti dixisse prophetice describuntur: Magna et mirabilia sunt opera tua, Domine Deus; justæ et veræ sunt viæ tuæ, Rex sæculorum. Quis non timebit te, et magnificabit nomen tuum? Et iterum: Etiam, Domine Deus omnipotens, justa ac vera judicia tua.
paras.en: [[49:6|And the heavens shall declare his justice|Et annuntiabunt cœli justitiam ejus]]: that is, the holy angels and perfect men, who on the day of judgment will judge with Christ as his assessors, will approve and praise the sentence of the Judge and the reward he will give to each. And they will do this [[49:6|for God is judge|quoniam Deus judex est]], that is, because they will know that he who judges can neither be deceived nor deceive, nor respect persons, nor overlook anything, since he is God, in whom error and injustice can have no place. But if this judge were a mere creature, it would not seem so safe to approve his judgment, since a creature can err and be deceived. Or thus: [[49:6|And the heavens shall declare|Et annuntiabunt cœli]], that is, the Apostles and other holy preachers leading a heavenly life on earth, [[49:6|his justice|justitiam ejus]], that is, the precepts and counsels of Christ, throughout the whole world. To either exposition may be referred what the Saints are described in the Apocalypse as saying in prophecy: [[Apoc 15:3|Great and wonderful are thy works, O Lord God Almighty. Just and true are thy ways, O King of ages|Magna et mirabilia sunt opera tua, Domine Deus; justæ et veræ sunt viæ tuæ, Rex sæculorum]]. [[Apoc 15:4|Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and magnify thy name?|Quis non timebit te, et magnificabit nomen tuum?]] And again: [[Apoc 16:7|Yea, O Lord God Almighty, true and just are thy judgments|Etiam, Domine Deus omnipotens, justa ac vera judicia tua]].

paras.t: Deinde agitur de institutione evangelicæ legis, atque Salvator, qui in unitate personæ est Deus ac homo: Audi, popule meus: id est, aure cordis et corporis auscultate, o Judæi, qui eratis populus Dei peculiaris: quemadmodum Moyses scribit, Te elegit Dominus Deus tuus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram; et loquar doctrinam perfectam. Israel, et testificabor tibi. Populum suum jam repetit, vocans eum Israel, quia de semine Jacob, quem angelus Israel appellavit, nati sunt. Sæpe namque nomine Israel designatur totus populus Judæorum, secundum quod ad Pharaonem Dominus dicit: Filius meus primogenitus Israel. Dixi tibi, Dimitte filium meum, ut sacrificet mihi. Moraliter quoque, per Israel intelligitur etiam militans Ecclesia, seu quilibet homo Deum contemplans. Ait ergo Christus: Israel, et testificabor tibi, id est, o filii Israel, ad quos specialiter missus sum, audite, et testificabor, id est, verbis, virtutibus atque miraculis affirmabo quod sequitur: Deus, Deus tuus ego sum. Christus enim in propria persona prædicavit Judæis, seque Deum esse sæpe asseruit. Unde scriptum est: Quærebant Judæi eum interficere, quia non solum solvebat sabbatum, sed et patrem suum dicebat Deum, æqualem se Deo faciens. Quumque dixissent ei Judæi, Tu quis es? respondit: Principium, qui et loquor vobis. Et hoc idem Christus miraculis confirmavit. Propter quod ipse ait: Si non facio opera Patris mei, nolite credere mihi; si autem facio, et si mihi non creditis, operibus credite.
paras.en: Next the institution of the Gospel law is treated, and the Saviour, who in the unity of his person is God and man, [says]: [[49:7|Hear, O my people|Audi, popule meus]]: that is, listen with the ear of heart and body, O Jews, who were God's peculiar people: as Moses writes, [[Deut 7:6|The Lord thy God hath chosen thee, to be his peculiar people of all peoples that are upon the earth|Te elegit Dominus Deus tuus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram]]; [[49:7|and I will speak|et loquar]] perfect doctrine. [[49:7|O Israel, and I will testify to thee|Israel, et testificabor tibi]]. He now addresses his people again, calling them Israel, because they were born of the seed of Jacob, whom the angel named Israel[[Gen 32:28||]]. For the whole people of the Jews is often designated by the name of Israel, as the Lord says to Pharao: [[Ex 4:22|Israel is my son, my firstborn|Filius meus primogenitus Israel]]. [[Ex 4:23|I have said to thee: Let my son go, that he may serve me|Dixi tibi, Dimitte filium meum, ut sacrificet mihi]] [Denis reads *ut sacrificet mihi*, "that he may sacrifice to me"]. In the moral sense too, by Israel is understood also the Church militant, or any man who contemplates God [Israel being interpreted "a man seeing God"]. Christ says, then: [[49:7|O Israel, and I will testify to thee|Israel, et testificabor tibi]], that is, O sons of Israel, to whom I am especially sent, hear, and I will testify, that is, I will affirm by words, mighty works and miracles what follows: [[49:7|I am God, thy God|Deus, Deus tuus ego sum]]. For Christ in his own person preached to the Jews, and often declared that he was God.
