Incerta, id est futura contingentia : de quibus proprie est prophetia, et quæ prævidere Deo proprium est, juxta illud Isaiæ : Quæ ventura sunt annuntiate nobis, et sciemus quia dii estis vos ; et occulta sapientiæ tuæ, id est profunda et alta mysteria de Divinitate ac summa Trinitate, Christique incarnatione, passione, resurrectione et ascensione, manifestasti mihi, per illuminationem Spiritus Sancti, clarius, purius et copiosius quam ceteris viribus : quia non per symbolicam illuminationem seu per sensibiles formas, sed per anagogicam irradiationem, id est per intelligibilem atque internam illuminationem sine sensibilium representatione formarum, accepi a Spiritu Sancto quæcumque in hoc libro conscripsi.
paras.en: [[50:8|For behold thou hast loved truth|Ecce enim veritatem dilexisti]]. As though he said: Because thou lovest truth, I confess my own fault without excuse; and because I do what is pleasing to thee, it is fitting that thou be gracious to me. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 8:32|And you shall know the truth: and the truth shall make you free|Cognoscetis veritatem, et veritas liberabit vos]]. And God loves truth above all, for likeness is the cause of love. Since, then, God is true by nature, and in his essence is the uncreated Truth, it is plain that he loves truth by nature. [[50:8|the uncertain|Incerta]], that is, future contingent things, which are properly the matter of prophecy, and which it belongs to God to foresee, according to that saying of Isaias: [[Is 41:23|Shew the things that are to come hereafter, and we shall know that ye are gods|Quæ ventura sunt annuntiate nobis, et sciemus quia dii estis vos]]; [[50:8|and hidden things of thy wisdom|et occulta sapientiæ tuæ]], that is, the deep and high mysteries of the Godhead and of the supreme Trinity, and of Christ's incarnation, passion, resurrection and ascension, [[50:8|thou hast made manifest to me|manifestasti mihi]], by the enlightening of the Holy Ghost, more clearly, purely and abundantly than to other men [the print has *viribus*, "powers"; *viris*, "men", seems meant]: for it was not by a symbolic enlightenment, or through sensible forms, but by an anagogical irradiation, that is, by an intelligible and inward enlightenment without the representation of sensible forms, that I received from the Holy Ghost whatever I have written in this book.

paras.t: Adsperges me, Domine, hyssopo. In Levitico legitur, quemadmodum Dominus jusserit mundandum a lepra, adspergi hyssopo ut mundaretur. Dum ergo ait, Adsperges me hyssopo, designat se spiritualem incurrisse lepram, a qua petit purgari hyssopi adspersione, id est humilis pœnitentiæ contritione. Hyssopus namque est herba brevis, loco saxoso radicitus hærens, pulmonisque inflationem repellens ac sanans. Idcirco per eam pœnitentia designatur : quæ in Christo (qui petra vocatur) fundatur, cordisque superbiam sanat, et hominem in propriis oculis parvum et modicum efficit. Et mundabor a macula interiori. Lavabis me, lotione spirituali per gratiæ infusionem, et super nivem dealbabor, id est, ampliori spiritualis munditiæ ornatu atque candore splendebo, quam sit nivis albedo. Spiritualis enim puritas, corporalem puritatem omnino excedit. Et hoc est quod per Ezechielem Dominus ait : Effundam super vos aquam mundam, et mundabimini ab omnibus inquinamentis vestris. De hac adspersione, mundatione et lotione Salvator etiam ait : Tu autem quum jejunas, unge caput tuum, et faciem tuam lava, ne videaris hominibus jejunans. Et alibi : Collyrio, inquit, inunge oculos tuos, ut videas. — Vel sic : Adsperges me hyssopo, id est fide et fructu seu merito sanguinis Christi : cujus utique fide ac fideli adspersione salvati sunt omnes veteres Sancti ; et mundabor : quia per meritum sanguinis Christi ab omni culpa purgamur. Lavabis me in fonte Baptismatis : quod ad catechumenos præsertim refertur ; et super nivem dealbabor : quoniam in Baptismo universa peccata donantur, juxta illud, Salvos nos facit Baptisma, non carnis depositio sordium, sed conscientiæ bonæ interrogatio in Deum.
paras.en: [[50:9|Thou shalt sprinkle me|Adsperges me]], O Lord, [[50:9|with hyssop|hyssopo]]. We read in Leviticus how the Lord commanded that one to be cleansed of leprosy should be sprinkled with hyssop, that he might be made clean[[Lev 14:2||]][[Lev 14:4||]][[Lev 14:6||]][[Lev 14:7||]]. When, then, he says, [[50:9|Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop|Adsperges me hyssopo]], he shows that he has incurred a spiritual leprosy, from which he asks to be purged by the sprinkling of hyssop, that is, by the contrition of humble penance. For hyssop is a low herb, clinging by its roots to stony places, which drives out and heals swelling of the lungs. Therefore penance is signified by it: which is founded on Christ (who is called the rock[[1 Cor 10:4||]]), heals the pride of the heart, and makes a man small and of little account in his own eyes. [[50:9|and I shall be cleansed|Et mundabor]] from the inward stain. [[50:9|thou shalt wash me|Lavabis me]], with a spiritual washing by the pouring in of grace, [[50:9|and I shall be made whiter than snow|et super nivem dealbabor]], that is, I shall shine with a fuller adornment and brightness of spiritual cleanness than is the whiteness of snow. For spiritual purity altogether surpasses bodily purity. And this is what the Lord says through Ezechiel: [[Ezech 36:25|I will pour upon you clean water, and you shall be cleansed from all your filthiness|Effundam super vos aquam mundam, et mundabimini ab omnibus inquinamentis vestris]]. Of this sprinkling, cleansing and washing the Saviour too says: [[Matt 6:17|But thou, when thou fastest anoint thy head, and wash thy face;|Tu autem quum jejunas, unge caput tuum, et faciem tuam lava]] [[Matt 6:18|That thou appear not to men to fast|ne videaris hominibus jejunans]]. And elsewhere: [[Apoc 3:18|with eyesalve|Collyrio]], he says, [[Apoc 3:18|anoint thy eyes|inunge oculos tuos]], [[Apoc 3:18|that thou mayest see|ut videas]]. — Or thus: [[50:9|Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop|Adsperges me hyssopo]], that is, with faith in the blood of Christ, and with its fruit or merit: by faith in which, and by its faithful sprinkling, all the saints of old were saved; [[50:9|and I shall be cleansed|et mundabor]]: for by the merit of the blood of Christ we are purged from all guilt. [[50:9|thou shalt wash me|Lavabis me]] in the font of Baptism: which refers especially to catechumens; [[50:9|and I shall be made whiter than snow|et super nivem dealbabor]]: since in Baptism all sins are forgiven, according to that saying: [[1 Pet 3:21|baptism, being of the like form, now saveth you also|Salvos nos facit Baptisma]]: [[1 Pet 3:21|not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but, the examination of a good conscience towards God|non carnis depositio sordium, sed conscientiæ bonæ interrogatio in Deum]].

paras.t: Auditui meo, exteriori et interiori, dabis gaudium de indulgentia peccatorum, et lætitiam de restitutione gratiarum. Ad litteram Deus dedit sancto David hoc gaudium, hancque lætitiam, dum ei per Nathan prophetam atque per inspirationem internam, veniam repromisit, gratiamque rependit. Nos quoque gaudium et lætitiam a Deo recipimus, dum nos per sacram Scripturam consolatur, dicendo illud : Si impius egerit pœnitentiam, omnium iniquitatum ejus non recordabor amplius. Et iterum : Revertimini et vivite, quia nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur et vivat. Nec his dissonat quod Salvator affirmat : Non est, inquiens, voluntas ante Patrem vestrum, ut pereat unus ex pusillis istis. Propter quod alibi habetur : Deus mortem non fecit, nec delectatur in perditione vivorum. Denique magnam nobis ingerit lætitiam, dum se tam paratum, imo paratissimum offert ad gratiam infundendam, secundum quod ipse protestatur : Omnis qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit; et pulsanti aperietur. Et iterum : Pater vester cœlestis dabit spiritum bonum petentibus se. Per instinctum quoque occultum Spiritus Sancti dat nobis Deus gaudium et lætitiam : quia (ut ait Apostolus) ipse Spiritus reddit testimonium spiritui nostro, quod sumus filii Dei. Et iterum : Dedit pignus Spiritus in cordibus nostris.
paras.en: [[50:10|To my hearing|Auditui meo]], outward and inward, [[50:10|thou shalt give joy|dabis gaudium]] at the pardon of sins, [[50:10|and gladness|et lætitiam]] at the restoring of graces. In the letter, God gave holy David this joy and this gladness when, through Nathan the prophet[[2 Kings 12:13||]] and through inward inspiration, he promised him pardon and gave him back grace. We too receive joy and gladness from God when he comforts us through holy Scripture, saying: [[Ezech 18:21|if the wicked do penance|Si impius egerit pœnitentiam]], [[Ezech 18:22|I will not remember all his iniquities|omnium iniquitatum ejus non recordabor amplius]]. And again: [[Ezech 18:32|return ye and live|Revertimini et vivite]], for [[Ezech 18:32|I desire not the death|nolo mortem]] of the sinner, but [[Ezech 18:23|that he should be converted from his ways, and live|ut convertatur et vivat]] [the margin gives Ezech. xviii, 32, 23; Denis's wording is closest to Ezech 33:11]. Nor is it out of tune with this when the Saviour declares: [[Matt 18:14|it is not|Non est]], he says, [[Matt 18:14|the will of your Father, who is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish|voluntas ante Patrem vestrum, ut pereat unus ex pusillis istis]]. For which reason we read elsewhere: [[Wis 1:13|God made not death, neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living|Deus mortem non fecit, nec delectatur in perditione vivorum]]. Lastly, he brings us great gladness by offering himself so ready, nay most ready, to pour in grace, as he himself declares: [[Matt 7:8|For every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh, it shall be opened|Omnis qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit; et pulsanti aperietur]][[Luke 11:10||]]. And again: your heavenly Father will [[Luke 11:13|give the good Spirit to them that ask him|dabit spiritum bonum petentibus se]]. Through the hidden prompting of the Holy Ghost, too, God gives us joy and gladness: for (as the Apostle says) [[Rom 8:16|the Spirit himself giveth testimony to our spirit that we are the sons of God|ipse Spiritus reddit testimonium spiritui nostro, quod sumus filii Dei]]. And again: he hath [[2 Cor 1:22|given the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts|Dedit pignus Spiritus in cordibus nostris]].

paras.t: Et exsultabunt ossa humiliata. Nomine partis designatum est totum, ut sit sensus : De infusione gaudii et lætitiæ exsultabo ego peccator et pœnitens, qui usque ad ossium humiliationem, seu corporis inclinationem, genuflexionem seu prostrationem humiliavi me ipsum. Vel : Exsultabunt ossa humiliata, id est, interior lætitia ex sua plenitudine in corpus redundabit, et ossa corporis certis indiciis interiorem jucunditatem ostendent. Sicut enim spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa, sic spiritus hilaris impinguat atque lætificat ossa. Vel : Exsultabunt, id est, hilariter et fortiter agent, ossa humiliata, id est virtutes animæ, quæ ante pœnitentiam oppressæ, sopitæ, otiosæque erant, sed post pœnitentiam hilariter et ferventer operari cœperunt, quoniam ubi abundavit iniquitas, abundat et gratia.
paras.en: [[50:10|and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice|Et exsultabunt ossa humiliata]]. The whole is signified by the name of a part, so that the sense is: At the pouring in of joy and gladness I shall rejoice, I, a sinner and a penitent, who have humbled myself even to the humbling of my bones, that is, by bowing the body, by kneeling or by lying prostrate. Or: [[50:10|the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice|Exsultabunt ossa humiliata]], that is, the inward gladness will overflow from its fullness into the body, and the bones of the body will shew the inward delight by sure signs. For as [[Prov 17:22|a sorrowful spirit drieth up the bones|spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa]], so a cheerful spirit fattens and gladdens the bones. Or: [[50:10|shall rejoice|Exsultabunt]], that is, shall act cheerfully and bravely, [[50:10|the bones that have been humbled|ossa humiliata]], that is, the powers of the soul, which before penance were oppressed, lulled to sleep and idle, but after penance began to work cheerfully and fervently, since where iniquity abounded, grace also abounds.

paras.t: Averte, o Domine, faciem tuam, id est considerationem tuam, a peccatis meis, et obliviscere ea, id est, per modum obliviscentis te habe in non ulciscendo et ignoscendo. Et hoc utique Deus piissimus libenter faciet, si tu ipse peccata tua adspicias, ponderes, defleas, corrigas, atque devites : alioqui faciet tibi quod de perseverantibus in peccato per Amos prophetam ait : Juravit Dominus : Si oblitus fuero usque ad finem omnia opera eorum. Unde negligenti et propria mala non deploranti, ait Apostolus : An divitias bonitatis Dei et patientiæ et longanimitatis contemnis ? Ignoras quoniam patientia Dei ad pœnitentiam te adducit ? Secundum duritiam autem tuam et impœnitens cor tuum, thesaurizas tibi iram in die iræ et revelationis justi judicii Dei. Itaque, o Domine, Averte faciem tuam, id est justitiæ tuæ animadversionem, a peccatis meis, ut nec gratiam in præsenti, nec gloriam in futuro mihi propter eorum demerita abstrahas ; et omnes iniquitates meas dele, dimittendo pœnam et culpam, recipiendoque me ad amicitiam tuam, ac si nunquam peccassem.
paras.en: [[50:11|Turn away|Averte]], O Lord, [[50:11|thy face|faciem tuam]], that is, thy regard, [[50:11|from my sins|a peccatis meis]], and forget them: that is, behave as one who forgets, by not avenging and by forgiving. And this God, most loving, will surely do gladly, if thou thyself look upon thy sins, weigh them, weep for them, amend them and shun them: otherwise he will do to thee what he says through Amos the prophet of those who persevere in sin: [[Amos 8:7|The Lord hath sworn|Juravit Dominus]]: [[Amos 8:7|surely I will never forget all their works|Si oblitus fuero usque ad finem omnia opera eorum]] [the Latin is a Hebrew form of oath, literally "If I shall forget …", that is, I shall never forget]. Hence to the careless man who does not bewail his own evils the Apostle says: [[Rom 2:4|Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and patience and longsuffering? Knowest thou not that the benignity of God leadeth thee to penance?|An divitias bonitatis Dei et patientiæ et longanimitatis contemnis ? Ignoras quoniam patientia Dei ad pœnitentiam te adducit]] [Denis reads *patientia Dei*, "the patience of God", where the Vulgate has *benignitas Dei*, "the benignity of God"] [[Rom 2:5|But according to thy hardness and impenitent heart, thou treasurest up to thyself wrath, against the day of wrath and revelation of the just judgment of God|Secundum duritiam autem tuam et impœnitens cor tuum, thesaurizas tibi iram in die iræ et revelationis justi judicii Dei]]. Therefore, O Lord, [[50:11|Turn away thy face|Averte faciem tuam]], that is, the chastisement of thy justice, [[50:11|from my sins|a peccatis meis]], so that thou withdraw from me neither grace in the present nor glory in the future on account of their demerits; [[50:11|and blot out all my iniquities|et omnes iniquitates meas dele]], by remitting the punishment and the guilt, and receiving me into thy friendship as though I had never sinned.

paras.t: Cor mundum crea in me, Deus : id est, esse spirituale et meritorium age et inchoa in me per gratiæ creationem. Beati enim mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt. Cordis enim munditia, omnium exercitiorum nostrorum finis ultimus esse debet, secundum quod Salomon admonet : Omni custodia custodi cor tuum. Et si veram cordis puritatem adipisci desideras, hunc versum mente et ore sic iteres, tractes, cogites, ores et depromas, quomodo naribus tuis anhelitum attrahis. Magna namque est et ineffabilis virtus versus hujus atque sequentium. Et spiritum rectum innova, id est, Spiritum Sanctum de novo infunde, in visceribus meis, id est in intimis animæ meæ, dando gratiam, sapientiam, caritatem, ceterasque virtutes ac dona Spiritus Sancti.
paras.en: [[50:12|Create a clean heart in me, O God|Cor mundum crea in me, Deus]]: that is, bring about and begin in me a spiritual and meritorious being, by the creation of grace. For [[Matt 5:8|Blessed are the clean of heart: they shall see God|Beati enim mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt]]. For cleanness of heart ought to be the last end of all our exercises, as Solomon admonishes: [[Prov 4:23|With all watchfulness keep thy heart|Omni custodia custodi cor tuum]]. And if thou desirest to gain true purity of heart, repeat this verse in mind and mouth, handle it, ponder it, pray it and bring it forth, as often as thou drawest breath through thy nostrils. For great and unspeakable is the power of this verse and of those that follow. [[50:12|and renew a right spirit|Et spiritum rectum innova]], that is, pour in the Holy Ghost anew, [[50:12|within my bowels|in visceribus meis]], that is, in the inmost parts of my soul, by giving grace, wisdom, charity, and the other virtues and gifts of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Ne projicias me propter peccata mea, a facie tua, id est a pietatis tuæ adspectu et conservatione ; et spiritum sanctum tuum, id est inhabitationem gratiosam et piam præsentiam Spiritus Sancti, ne auferas a me, sed in bono conserva me.
paras.en: [[50:13|Cast me not away|Ne projicias me]] for my sins [[50:13|from thy face|a facie tua]], that is, from the gaze and keeping of thy loving-kindness; and [[50:13|thy holy spirit|spiritum sanctum tuum]], that is, the gracious indwelling and loving presence of the Holy Ghost, [[50:13|take not|ne auferas]] [[50:13|from me|a me]], but keep me in good.

paras.t: Redde mihi lætitiam salutaris tui, id est contemplationem jucundam de Christo, in quo omnium salus consistit. Hanc enim videtur David per culpam ad tempus perdidisse, et spiritum propheticum amisisse. Unde nec proprii peccati enormitatem advertit. Nos quoque eam peccando amittimus : quoniam in malevolam animam non introibit sapientia. Idcirco pro ejus restitutione, augmento et conservatione indesinenter orare debemus. Et spiritu principali, id est Spiritu Sancto, confirma me, stabiliendo cor meum in gratia ejus : quia ut ait Apostolus, Optimum est gratia stabiliri cor. Nemo enim coronatur, nisi legitime certet ; nec salvabitur, nisi qui usque in finem perseveraverit : quod nulli possibile est, nisi quem Deus Spiritu Sancto confirmat.
paras.en: [[50:14|Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation|Redde mihi lætitiam salutaris tui]], that is, the joyful contemplation of Christ, in whom the salvation of all consists [*salutare*, "salvation", can also mean "Saviour"]. For David seems to have lost this for a time through his sin, and to have lost the prophetic spirit; and so he did not even notice the enormity of his own sin. We too lose it by sinning, for [[Wis 1:4|wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul|in malevolam animam non introibit sapientia]]. Therefore we ought to pray without ceasing for its restoring, increase and keeping. And [[50:14|with a perfect spirit|spiritu principali]] [*principalis*, "princely, ruling"], that is, with the Holy Ghost, [[50:14|strengthen me|confirma me]], establishing my heart in his grace: for, as the Apostle says, [[Heb 13:9|it is best that the heart be established with grace|Optimum est gratia stabiliri cor]]. For no one is crowned unless he strive lawfully; nor will any be saved but he who perseveres to the end: which is possible for none, unless God strengthens him with the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Ecce in versibus istis beatissimus David supergloriosissimæ Trinitatis fidem atque mysterium evidenter demonstrat. Nam nomine Dei, designat Patrem ; nomine spiritus recti, principalis et sancti, exprimit Spiritum Sanctum ; nomine autem salutaris, explicat Filium, de quo Petrus ait, Non est in alio aliquo salus. Similiter Isaias propheta Trinitatem divinarum personarum clare fatetur, dum per eum Dominus ait : Ego primus et ego novissimus. Et post pauca iste primus et novissimus subdit : Et nunc Dominus Deus misit me, et spiritus ejus. Ibi per primum et novissimum intelligitur Christus, qui in Apocalypsi ait, Ego sum Alpha et Omega, principium et finis ; et rursus, Ego sum primus et novissimus et vivus, et fui mortuus, et ecce sum vivens in sæcula sæculorum, et habeo claves mortis et inferni. Dum ergo Christus se missum a Domino et Spiritu ejus testatur, Trinitatis mysterium clarissime demonstratur.
paras.en: See how in these verses most blessed David plainly shews forth the faith and mystery of the most glorious Trinity. For by the name of God he signifies the Father; by the name of the right, the principal and the holy spirit he expresses the Holy Ghost; and by the name of salvation he sets forth the Son, of whom Peter says, [[Acts 4:12|Neither is there salvation in any other|Non est in alio aliquo salus]]. In like manner Isaias the prophet clearly confesses the Trinity of the divine Persons, when the Lord says through him: [[Is 48:12|I am the first, and I am the last|Ego primus et ego novissimus]]. And a little after, this First and Last adds: [[Is 48:16|and now the Lord God hath sent me, and his spirit|Et nunc Dominus Deus misit me, et spiritus ejus]]. There by the First and the Last is understood Christ, who says in the Apocalypse, [[Apoc 22:13|I am Alpha and Omega|Ego sum Alpha et Omega]], [[Apoc 22:13|the beginning and the end|principium et finis]]; and again, [[Apoc 1:17|I am the First and the Last|Ego sum primus et novissimus]], [[Apoc 1:18|And alive, and was dead. And behold I am living for ever and ever and have the keys of death and of hell|et vivus, et fui mortuus, et ecce sum vivens in sæcula sæculorum, et habeo claves mortis et inferni]] [the margin gives Apoc. i, 17 and "Is. xxxii, 13", which does not fit: no doubt Apoc. xxii, 13 misread; the first words stand in Apoc 22:13 (and 1:8), the second in Apoc 1:17–18]. Since, then, Christ testifies that he was sent by the Lord and his Spirit, the mystery of the Trinity is most clearly shewn.

paras.t: Docebo iniquos vias tuas : id est, gratiam mihi a te concessam, aliis communicabo, eosque ad pœnitentiam salutarem inducere meo exemplo studebo, atque præcepta divina observare eos exhortabor. Hoc ad sanctum David tanquam ad populi principem pertinebat : imo ad quoslibet aliquo modo pertinere videtur, secundum illud, Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes, sicut boni dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei. Propter quod Paulus ait : Fratres, et si homo præoccupatus fuerit in aliquo delicto, vos qui spirituales estis, hujusmodi instruite in spiritu lenitatis, considerans te ipsum, ne et tu tenteris. Unde Dionysius dicit, quod omnium divinarum perfectionum altissima est, Dei cooperatorem exsistere in reductione animarum ad primum principium. Et impii ad te convertentur, ex mea doctrina : quod valde meritorium est, quemadmodum scriptum est : Qui converti fecerit peccatorem ab errore viæ suæ, salvabit animam ejus a morte, et operit multitudinem peccatorum. Et Daniel dicit : Qui docti fuerint, fulgebunt quasi splendor firmamenti ; et qui ad justitiam erudiunt plurimos, quasi stellæ in perpetuas æternitates.
paras.en: [[50:15|I will teach the unjust thy ways|Docebo iniquos vias tuas]]: that is, I will share with others the grace granted me by thee, and I will strive by my example to lead them to saving penance, and I will exhort them to keep the divine commandments. This belonged to holy David as the prince of the people; nay, it seems in some way to belong to everyone, according to that saying: [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another: as good stewards of the manifold grace of God|Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes, sicut boni dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei]]. For which reason Paul says: [[Gal 6:1|Brethren, and if a man be overtaken in any fault, you, who are spiritual, instruct such a one in the spirit of meekness, considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted|Fratres, et si homo præoccupatus fuerit in aliquo delicto, vos qui spirituales estis, hujusmodi instruite in spiritu lenitatis, considerans te ipsum, ne et tu tenteris]]. Hence Dionysius says that of all divine perfections the highest is to be God's fellow worker in leading souls back to their first principle. [[50:15|and the wicked shall be converted to thee|Et impii ad te convertentur]], by my teaching: which is very meritorious, as it is written: [[Jas 5:20|he who causeth a sinner to be converted from the error of his way shall save his soul from death and shall cover a multitude of sins|Qui converti fecerit peccatorem ab errore viæ suæ, salvabit animam ejus a morte, et operit multitudinem peccatorum]]. And Daniel says: [[Dan 12:3|they that are learned, shall shine as the brightness of the firmament: and they that instruct many to justice, as stars for all eternity|Qui docti fuerint, fulgebunt quasi splendor firmamenti ; et qui ad justitiam erudiunt plurimos, quasi stellæ in perpetuas æternitates]].

paras.t: Sed quis dignus est ita illuminari divinitus, ut sit ipse ad aliorum informationem idoneus ? Respondeat nobis illustrissimus Isaias qui ait : Quem docebit Dominus scientiam, et quem intelligere faciet auditum ? Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere, id est eos qui carnales delicias atque sensuales voluptates devitant, et solidum cibum capere possunt ; qui in carne viventes, non secundum carnem ambulant, nec mundi vanitates admittunt. Hinc enim videmus multos ad alios instruendos multum paratos ; sed parum aut nihil proficiunt, quoniam non ex Spiritu Sancto, sed proprio sensu loquuntur, habentque verba frigida, arida, non acuta, penetrativa et calida. Quibus singulis ait Apostolus : Confidis te ipsum esse ducem cæcorum, lumen eorum qui in tenebris sunt, eruditorem insipientium, magistrum infantium, etc. Qui ergo alium doces, te ipsum non doces ? Qui gloriaris in lege, per prævaricationem legis Deum inhonoras ?
paras.en: But who is worthy to be so enlightened from on high as to be fit himself for the instruction of others? Let the most illustrious Isaias answer us, who says: [[Is 28:9|Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand the hearing? them that are weaned from the milk, that are drawn away from the breasts|Quem docebit Dominus scientiam, et quem intelligere faciet auditum ? Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere]], that is, those who shun carnal delights and sensual pleasures, and can take solid food[[Heb 5:14||]]; who, living in the flesh, do not walk according to the flesh[[2 Cor 10:3||]], nor admit the vanities of the world. For hence we see many very ready to instruct others; but they profit little or nothing, because they speak not from the Holy Ghost but from their own mind, and have words that are cold and dry, not sharp, piercing and warm. To each of these the Apostle says: [[Rom 2:19|Art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them that are in darkness,|Confidis te ipsum esse ducem cæcorum, lumen eorum qui in tenebris sunt]] [[Rom 2:20|An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants|eruditorem insipientium, magistrum infantium]], etc. [[Rom 2:21|Thou therefore, that teachest another, teachest not thyself|Qui ergo alium doces, te ipsum non doces]]? [[Rom 2:23|Thou, that makest thy boast of the law, by transgression of the law dishonourest God|Qui gloriaris in lege, per prævaricationem legis Deum inhonoras]]?

paras.t: Libera me de sanguinibus, id est peccatis præteritis, præsentibus et futuris, Deus omnium, Deus salutis meæ, in cujus potestate salus mea consistit, a quo tota perfectio mea procedit, et omne bonum animæ meæ dependet ; et exsultabit, id est, cum exsultatione cantabit et dicet, lingua mea justitiam tuam, id est justa judicia tua, quibus obstinatos condemnas, pœnitentibus misereris, orantes exaudis, toto corde conversis abundantiam gratiæ tribuis, et peccatorem propria peccata confitentem justificas.
paras.en: [[50:16|Deliver me from blood|Libera me de sanguinibus]] [literally "from bloods", that is, from blood-guiltiness], that is, from sins past, present and to come, [[50:16|O God|Deus]] of all, [[50:16|thou God of my salvation|Deus salutis meæ]], in whose power my salvation lies, from whom all my perfection proceeds, and on whom every good of my soul depends; and [[50:16|shall extol|exsultabit]] [literally "shall exult"], that is, shall sing and tell with exultation, [[50:16|my tongue|lingua mea]] [[50:16|thy justice|justitiam tuam]], that is, thy just judgments, by which thou condemnest the obstinate, hast mercy on penitents, hearest those who pray, bestowest abundance of grace on those converted with their whole heart, and justifiest the sinner who confesses his own sins.

paras.t: Domine, labia mea aperies, id est, ex interiori devotione et gratia facies labia mea in actum bonæ locutionis prorumpere, sic quod ex monitione Spiritus Sancti ad loquendum procedam, non quasi ex me ipso inductus. Qui enim a se ipso loquitur, gloriam propriam quærit. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam : quia tunc vere dignus ero laudator, si labia mea a te aperiantur, quemadmodum alibi dicis : Aperi os tuum, et ego implebo illud.
paras.en: [[50:17|O Lord, thou wilt open my lips|Domine, labia mea aperies]], that is, from inward devotion and grace thou wilt make my lips break forth into the act of good speech, so that I go forward to speak at the prompting of the Holy Ghost, not as moved of myself. For [[John 7:18|He that speaketh of himself seeketh his own glory|Qui enim a se ipso loquitur, gloriam propriam quærit]]. [[50:17|and my mouth shall declare thy praise|Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam]]: for then shall I truly be a worthy praiser, if my lips are opened by thee, as thou sayest elsewhere: [[Ps 80:11|open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it|Aperi os tuum, et ego implebo illud]] [Denis has *Aperi*, "open", where the Vulgate has *Dilata*, "open wide"; a footnote in the print gives the place and the reading *Dilata*].

paras.t: Deinde David causam allegat, cur decuit Deum sibi ignoscere. Quoniam si voluisses sacrificium legale, dedissem utique sacrificium pro satisfactione mei excessus ; sed holocaustis legalibus et figurativis non delectaberis. Sacrificia enim veteris legis nec continebant gratiam, neque per se accepta erant, sed ex devotione offerentis dumtaxat. Idcirco per ea nullus Deum placare potuit, nisi qui ante oblationem vel saltem in ea gratiam habuit. Unde ait scriptura Geneseos : Respexit Dominus ad Abel et ad munera ejus. Primo enim respexit ad offerentem, deinde ad hostiam. Indiguit itaque David ante sacrificiorum oblationem vel in ea gratiam adipisci. Quilibet quoque fidelis de se ipso hæc verba dicere potest : quia si Deo placerent, etiam in novo Testamento sacrificia legalia permanerent, et pro satisfactione a Christianis immolarentur.
paras.en: Next David alleges the reason why it was fitting for God to forgive him. [[50:18|For if thou hadst desired sacrifice|Quoniam si voluisses sacrificium]] of the law, [[50:18|I would indeed have given it|dedissem utique]], a sacrifice in satisfaction for my offence; but [[50:18|with burnt offerings|holocaustis]] of the law, which are figures, [[50:18|thou wilt not be delighted|non delectaberis]]. For the sacrifices of the old law neither contained grace nor were acceptable of themselves, but only by reason of the devotion of the one who offered them. Therefore no one could appease God by them except one who had grace before the offering, or at least in it. Hence the Scripture of Genesis says: [[Gen 4:4|the Lord had respect to Abel, and to his offerings|Respexit Dominus ad Abel et ad munera ejus]]. For first he had respect to the one who offered, then to the victim. So David needed to obtain grace before the offering of sacrifices, or in it. And any of the faithful can say these words of himself: for if they were pleasing to God, the sacrifices of the law would remain even in the New Testament, and would be offered by Christians in satisfaction.

paras.t: Sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus : id est, anima pro peccatis gemens ac tristis, est sacrificium Deo acceptum : quia se ipsam Deo offert, propriam voluntatem ei subjiciens ad agenda et patienda quæ sunt Deo placita. Unde Ecclesiasticus inducit : Salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate. Et Baruch : Anima quæ tristis est super magnitudine mali, et incedit curva et infirma, et oculi deficientes, et anima esuriens dat gloriam et justitiam tibi Domino. Cor contritum et humiliatum, Deus, non despicies, sicut per Isaiam testatus es : Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu, et trementem sermones meos? Et Job ait : Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria, et salvabitur innocens. Et Ecclesiasticus : Oratio humiliantis se cœlos penetrabit.
paras.en: [[50:19|A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit|Sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus]]: that is, a soul groaning and sorrowful for its sins is a sacrifice acceptable to God, because it offers itself to God, subjecting its own will to him, to do and to suffer the things that are pleasing to God. Hence Ecclesiasticus brings in: [[Ecclus 35:2|It is a wholesome sacrifice to take heed to the commandments, and to depart from all iniquity.|Salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate]] And Baruch: [[Bar 2:18|the soul that is sorrowful for the greatness of evil she hath done, and goeth bowed down, and feeble, and the eyes that fail, and the hungry soul giveth glory and justice to thee the Lord|Anima quæ tristis est super magnitudine mali, et incedit curva et infirma, et oculi deficientes, et anima esuriens dat gloriam et justitiam tibi Domino]]. [[50:19|a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise|Cor contritum et humiliatum, Deus, non despicies]], as thou hast testified by Isaias: [[Is 66:2|to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit, and that trembleth at my words?|Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu, et trementem sermones meos?]] And Job says: [[Job 22:29|he that hath been humbled, shall be in glory|Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria]], and [[Job 22:30|The innocent shall be saved|salvabitur innocens]]. And Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 35:21|The prayer of him that humbleth himself, shall pierce the clouds|Oratio humiliantis se cœlos penetrabit]] [Denis reads *cœlos*, "the heavens", where the Vulgate has *nubes*, "the clouds"].

paras.t: Benigne fac, Domine, in bona voluntate tua Sion, et ædificentur muri Jerusalem. Versus iste cum sequenti, primo exponendus est litteraliter ; et est sensus : O Domine, in tua bona voluntate qua promisisti mihi quod filius meus Salomon ædificaret tibi templum, fac benigne Sion, id est, pie adimple in monte Sion quod promisisti, ut scilicet in eo ædificetur templum nomini tuo ; et ædificentur muri Jerusalem, id est parietes templi vel muri civitatis, quos David vidit in spiritu sæpius destruendos. Tunc, id est templo ædificato, acceptabis sacrificium justitiæ, quod tibi juste offertur, oblationes, quæ non totaliter incendebantur, et holocausta, quæ omnino comburebantur ; tunc imponent ministri templi super altare tuum, in templo, vitulos, quia secundum legem vitulus erat animal aptum ad offerendum.
paras.en: [[50:20|Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will with Sion|Benigne fac, Domine, in bona voluntate tua Sion]]; [[50:20|that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up|et ædificentur muri Jerusalem]] [the text printed here has *et ædificentur*, "and let the walls be built"; the margin gives the other reading *ut*, "that", as in the Vulgate]. This verse, together with the next, is to be explained first according to the letter, and the sense is: O Lord, in thy good will, by which thou didst promise me that my son Solomon would build thee a temple[[2 Kings 7:12||]][[2 Kings 7:13||]], deal favourably with Sion, that is, graciously fulfil on Mount Sion what thou hast promised, namely that a temple be built on it to thy name; and let the walls of Jerusalem be built up, that is, the walls of the temple or the walls of the city, which David saw in the spirit were to be destroyed many times. [[50:21|Then|Tunc]], that is, when the temple is built, [[50:21|shalt thou accept the sacrifice of justice|acceptabis sacrificium justitiæ]], which is justly offered to thee, [[50:21|oblations|oblationes]], which were not wholly burnt, [[50:21|and whole burnt offerings|et holocausta]], which were burnt entirely; [[50:21|then shall they lay|tunc imponent]] (the ministers of the temple) [[50:21|upon thy altar|super altare tuum]], in the temple, [[50:21|calves|vitulos]], because according to the law the calf was an animal fit for offering.

paras.t: Moraliter vero sic exponuntur : Benigne fac, Domine, in bona voluntate tua, qua hominibus semper gratiam repromittis, dummodo convertantur ad te, Sion, id est Ecclesiæ militantis, te per fidem speculantes, conservando eam in fide et gratia Christi, et ædificentur muri Jerusalem, id est prælati Ecclesiæ, qui sunt aliorum defensores ac muri seu firmamentum. Illi ergo spiritualiter ædificentur, id est, in profectu virtutum et gratia confirmentur : quemadmodum dicit Apostolus, Quæ ædificationis sunt, invicem custodiamus ; et, Unusquisque proximo suo placeat in bonum, ad ædificationem. Vel : Ædificentur muri Jerusalem, id est, duo populi Judæi et Græci in unam Ecclesiæ fidem concurrant, et unus in Christo populus fiant, sicut Apostolus dicit : Non est distinctio Judæi et Græci. Tunc acceptabis in Ecclesia catholica sacrificium justitiæ, id est sacrificium laudis et Eucharistiæ, oblationes orationum et eleemosynarum, exteriorumque rerum, et holocausta, id est, propriarum voluntatum meram atque spontaneam abnegationem, eorum videlicet qui se totos divino cultui offerunt, cuncta contemnunt, nec aliquid sibi proprium retinent. Tunc imponent super altare tuum : quod est humanitas Christi, per quam omnia nostra officia fiunt accepta ; vitulos, id est se ipsos, sequendo vestigia ejus, et ejus exemplo se ipsos quotidie mortificantes, sicut testatur Apostolus : In omni fiducia magnificabitur Christus in corpore meo, sive per vitam, sive per mortem. Mihi enim vivere Christus est, et mori lucrum. Vel : Imponent super altare tuum vitulos, id est, in fide Ecclesiæ offerent tibi laudes divinas : sicut apud Osee scriptum est, Reddemus vitulos labiorum nostrorum.
paras.en: In the moral sense these verses are explained thus: [[50:20|Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will|Benigne fac, Domine, in bona voluntate tua]], by which thou ever promisest grace to men, provided they turn to thee, [[50:20|with Sion|Sion]], that is, with the Church militant, which beholds thee by faith, by keeping her in the faith and grace of Christ; [[50:20|that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up|et ædificentur muri Jerusalem]], that is, the prelates of the Church, who are the defenders of the others, and their walls or bulwark. Let them, then, be built up spiritually, that is, be strengthened in progress in the virtues and in grace: as the Apostle says, [[Rom 14:19|keep the things that are of edification, one towards another|Quæ ædificationis sunt, invicem custodiamus]]; and, [[Rom 15:2|every one of you Please his neighbour unto good, to edification|Unusquisque proximo suo placeat in bonum, ad ædificationem]]. Or: Let the walls of Jerusalem be built up, that is, let the two peoples, Jews and Greeks, come together into the one faith of the Church and become one people in Christ, as the Apostle says: [[Rom 10:12|there is no distinction of the Jew and the Greek|Non est distinctio Judæi et Græci]]. [[50:21|Then shalt thou accept|Tunc acceptabis]], in the Catholic Church, [[50:21|the sacrifice of justice|sacrificium justitiæ]], that is, the sacrifice of praise and of the Eucharist [the Latin *Eucharistia* also means "thanksgiving"], [[50:21|oblations|oblationes]] of prayers and of alms and of outward things, [[50:21|and whole burnt offerings|et holocausta]], that is, the pure and willing renunciation of their own wills, namely by those who offer themselves wholly to the worship of God, despise all things, and keep nothing as their own. [[50:21|then shall they lay|Tunc imponent]] [[50:21|upon thy altar|super altare tuum]], which is the humanity of Christ, through which all our services become acceptable, [[50:21|calves|vitulos]], that is, themselves, following in his footsteps and after his example mortifying themselves daily, as the Apostle testifies: [[Phil 1:20|with all confidence|In omni fiducia]] [[Phil 1:20|shall Christ be magnified in my body, whether it be by life or by death|magnificabitur Christus in corpore meo, sive per vitam, sive per mortem]]. [[Phil 1:21|For to me, to live is Christ: and to die is gain.|Mihi enim vivere Christus est, et mori lucrum.]] Or: They shall lay calves upon thy altar, that is, in the faith of the Church they shall offer thee divine praises: as it is written in Osee, [[Osee 14:3|we will render the calves of our lips|Reddemus vitulos labiorum nostrorum]].

paras.t: Porro anagogice exponuntur hæc sic : Benigne fac, Domine, in bona voluntate tua Sion, id est triumphanti Ecclesiæ te per speciem contemplanti, et ædificentur muri Jerusalem, id est, ruina angelorum malorum reparetur per salvationem hominum electorum. Tunc, quando videlicet venerit quod perfectum est, maxime post diem generalis judicii, quando omnino reædificati erunt muri cœlestis Jerusalem, quæ est mater nostra, de qua nobis quotidie gloriosa dicuntur (utinam et digne desiderentur) : tunc, inquam, o Domine, acceptabis sacrificium justitiæ, id est laudes perpetuas, purissimas, atque perfectas, oblationes, quibus omnes Beati in patria se totos offerunt tibi, stantes semper inavertibiliter conversi et fixi in te ; et holocausta, id est actus caritatis perfectos. Sancti enim in patria præceptum de amando Deum perfecte adimplent, quod in via fieri nequit : et hi actus caritatis, holocausta dicuntur, quia per eos intellectuales creaturæ in divinum amorem totaliter resolvuntur. Tunc imponent super altare tuum, id est in cœlo empyreo, vitulos labiorum, sicut expositum est ; vel, Vitulos, id est se ipsos, quoniam igne divini amoris incenduntur, liquefiunt, et in Deum penitus transformantur.
paras.en: Further, in the anagogical sense these words are explained thus: [[50:20|Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will with Sion|Benigne fac, Domine, in bona voluntate tua Sion]], that is, with the Church triumphant, which contemplates thee by sight; [[50:20|that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up|et ædificentur muri Jerusalem]], that is, let the fall of the wicked angels be repaired by the salvation of elect men. [[50:21|Then|Tunc]], namely when [[1 Cor 13:10|that which is perfect is come|venerit quod perfectum est]], above all after the day of the general judgment, when the walls of the heavenly Jerusalem will have been wholly rebuilt[[Amos 9:11||]] [the margin gives Amos iv, 11, which does not fit; Amos 9:11, on rebuilding the breaches of the walls, does], [[Gal 4:26|which is our mother|quæ est mater nostra]], of which glorious things are told us daily[[Ps 86:3||]] (would that they were also worthily longed for): then, I say, O Lord, [[50:21|shalt thou accept the sacrifice of justice|acceptabis sacrificium justitiæ]], that is, everlasting praises, most pure and perfect; [[50:21|oblations|oblationes]], by which all the Blessed in the fatherland offer themselves wholly to thee, standing ever unturnably turned towards thee and fixed in thee; [[50:21|and whole burnt offerings|et holocausta]], that is, perfect acts of charity. For the Saints in the fatherland fulfil perfectly the commandment to love God, which cannot be done on the way [that is, in this life, as wayfarers]; and these acts of charity are called whole burnt offerings because through them intellectual creatures are wholly dissolved into the love of God. [[50:21|then shall they lay|Tunc imponent]] [[50:21|upon thy altar|super altare tuum]], that is, in the empyrean heaven, [[50:21|calves|vitulos]] of the lips, as was explained above; or, calves, that is, themselves, since they are set on fire by the fire of divine love, melt, and are wholly transformed into God.

paras.t: Ecce excellentissimum psalmum audivimus, qui non solum verborum suorum sensu nos instruit, sed etiam auctoris sui exemplo nos plurimum erudit. Quis enim de se ipso præsumere potest, quum videat auctorem psalmi hujus, sanctum David, post tantam divinorum adeptionem charismatum, tam graviter cecidisse, non solum in adulterium, sed et in homicidium ? Qui quum in juvenili ætate tam perfectus et humilis exstitisset, ut nec inimicum suum letalem lædere vellet, aut lædi permitteret, sed bonum pro malo reddens, eum a morte eriperet qui totis viribus se interficere laborabat, qui leonem et ursum devicit, qui gigantem dejecit, qui tantas tamque sacratissimas revelationes suscepit, jam senectute potitus, in tam immania se peccata prostravit. Denique, quis desperare possit, dum audit virum adulterum et homicidam ad tantam perfectionem reductum? Studeamus ergo, carissimi, cum sancto David veraciter pœnitere, atque in omnibus non simulatam humilitatem amplecti : quia (ut ait Leo Papa) tota christianæ sapientiæ disciplina non in abundantia verbi, non in astutia disputandi, neque in appetitu laudis et gloriæ, sed in vera et voluntaria humilitate consistit : quam Dominus Jesus ab utero Matris usque ad supplicium crucis, pro omni fortitudine et elegit, et docuit. Et iterum : Tota, inquit, victoria Salvatoris, qua et diabolum superavit et mundum, humilitate est concepta, humilitate confecta. Unde Christus testatur : Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum. Quicumque ergo humiliaverit se sicut parvulus iste, hic major est in regno cœlorum. Ad quod nos post hujus incolatum exsilii statim perducat Creator omnipotens, trinus et simplex, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: Behold, we have heard a most excellent psalm, which not only instructs us by the sense of its words but also teaches us very much by the example of its author. For who can presume upon himself, when he sees the author of this psalm, holy David, after receiving such great divine gifts, fall so grievously, not only into adultery but also into murder? He who in his youth had been so perfect and humble that he would neither harm his deadly enemy himself nor let him be harmed[[1 Kings 24:7||]][[1 Kings 26:9||]] [the margin gives 1 Kings xxiv, 5–8, and xxvi, 7–12], but, returning good for evil, rescued from death the man who was striving with all his strength to kill him; who overcame the lion and the bear[[1 Kings 17:34||]][[1 Kings 17:36||]], who struck down the giant[[1 Kings 17:49||]], who received such great and most sacred revelations: he, now come to old age, threw himself down into such monstrous sins. And again, who could despair, when he hears that a man who was an adulterer and a murderer was brought back to such great perfection? Let us therefore strive, dearly beloved, to repent truly with holy David, and in all things to embrace a humility that is not feigned: for (as Pope Leo says) the whole discipline of Christian wisdom consists not in abundance of words, not in cleverness in disputing, nor in the desire of praise and glory, but in true and willing humility, which the Lord Jesus, from his Mother's womb to the punishment of the cross, chose and taught in place of all strength. And again: The whole victory of the Saviour, he says, by which he overcame both the devil and the world, was conceived in humility and accomplished in humility. Hence Christ testifies: [[Matt 18:3|unless you be converted, and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum]]. [[Matt 18:4|Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, he is the greater in the kingdom of heaven.|Quicumque ergo humiliaverit se sicut parvulus iste, hic major est in regno cœlorum]] To this may the almighty Creator, three and simple, who is God sublime above all things and blessed, bring us straightway after the sojourn of this exile. Amen.

paras.t: Precatio. Miserator Deus, faciem tuam a peccatis nostris averte, et omnes in conspectu tuo iniquitates nostras dele ; lava nos ab injustitia nostra, ut dono gratiæ tuæ emundati, in sancta ac tibi placita conversatione semper maneamus.
paras.en: Prayer. O merciful God, [[50:11|turn away thy face|faciem tuam a peccatis nostris averte]] from our sins, and [[50:11|blot out|dele]] all our iniquities in thy sight; [[50:4|wash|lava]] us from our injustice, that, cleansed by the gift of thy grace, we may ever abide in a holy way of life pleasing to thee.

51.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI PRIMI : QUID GLORIARIS IN MALITIA ? ETC.
51.title_en: Literal exposition of the fifty-first psalm: Why dost thou glory in malice? etc.

paras.t: Psalmus jam declarandus, hoc titulo prænotatur : In finem, intellectus David, quum venit Doeg Idumæus, et annuntiavit Sauli, et dixit : Venit David in domum Achimelech. Juxta intellectum litteralem, sensus tituli hujus clarus est ex historia libri Regum. Legitur enim ibidem, quemadmodum Saul dolens de evasione David, dixit ad servos suos : Audite me, filii Jemini, quia non est in vobis qui doleat vicem meam, et annuntiet mihi de David filio Isai. Respondens autem Doeg Idumæus, qui erat primus inter servos Saulis, et potentissimus pastorum ejus : Vidi, inquit, filium Isai in Nobe apud Achimelech sacerdotem, qui cibaria et gladium Goliath dedit ei. Ob hanc causam præcepit Saul occidi ipsum Achimelech (seu Abimelech, quia utrumque dicitur) et omnem domum patris ejus. Cujus facinoris Doeg exsecutor fuit, sicut ibidem legitur : Conversus Doeg irruit in sacerdotes, et trucidavit in illa die octoginta quinque viros vestitos ephod lineo. Nobe quoque civitatem sacerdotum percussit in ore gladii, tam homines quam jumenta. Abiathar vero, filius Achimelech, evasit, et venit ad David, eique retulit cuncta quæ facta sunt.
paras.en: The psalm now to be explained is headed with this title: [[51:1|Unto the end, understanding for David|In finem, intellectus David]], [[51:2|When Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul: David went to the house of Achimelech|quum venit Doeg Idumæus, et annuntiavit Sauli, et dixit : Venit David in domum Achimelech]]. In the literal understanding, the sense of this title is clear from the history in the book of Kings. For we read there how Saul, grieving over David's escape, [[1 Kings 22:7|said to his servants|dixit ad servos suos]]: [[1 Kings 22:7|Hear me now, ye sons of Jemini|Audite me, filii Jemini]]: [[1 Kings 22:8|There is not one of you that pitieth my case, nor that giveth me any information|non est in vobis qui doleat vicem meam, et annuntiet mihi]] about David the son of Isai. Then Doeg the Edomite, who [[1 Kings 22:9|was the chief among the servants of Saul|erat primus inter servos Saulis]] and the chiefest of his herdsmen, answered: [[1 Kings 22:9|I saw|Vidi]], he said, [[1 Kings 22:9|the son of Isai, in Nobe, with Achimelech|filium Isai in Nobe apud Achimelech]] the priest, who [[1 Kings 22:10|gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath|cibaria et gladium Goliath dedit ei]]. For this cause Saul commanded that Achimelech himself (or Abimelech, for he is called by both names) should be put to death, and all his father's house[[1 Kings 22:16||]][[1 Kings 22:17||]]. Doeg carried out this crime, as we read in the same place: [[1 Kings 22:18|And Doeg, the Edomite, turned, and fell upon the priests, and slew in that day eighty-five men that wore the linen ephod|Conversus Doeg irruit in sacerdotes, et trucidavit in illa die octoginta quinque viros vestitos ephod lineo]]. [[1 Kings 22:19|And Nobe, the city of the priests, he smote with the edge of the sword|Nobe quoque civitatem sacerdotum percussit in ore gladii]], men and beasts alike. But Abiathar, the son of Achimelech, escaped and came to David[[1 Kings 22:20||]], and told him all that had been done[[1 Kings 22:21||]].

paras.t: De hoc igitur edidit David hunc psalmum, qui ad litteram exponi potest de ipsa re gesta, quamvis fructuosius convenientiusque exponatur de re significata seu figurata. Dum enim psalmi de Christo vel Ecclesia litteraliter intelliguntur, litteralis sensus dulcis et devotione plenus est, et diligenter scrutandus. Dum vero de David, seu simili aliquo intelliguntur, litteralis sensus parum devotionis atque dulcedinis confert. Unde devoti parum afficiuntur in expositione hujusmodi. Ideo de tali expositione pauca dicam.
paras.en: On this matter, then, David composed this psalm, which can be expounded according to the letter of the event itself, although it is expounded more fruitfully and more fittingly of the thing signified or prefigured. For when the psalms are understood literally of Christ or of the Church, the literal sense is sweet and full of devotion, and must be searched out diligently. But when they are understood of David, or of someone like him, the literal sense brings little devotion and sweetness. Hence the devout are little moved by an exposition of this kind. Therefore I shall say little about such an exposition.

paras.t: Secundum hanc itaque expositionem sensus tituli est : Intellectus David, id est, in psalmo isto ponitur eruditio sancti David, dirigens nos in finem, id est in veram felicitatem et Christum, ad quam perveniemus, si eruditioni hujus psalmi paruerimus : intellectus, inquam, a David conscriptus, quum venit, id est, postquam venit, Doeg Idumæus. Cetera enim jam patuerunt.
paras.en: According to this exposition, then, the sense of the title is: [[51:1|understanding for David|Intellectus David]], that is, in this psalm is set down the teaching of holy David, directing us [[51:1|Unto the end|in finem]], that is, to true happiness and to Christ, which we shall reach if we obey the teaching of this psalm: an understanding, I say, written by David [[51:2|When Doeg the Edomite came|quum venit]], that is, after Doeg the Edomite had come. The rest has already been made plain.

paras.t: Increpatorie ergo alloquens David ipsum Doeg, ait : Quid gloriaris in malitia? id est, quo fructu et utilitate lætaris de opere malo, et perpetratione peccati, quo me virum innocentem et Achimelech sacerdotem prodidisti, eumque cum suis consanguineis occidisti ? Gloriabatur enim Doeg de his, quia per hæc maximam sibi amicitiam acquisivit regis iniqui. Sed hæc gloriatio, mala animæque nociva fuit : ideo David Doeg redarguit, Quid, inquiens, gloriaris in malitia, quod tibi non expedit ? Qui potens es in iniquitate, id est, qui potens fuisti ad occidendum viros innoxios, et potestate tibi collata abusus es, opprimendo te meliores.
paras.en: Rebuking Doeg himself, then, David says to him: [[51:3|Why dost thou glory in malice|Quid gloriaris in malitia?]]? that is, what fruit and profit hast thou in rejoicing over the evil deed and the committing of sin, by which thou didst betray me, an innocent man, and Achimelech the priest[[1 Kings 22:9||]], and didst kill him with his kinsmen[[1 Kings 22:18||]] [the margin cites 1 Reg. xxii, but its verse numbers cannot be read; the betrayal is at 1 Kings 22:9, the slaughter at 22:18]? For Doeg gloried in these things, because by them he won for himself the closest friendship of the wicked king. But this glorying was evil and harmful to his soul: therefore David reproves Doeg: [[51:3|Why|Quid]], he says, [[51:3|dost thou glory in malice|gloriaris in malitia]], when it profits thee nothing? [[51:3|thou that art mighty in iniquity|Qui potens es in iniquitate]], that is, who wast mighty to slay innocent men, and didst abuse the power given thee by oppressing men better than thyself.

paras.t: Tota die, id est incessanter, injustitiam cogitavit lingua tua, id est, opus injustum, dolos, atque insidias contra me et meos amicos concepit lingua cordis tui, videlicet intellectus, quo interiora verba seu cogitationes formantur ; vel, Lingua oris cogitavit, id est, ex interiori cogitatione dixit. Doeg enim assidue insidiabatur sancto David et ejus consociis. Unde David ad Abiathar dixit : Sciebam in die illa, quod quum ibi esset Doeg Idumæus, procul dubio annuntiaret Sauli. Sicut novacula acuta fecisti dolum. Novacula acuta, quum pilos tollere habeat, aliquando dire et subito vulnerat. Sic detractores et impii, quum regem et dominum suum bene et recte informare deberent, falsa ei vel non revelanda annuntiant, aliis detrahunt, damna infligunt, et mortem procurant : et hoc modo Doeg dolum quæsivit in David et Achimelech, atque in ceteros, quos primo diffamavit, deinde occidit.
paras.en: [[51:4|All the day long|Tota die]], that is, unceasingly, [[51:4|thy tongue hath devised injustice|injustitiam cogitavit lingua tua]], that is, the tongue of thy heart, namely the understanding, by which inward words or thoughts are formed, has conceived unjust work, deceits and snares against me and my friends; or, the tongue of the mouth has devised, that is, has spoken out of inward thought. For Doeg was constantly lying in wait for holy David and his companions. Hence David said to Abiathar: [[1 Kings 22:22|I knew that day when Doeg, the Edomite, was there, that without doubt he would tell Saul|Sciebam in die illa, quod quum ibi esset Doeg Idumæus, procul dubio annuntiaret Sauli]]. [[51:4|as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit|Sicut novacula acuta fecisti dolum]]. A sharp razor, though its work is to take off hairs, sometimes wounds cruelly and suddenly. So detractors and wicked men, when they ought to inform their king and lord well and rightly, report to him falsehoods, or things that should not be revealed; they disparage others, inflict harm and procure death: and in this way Doeg sought to work deceit against David and Achimelech, and against the others, whom he first defamed and then slew.

paras.t: Dilexisti, o Doeg, malitiam, id est opus crudele, super benignitatem, id est magis quam opus misericordiæ, quoniam sacerdotes crudeliter trucidasti, neque innocentibus es misertus ; iniquitatem magis quam loqui æquitatem, id est, magis amasti loqui verba iniqua, dolosa et invidiosa, quam vera ac justa. Doeg enim, ut Sauli amplius complaceret, multa crimina David imposuit : et quod dixit Achimelech consuluisse Dominum pro David, aliqui dicunt fuisse falsum, et a Doeg confictum, sicut moris est detractoribus, dum aliquid verum annuntiant, falsa miscere. Non enim in textu libri Regum habebatur, quod Achimelech consuleret Dominum pro David, sed quod panes et gladium dederit ei.
paras.en: [[51:5|Thou hast loved|Dilexisti]], O Doeg, [[51:5|malice|malitiam]], that is, cruel work, [[51:5|more than goodness|super benignitatem]], that is, more than the work of mercy, since thou didst cruelly slaughter the priests and hadst no pity on the innocent; [[51:5|and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness|iniquitatem magis quam loqui æquitatem]], that is, thou hast loved more to speak words wicked, deceitful and spiteful than words true and just. For Doeg, to please Saul the more, laid many charges against David: and as for his saying that Achimelech consulted the Lord for David[[1 Kings 22:10||]], some say that this was false and made up by Doeg, as is the way of detractors, who, when they report something true, mix falsehoods with it. For it was not contained in the text of the book of Kings that Achimelech consulted the Lord for David, but that he gave him loaves and a sword[[1 Kings 21:6||]][[1 Kings 21:9||]].

paras.t: Dilexisti omnia verba præcipitationis, id est sermones ad præcipitandum et occidendum ordinatos, tam proprii oris, quam domini tui Saulis, quem libenter audisti loqui dura adversum me, o lingua dolosa, id est, o tu, Doeg, qui linguam dolosam habebas. Solet namque nomine partis, totum significari, præsertim dum quis maxime vacat actui partis alicujus : quemadmodum ait Apostolus, Cretenses semper mendaces, malæ bestiæ, ventres pigri.
paras.en: [[51:6|Thou hast loved all the words of ruin|Dilexisti omnia verba præcipitationis]] [præcipitatio, which the Douay-Rheims renders "ruin", is literally a hurling headlong; hence Denis's gloss], that is, speeches framed for hurling men down and killing them, both those of thy own mouth and those of thy lord Saul, whom thou didst gladly hear speaking harsh things against me, [[51:6|O deceitful tongue|o lingua dolosa]], that is, O thou, Doeg, who hadst a deceitful tongue. For the whole is often signified by the name of a part, especially when someone is chiefly given to the act of some part: as the Apostle says, [[Tit 1:12|The Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, slothful bellies|Cretenses semper mendaces, malæ bestiæ, ventres pigri]].

paras.t: Propterea, o Doeg, Deus justus judex destruet te in finem, omne spirituale et meritorium esse tibi auferendo, seu non præstando, teque æternaliter condemnando, nisi pœnitentiam egeris. Evellet te, et emigrabit te de tabernaculo tuo, id est, te ab hostibus tuis occidi permittet : sicut et factum est. In monte enim Gelboe cum Saule occisus est : quia, secundum Hebræos, ipse tunc erat armiger Saulis, qui quum vidisset Saulem irruisse in gladium suum, irruit etiam ipse in gladium proprium. Tunc ergo evulsus est Doeg de tabernaculo suo, id est, anima ejus a corpore separata fuit, et domum suam non magis inhabitavit, sed aliis eam reliquit. Et radicem tuam de terra viventium, id est, semen seu filium tuum evellet Dominus de terra Judææ. Nam et filium ejus David occidit, ut dicunt Hebræi. Qui enim annuntiavit David, dicens Saulem et filios ejus cecidisse in prælio, adjiciens se irruisse in Saulem, filius Doeg fuisse putatur. Quum enim dixisset ei David, Unde es tu ? respondit, Filius hominis advenæ Amalecitæ ego sum: tuncque occidit eum David, eo quod dixisset se misisse manum suam in christum Domini. Ecce ex isto apparet, quod David in spiritu præcognovit dejectionem et pœnam Doeg.
paras.en: [[51:7|Therefore|Propterea]], O Doeg, God the just judge will [[51:7|destroy thee for ever|destruet te in finem]], by taking away from thee, or not granting thee, all spiritual and meritorious being, and by condemning thee eternally, unless thou do penance. [[51:7|he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place|Evellet te, et emigrabit te de tabernaculo tuo]], that is, he will let thee be slain by thy enemies: as indeed came to pass. For he was slain with Saul on mount Gelboe, since, according to the Hebrews, he was then Saul's armourbearer; and when he saw that Saul had fallen upon his own sword[[1 Kings 31:4||]], [[1 Kings 31:5|he also fell upon his sword|irruit etiam ipse in gladium proprium]]. Then, therefore, Doeg was plucked out of his dwelling place, that is, his soul was separated from his body, and he dwelt in his house no more, but left it to others. [[51:7|and thy root out of the land of the living|Et radicem tuam de terra viventium]], that is, the Lord will pluck thy seed, or thy son, out of the land of Judea. For David killed his son too, as the Hebrews say. For the man who brought word to David that Saul and his sons had fallen in battle[[2 Kings 1:4||]], adding that he had set upon Saul[[2 Kings 1:10||]], is thought to have been the son of Doeg. For when David said to him, [[2 Kings 1:13|Whence art thou?|Unde es tu ?]] he answered, [[2 Kings 1:13|I am the son of a stranger of Amalec|Filius hominis advenæ Amalecitæ ego sum]]: and then David slew him[[2 Kings 1:15||]], because he had said that he had put forth his hand against the Lord's anointed[[2 Kings 1:16||]]. See, from this it appears that David foresaw in spirit the downfall and punishment of Doeg.

paras.t: Videbunt justi, id est, diligenter considerabunt justam Dei ultionem in Doeg, et timebunt divinum judicium, ne ipsis simili modo contingat. Pestilente enim flagellato, sapiens sapientior erit. Et super eum ridebunt, id est, de justa pœna Doeg gaudebunt, conformando se divinæ justitiæ, et dicent:
paras.en: [[51:8|The just shall see|Videbunt justi]], that is, shall diligently consider God's just vengeance on Doeg, [[51:8|and fear|et timebunt]] the divine judgment, lest the like befall them. For the saying holds: [[Prov 19:25|The wicked man being scourged, the fool shall be wiser|Pestilente enim flagellato, sapiens sapientior erit]] [Denis reads sapiens, "the wise man", where the Vulgate has stultus, "the fool"]. [[51:8|and shall laugh at him|Et super eum ridebunt]], that is, they shall rejoice at Doeg's just punishment, conforming themselves to God's justice, [[51:8|and say|et dicent]]:

paras.t: Ecce homo qui non posuit Deum adjutorem suum, id est, qualiter accidit ei, qui non est in Deo confisus. Sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum. Doeg enim ditissimus fuit, quoniam potentissimus pastorum Saul erat; hasque divitias adulando et justitiam pervertendo collegit, atque in ipsis potius quam in Deo speravit. Et prævaluit in vanitate sua. Doeg namque ad tempus contra justum David et alios bonos confortatus est, et in vanitate sua, id est superbia et vanis divitiis, floruit, viguit, aliosque oppressit.
paras.en: [[51:9|Behold the man that made not God his helper|Ecce homo qui non posuit Deum adjutorem suum]], that is, see how it has gone with him who did not trust in God. [[51:9|But trusted in the abundance of his riches|Sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum]]. For Doeg was very rich, since he was [[1 Kings 21:7|the chiefest of Saul's herdsmen|potentissimus pastorum Saul]]; and he gathered these riches by flattery and by perverting justice, and put his hope in them rather than in God. [[51:9|and prevailed in his vanity|Et prævaluit in vanitate sua]]. For Doeg was strengthened for a time against just David and other good men, and in his vanity, that is, in pride and vain riches, he flourished, grew strong, and oppressed others.

paras.t: Ego autem David sicut oliva fructifera exsistens in domo Dei, id est in Synagoga seu populo Judæorum, quos verbis atque exemplis instruxi, et in bonis operibus fecundavi: sicque ad instar olivæ fructificavi in populo, cujus dux fui, multos convertendo ad Deum, conversos quoque et bonos provocando ad meliora; speravi in misericordia Dei in æternum, id est toto tempore vitæ meæ, et in sæculum sæculi, id est sine fine: non quod in futura vita, scilicet in patria, maneat spes; sed, Speravi, inquit, in misericordia Dei in æternum, et in sæculum sæculi, id est ad hoc seu propter hunc finem, ut æterna, non temporalia, bona ab ipso adipiscar, et æternaliter felix efficiar.
paras.en: [[51:10|But I|Ego autem]], David, [[51:10|as a fruitful olive tree|sicut oliva fructifera]], being [[51:10|in the house of God|in domo Dei]], that is, in the Synagogue or people of the Jews, whom I have instructed by word and example and made fruitful in good works: and so, like an olive tree, I have borne fruit among the people whose leader I was, converting many to God, and spurring on the converted and the good to better things; [[51:10|have hoped in the mercy of God for ever|speravi in misericordia Dei in æternum]], that is, the whole time of my life, [[51:10|yea for ever and ever|et in sæculum sæculi]], that is, without end: not that hope remains in the life to come, that is, in the fatherland; but, I [[51:10|have hoped|Speravi]], he says, [[51:10|in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever|in misericordia Dei in æternum, et in sæculum sæculi]], that is, to this end, or for this purpose, that I may obtain from him eternal, not temporal, goods, and be made eternally happy.

paras.t: Confitebor tibi, id est, ad gloriam tuam tua bona, et mea mala, confessione laudis et pœnitentiæ enarrabo, in sæculum, id est diu et indesinenter, quia fecisti mihi tantam pietatem et gratiam. Et exspectabo nomen tuum, id est, patienter præstolabor adventum tuum, resurrectionem futuram, et gloriam Beatorum: nec in adversis relinquam te, sed quidquid mihi acciderit, spem habebo immobilem in te, seu in nomine tuo; quoniam bonum est in conspectu sanctorum tuorum, id est, quia nomen tuum dulce et bonum est judicio electorum, et in consideratione et experientia devotorum, qui gustaverunt quam magna sit multitudo dulcedinis tuæ, Domine, idcirco et optime sentiunt de te: quemadmodum Jeremias testatur, Bonus est Dominus sperantibus in eum, et animæ quærenti illum.
paras.en: [[51:11|I will praise thee|Confitebor tibi]] [confiteri means both to praise and to confess; hence the confession of praise and of penance], that is, to thy glory I will tell forth thy good things and my evil ones, by the confession of praise and of penance, [[51:11|for ever|in sæculum]], that is, long and unceasingly, [[51:11|because thou hast done it|quia fecisti]]: done me such great kindness and grace. [[51:11|and I will wait on thy name|Et exspectabo nomen tuum]], that is, I will patiently await thy coming, the resurrection to come, and the glory of the Blessed: nor will I forsake thee in adversity, but whatever befalls me I will keep an unshaken hope in thee, or in thy name; [[51:11|for it is good in the sight of thy saints|quoniam bonum est in conspectu sanctorum tuorum]], that is, because thy name is sweet and good in the judgment of the elect, and in the reflection and experience of the devout, who have tasted [[Ps 30:20|how great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord|quam magna sit multitudo dulcedinis tuæ, Domine]], and therefore think most highly of thee: as Jeremias testifies, [[Lam 3:25|The Lord is good to them that hope in him, to the soul that seeketh him|Bonus est Dominus sperantibus in eum, et animæ quærenti illum]].

51.title: EXPOSITIO ALLEGORICA, VIDELICET DE CHRISTO, EJUSDEM PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI PRIMI.
51.title_en: Allegorical exposition, namely of Christ, of the same fifty-first psalm.

paras.t: Allegoricus denique sensus sacræ Scripturæ est, dum ea quæ de veteribus Sanctis leguntur, de Christo intelliguntur. Omnia enim in figuris contingebant illis. Secundum hunc itaque intellectum, per David, qui interpretatur manu fortis, seu desiderabilis adspectu, intelligitur Christus, virtus Dei, qui est speciosus forma præ filiis hominum. Per Doeg vero, qui interpretatur motus, intelligitur Judas proditor, avaritia inflammatus ad Christum vendendum. Per Saulem vero, qui interpretatur appetitio seu mors, intelligitur princeps sacerdotum, seu populus Judæorum, Christi sanguinem sitiens.
paras.en: The allegorical sense of Holy Scripture, lastly, is when the things that are read of the saints of old are understood of Christ. For [[1 Cor 10:11|all these things happened to them in figure|Omnia enim in figuris contingebant illis]]. In this understanding, then, by David, which is interpreted *strong of hand* or *desirable to behold*, is understood [[1 Cor 1:24|Christ, the power of God|Christus, virtus Dei]], who is [[Ps 44:3|beautiful above the sons of men|speciosus forma præ filiis hominum]] [the margin gives Ps. xlv, 3, the Hebrew numbering; in the Vulgate it is Ps 44:3]. By Doeg, which is interpreted *movement*, is understood Judas the traitor[[John 12:6||]][[Matt 26:14||]], inflamed with avarice to sell Christ. By Saul, which is interpreted *desire* or *death*, is understood the chief of the priests, or the people of the Jews, thirsting for the blood of Christ[[Matt 27:1||]].

paras.t: Est igitur sensus: In finem, intellectus David, id est, intellectus hujus psalmi in Deum nos dirigens, convenit Christo per David figurato: quum venit Doeg Idumæus, id est Judas traditor avarus atque terrenus (Idumæus namque interpretatur terrenus), et annuntiavit Sauli, id est principi sacerdotum ac ejus concilio, et dixit ei: Venit David, id est Christus, in domum Achimelech, id est in societatem discipulorum suorum. Achimelech siquidem interpretatur regnum patris mei: per quod designatur Ecclesia, in qua Deus per gratiam regnat. Hæc vero annuntiatio Judæ fuit feria quarta, dum Christum vendidit, dicens Judæis eum venisse in Bethaniam cum discipulis suis in domum Marthæ; et item feria quinta, quando post buccellam exivit continuo, dicens Judæis Jesum venisse cum discipulis suis in cœnaculum, in quo Cœnam novissimam celebravit, et esse exiturum in locum in quem Jesus frequenter egredi consuevit. Unde scriptum est: Sciebat autem et Judas, qui tradebat eum, locum, quia frequenter Jesus convenerat illuc, etc. Diligenter namque indicavit Judas Judæis, locum in quem Christus advenit, et inter quos fuit: quoniam, sicut scriptum est, Quærebat opportunitatem ut traderet eum sine turba.
paras.en: The sense, then, is this: [[51:1|Unto the end, understanding for David|In finem, intellectus David]], that is, the understanding of this psalm, directing us unto God, befits Christ, who was figured by David: [[51:2|When Doeg the Edomite came|quum venit Doeg Idumæus]], that is, Judas the betrayer, covetous and earthly (for *Idumæan* is interpreted *earthly*), [[51:2|and told Saul|et annuntiavit Sauli]], that is, the chief of the priests and his council, and said to him: [[51:2|David went|Venit David]], that is, Christ, [[51:2|to the house of Achimelech|in domum Achimelech]], that is, into the fellowship of his disciples. For *Achimelech* is interpreted *the kingdom of my father*: by which is signified the Church, in which God reigns by grace. Now this telling by Judas was on the fourth day of the week [*feria quarta*, the Wednesday of Holy Week], when he sold Christ[[Matt 26:14||]], telling the Jews that he had come to Bethania with his disciples, to the house of Martha; and again on the fifth day of the week, when he, [[John 13:30|having received the morsel, went out immediately|post buccellam exivit continuo]], telling the Jews that Jesus had come with his disciples to the upper room in which he celebrated the Last Supper, and that he would go out to the place to which Jesus was often wont to go. Hence it is written: [[John 18:2|And Judas also, who betrayed him, knew the place: because Jesus had often resorted thither|Sciebat autem et Judas, qui tradebat eum, locum, quia frequenter Jesus convenerat illuc]], etc. [the margin gives Ibid. xxii, 2, that is, John 22:2; the words are John 18:2]. For Judas diligently showed the Jews the place to which Christ came, and among whom he was; since, as it is written, [[Luke 22:6|he sought opportunity to betray him in the absence of the multitude|Quærebat opportunitatem ut traderet eum sine turba]].

paras.t: Propheta igitur in persona Christi, seu ipse Christus, Judam proditorem redarguens, ait: Quid gloriaris in malitia, id est in venditione et proditione sanguinis innocentis Magistri ac Domini tui, qui tibi tot bona contulit, tantaque dilectionis signa ostendit, qui potens es in iniquitate, id est, qui tardus et impotens fuisti ad bene operandum, velox autem et cautus ad vendendum atque prodendum? Tota die, præcipue feria quarta et quinta ante Parasceven, injustitiam, id est injustam venditionem et fallacem proditionem, cogitavit lingua tua, quando cum Judæis tractabas quomodo me traderes eis. Sicut novacula acuta fecisti dolum, quia in facie me laudasti, et occulte detraxisti. Maxime autem dolum fecit Judas sicut acuta novacula, quando antecedebat cohortem et ministros Judæorum, dicens eisdem: Quemcumque osculatus fuero, ipse est; tenete eum, et ducite caute. Ideo namque Christus ei dixit: Juda, osculo Filium hominis tradis?
paras.en: So the Prophet in the person of Christ, or Christ himself, rebuking Judas the traitor, says: [[51:3|Why dost thou glory in malice|Quid gloriaris in malitia]], that is, in selling and betraying the blood of thy innocent Master and Lord, who bestowed so many good things on thee and showed thee such tokens of love, [[51:3|thou that art mighty in iniquity|qui potens es in iniquitate]], that is, who wast slow and powerless to do good, but quick and wary to sell and betray? [[51:4|All the day long|Tota die]], especially on the fourth and fifth days of the week before the Parasceve [that is, the Wednesday and Thursday before Good Friday], [[51:4|injustice|injustitiam]], that is, an unjust sale and a deceitful betrayal, [[51:4|thy tongue hath devised|cogitavit lingua tua]], when thou didst treat with the Jews how thou mightest deliver me to them[[Matt 26:14||]]. [[51:4|as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit|Sicut novacula acuta fecisti dolum]], because thou didst praise me to my face and slander me in secret. And Judas wrought deceit like a sharp razor most of all when he went before the band and the servants of the Jews, saying to them: [[Mark 14:44|Whomsoever I shall kiss, that is he. Lay hold on him: and lead him away carefully|Quemcumque osculatus fuero, ipse est; tenete eum, et ducite caute]]. For that is why Christ said to him: [[Luke 22:48|Judas, dost thou betray the Son of man with a kiss?|Juda, osculo Filium hominis tradis?]]

paras.t: Dilexisti, o Juda, malitiam super benignitatem, quia fur eras, et loculos habens, ea quæ mittebantur, furabaris: et ita benignitatem, id est misericordiæ opera, omisisti, quia egenis danda, tibi cupide reservasti; iniquitatem magis quam loqui æquitatem, id est, magis voluisti cum Judæis tractare de injusta Christi venditione et morte, quam Magistrum tuum, quem innocentem cognoveras, excusare. Dilexisti omnia verba præcipitationis, id est sermones principum sacerdotum de Christi præcipitatione, oppressione, et occisione loquentium, o lingua dolosa, quæ Magistro tuo dolose dixisti: Ave, Rabbi.
paras.en: [[51:5|Thou hast loved|Dilexisti]], O Judas, [[51:5|malice more than goodness|malitiam super benignitatem]], because thou wast a thief and, [[John 12:6|having the purse|loculos habens]], didst steal [[John 12:6|the things that were put therein|ea quæ mittebantur]] [the margin gives John vii, 6; the words are John 12:6]: and so thou didst neglect goodness, that is, the works of mercy, because what was to be given to the needy thou didst covetously keep for thyself; [[51:5|and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness|iniquitatem magis quam loqui æquitatem]], that is, thou wouldst rather treat with the Jews of the unjust sale and death of Christ than excuse thy Master, whom thou knewest to be innocent. [[51:6|Thou hast loved all the words of ruin|Dilexisti omnia verba præcipitationis]], that is, the speeches of the chief priests, who spoke of the casting down, the oppression and the slaying of Christ[[Matt 26:3||]], [[51:6|O deceitful tongue|o lingua dolosa]], that didst say deceitfully to thy Master: [[Matt 26:49|Hail, Rabbi|Ave, Rabbi]].

paras.t: Propterea Deus destruet te in finem, quia æternaliter disperibis atque damnaberis. Revelabunt enim cœli iniquitatem Judæ, et terra adversus eum consurget. Evellet te, et emigrabit te de tabernaculo tuo. Hoc in Juda impletum est, dum abiens, laqueo se suspendit, et crepuit medius, et diffusa sunt omnia viscera ejus. Tunc enim Deus evulsit animam ejus a corpore, ipsumque Judam separavit a tabernaculo suo, id est a domo Christi seu Apostolorum collegio, auferendo ei gratiam in præsenti, et gloriam in futuro. Unde et Christus ante passionem Apostolis dixit: Nonne ego vos duodecim elegi, et unus ex vobis diabolus est? Hoc autem (sicut Evangelista subjungit) de Juda asseruit. Et radicem tuam de terra viventium: id est, Deus in tantum destruet atque evellet te, o Juda, de terra viventium, id est de Ecclesia electorum et regione vivorum, ut reparari non possis, neque ad vitam resurgere. Per radicem ergo intelligit potentiam reparandi gratiam, seu resurgendi ad vitam.
paras.en: [[51:7|Therefore will God destroy thee for ever|Propterea Deus destruet te in finem]], because thou shalt perish and be damned eternally.
