For [[Job 20:27|The heavens shall reveal|Revelabunt enim cœli]] the iniquity of Judas, [[Job 20:27|and the earth shall rise up against him|et terra adversus eum consurget]]. [[51:7|he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place|Evellet te, et emigrabit te de tabernaculo tuo]]. This was fulfilled in Judas when he [[Matt 27:5|went and hanged himself with an halter|abiens, laqueo se suspendit]], and [[Acts 1:18|burst asunder in the midst: and all his bowels gushed out|crepuit medius, et diffusa sunt omnia viscera ejus]]. For then God plucked his soul out of his body, and separated Judas himself from his dwelling place, that is, from the house of Christ or the college of the Apostles, taking from him grace in the present and glory in the future. Hence too Christ said to the Apostles before his passion: [[John 6:71|Have not I chosen you twelve? And one of you is a devil|Nonne ego vos duodecim elegi, et unus ex vobis diabolus est]]? And this (as the Evangelist adds) he said of Judas[[John 6:72||]]. [[51:7|and thy root out of the land of the living|Et radicem tuam de terra viventium]]: that is, God will destroy and pluck thee out, O Judas, from the land of the living, that is, from the Church of the elect and the region of the living, so utterly that thou canst not be restored nor rise again to life. By the root, then, he means the power of recovering grace, or of rising again to life.

paras.t: Videbunt justi, id est sancti Apostoli aliique fideles, suspensionem et damnationem proditoris nequissimi. Propter quod in Actibus Lucas ait: Notum factum est (verbum hoc, scilicet suspensio Judæ) omnibus habitantibus Jerusalem, ita ut appellaretur ager ille lingua eorum, Haceldama, id est ager sanguinis. Ecce homo qui non posuit Deum adjutorem suum, id est, qui in Christo magistro ac Domino suo non fundavit nec stabilivit se ipsum; sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum, id est, spem suam in rebus terrenis locavit, quas, furando et Christum vendendo, collegit, et prævaluit in vanitate sua, id est, contra Christum roboravit cor suum, et in cupiditate vanissima ita permissus est prævalere contra Christum, quod vendidit et tradidit eum. Non quod simpliciter aliquis contra Christum prævaluit: ipse enim oblatus est quia voluit; sed prævaluisse dicuntur iniqui contra eum, quia permissi sunt eum occidere. Unde superius Christus dixit: Inimici autem mei vivunt, et confirmati sunt super me. Et Pilato dicenti, Nescis quia potestatem habeo crucifigendi te? Christus respondit: Non haberes potestatem adversum me ullam, nisi tibi datum esset desuper.
paras.en: [[51:8|The just shall see|Videbunt justi]], that is, the holy Apostles and the other faithful, the hanging[[Matt 27:5||]] and damnation of the most wicked traitor. Wherefore Luke says in the Acts: [[Acts 1:19|And it became known|Notum factum est]] (this thing, namely the hanging of Judas) [[Acts 1:19|to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem: so that the same field was called in their tongue, Haceldama, that is to say, The field of blood|omnibus habitantibus Jerusalem, ita ut appellaretur ager ille lingua eorum, Haceldama, id est ager sanguinis]]. [[51:9|Behold the man that made not God his helper|Ecce homo qui non posuit Deum adjutorem suum]], that is, who did not ground or establish himself in Christ his master and Lord; [[51:9|But trusted in the abundance of his riches|sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum]], that is, placed his hope in earthly things, which he gathered by stealing and by selling Christ, [[51:9|and prevailed in his vanity|et prævaluit in vanitate sua]], that is, hardened his heart against Christ, and in his most vain covetousness was permitted to prevail against Christ so far that he sold and betrayed him. Not that anyone prevailed against Christ simply: for [[Is 53:7|He was offered because it was his own will|oblatus est quia voluit]]; but the wicked are said to have prevailed against him because they were permitted to kill him. Hence Christ said above: [[Ps 37:20|But my enemies live, and are stronger than I|Inimici autem mei vivunt, et confirmati sunt super me]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxvi, 20; the words are Ps 37:20, earlier in the Psalter]. And to Pilate, who said: [[John 19:10|Knowest thou not that I have power to crucify thee|Nescis quia potestatem habeo crucifigendi te]]? Christ answered: [[John 19:11|Thou shouldst not have any power against me, unless it were given thee from above|Non haberes potestatem adversum me ullam, nisi tibi datum esset desuper]].

paras.t: Denique, sicut psalmus iste hucusque de Juda expositus est, sic posset de populo Judæorum contra Christum furentium explanari. Hic namque populus gloriabatur in malitia, irridendo, blasphemando, persequendo, occidendoque Dominum Salvatorem. Tota quoque die, præsertim in die Parasceves, injustitiam, id est falsas accusationes et mortis sententiam, contra Christum cogitavit lingua ipsius, clamans ad præsidem, Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram; et, Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum. Sed et sicut novacula acuta fecit dolum, mittendo discipulos Pharisæorum cum Herodianis, ut caperent Jesum in sermone. Dilexit etiam omnia verba præcipitationis, clamando ad judicem, Si hunc dimittis, non es amicus Cæsaris; et, Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros. Quibus verbis se ipsos et posteros suos vehementius præcipitaverunt, quam Christum. Pervenit enim, ut ait Apostolus, super eos ira Dei usque in finem.
paras.en: Lastly, as this psalm has so far been expounded of Judas, so it could be explained of the people of the Jews raging against Christ. For this people did [[51:3|glory in malice|gloriabatur in malitia]], mocking, blaspheming, persecuting and slaying the Lord and Saviour. Also, [[51:4|All the day long|Tota quoque die]], especially on the day of the Parasceve, its tongue [[51:4|hath devised|cogitavit]] [[51:4|injustice|injustitiam]] against Christ, that is, false accusations and the sentence of death, crying to the governor: [[Luke 23:2|We have found this man perverting our nation|Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram]]; and: [[John 19:15|Away with him: Away with him: Crucify him|Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum]]. And [[51:4|as a sharp razor|sicut novacula acuta]] it also [[51:4|wrought deceit|fecit dolum]], by sending the disciples of the Pharisees with the Herodians to catch Jesus in his speech[[Mark 12:13||]] [Denis's wording here is closer to Matt 22:15–16]. It loved also [[51:6|all the words of ruin|omnia verba præcipitationis]], crying to the judge: [[John 19:12|If thou release this man, thou art not Caesar's friend|Si hunc dimittis, non es amicus Cæsaris]]; and: [[Matt 27:25|His blood be upon us and upon our children|Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]]. By which words they cast themselves and their posterity down headlong more violently than they cast down Christ [a play on *præcipitatio*, the word rendered *ruin*, literally a casting down headlong]. For, as the Apostle says, [[1 Thess 2:16|the wrath of God is come upon them to the end|super eos ira Dei usque in finem]].

paras.t: Propter quod subditur: Propterea, scilicet propter iniquitatem in Christum commissam, Deus destruet te in finem, id est, usque in finem mundi relinquet te: quemadmodum per Danielem prædictum est, Finis ejus, scilicet populi Judæorum, vastitas, et usque in finem perseverabit desolatio. Et Amos: Domus Israel cecidit, et non adjiciet ut resurgat. Evellet te, et emigrabit te de tabernaculo tuo, id est, de terra promissionis ejiciet te: sicut per Titum et Vespasianum impletum cognoscimus, juxta illud Danielis: Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo. Et radicem tuam de terra viventium, id est, vim generativam auferet tibi in terra patrum tuorum: quia post ejectionem prædictam non generaverunt, nec multiplicati sunt in propria terra ut ante, nec eam reparare potuerunt ut ante. Vel, Radicem tuam de terra viventium, id est, a regno cœlorum omnino eradicabit te: sicut et Christus in Evangelio ait, Filii regni ejicientur in tenebras exteriores.
paras.en: Wherefore it is added: [[51:7|Therefore|Propterea]], namely because of the iniquity committed against Christ, [[51:7|will God destroy thee for ever|Deus destruet te in finem]] [Latin *in finem*, unto the end], that is, he will forsake thee until the end of the world: as was foretold by Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|the end thereof|Finis ejus]], namely of the people of the Jews, [[Dan 9:26|shall be waste|vastitas]], and [[Dan 9:27|the desolation shall continue even to the consummation, and to the end|usque in finem perseverabit desolatio]]. And Amos: [[Amos 5:1|The house of Israel is fallen, and it shall rise no more|Domus Israel cecidit, et non adjiciet ut resurgat]]. [[51:7|he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place|Evellet te, et emigrabit te de tabernaculo tuo]], that is, he will cast thee out of the land of promise: as we know was fulfilled by Titus and Vespasian, according to that word of Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|a people, with their leader, that shall come, shall destroy the city, and the sanctuary|Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo]]. [[51:7|and thy root out of the land of the living|Et radicem tuam de terra viventium]], that is, he will take from thee the power of begetting in the land of thy fathers: for after the casting out spoken of they did not beget, nor were they multiplied in their own land as before, nor could they restore it as before. Or: [[51:7|thy root out of the land of the living|Radicem tuam de terra viventium]], that is, he will root thee out altogether from the kingdom of heaven: as Christ too says in the Gospel: [[Matt 8:12|the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into the exterior darkness|Filii regni ejicientur in tenebras exteriores]].

paras.t: Videbunt justi, id est ex Judæis ad Christum conversi, prædictam infidelium pœnam, et timebunt Dominum Jesum Christum judicem tam districtum; et super eum, scilicet populum infidelem, ridebunt, applaudendo divinæ justitiæ; et dicent: Ecce homo qui non posuit Deum adjutorem suum: id est, vide Israel secundum carnem, qui ignorans Dei justitiam, et suam volens statuere, justitiæ Dei non fuit subjectus, nec gratiæ Christi est innixus, sed in lege totam spem posuit. Ideo additur: sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum, id est, de propriis meritis gloriatus est, et de lege ac genere superbivit, nec ad gratiam Dei et fidem Christi humiliter accedere voluit. Vel, Speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum corporalium: quia Judæi avarissimi erant. Nam Christo contra avaritiam disputante, dixerunt: Dæmonium habet et insanit, quid eum auditis? Et prævaluit in vanitate sua, id est, in superbia cordis sui ad tempus prævaluit contra primitivam Ecclesiam Christi, quam populus Judæorum frequenter persequebatur, sicut in Actis Apostolorum narratur.
paras.en: [[51:8|The just shall see|Videbunt justi]], that is, those of the Jews converted to Christ, the punishment of the unbelievers spoken of, [[51:8|and fear|et timebunt]] the Lord Jesus Christ, so strict a judge; and [[51:8|at him|super eum]], namely the unbelieving people, they [[51:8|shall laugh|ridebunt]], applauding the divine justice; [[51:8|and say|et dicent]]: [[51:9|Behold the man that made not God his helper|Ecce homo qui non posuit Deum adjutorem suum]]: that is, behold Israel according to the flesh, who, [[Rom 10:3|not knowing the justice of God|ignorans Dei justitiam]], [[Rom 10:3|and seeking to establish their own|et suam volens statuere]], [[Rom 10:3|have not submitted themselves to the justice of God|justitiæ Dei non fuit subjectus]] [Denis puts the Apostle's words in the singular, of Israel], nor leaned upon the grace of Christ, but put all his hope in the law. Therefore it is added: [[51:9|But trusted in the abundance of his riches|sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum]], that is, he gloried in his own merits and was proud of the law and of his race[[Matt 3:7||]][[John 8:33||]][[John 8:39||]], and would not come humbly to the grace of God and the faith of Christ. Or: he [[51:9|trusted in the abundance of his riches|Speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum]], his bodily riches: for the Jews were most avaricious. For when Christ disputed against avarice[[Luke 16:9||]][[John 10:1||]][[John 10:8||]][[John 10:10||]][[John 10:12||]][[John 10:13||]], they said: [[John 10:20|He hath a devil and is mad. Why hear you him?|Dæmonium habet et insanit, quid eum auditis?]] [[51:9|and prevailed in his vanity|Et prævaluit in vanitate sua]], that is, in the pride of his heart he prevailed for a time against the primitive Church of Christ, which the people of the Jews often persecuted, as is told in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 4:1||]][[Acts 7:1||]][[Acts 8:1||]].

paras.t: Ego autem sicut oliva fructifera in domo Dei. Hoc Christo maxime competit, qui, secundum Apostolum, multos filios adduxit in gloriam. Ipse namque fructum copiosissimum attulit Deo, quia per passionis suæ meritum omnes electos redemit, et non est in alio aliquo salus. Unde de fecunditate Christi apud Isaiam scriptum est: Hæc dicit Dominus formans me ex utero servum sibi, ut reducam Jacob ad eum; et glorificatus sum in oculis Domini. Et dixit: Parum est ut sis mihi servus ad suscitandas tribus Jacob, et fæces Israel convertendas; dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ. Et hoc est quod Daniel dicit: Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei. Christus itaque sicut oliva fructifera fuit in domo Dei: quæ domus sumus nos, secundum Apostolum, quia per ipsum reconciliati sumus Deo. Unde ad Ephesios dicit Apostolus: Deus instauravit omnia in Christo, sive quæ in cœlo sunt, sive quæ in terra.
paras.en: [[51:10|But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God|Ego autem sicut oliva fructifera in domo Dei]]. This befits Christ above all, who, according to the Apostle, [[Heb 2:10|had brought many children into glory|multos filios adduxit in gloriam]]. For he brought forth most abundant fruit to God, since by the merit of his passion he redeemed all the elect, and there is no [[Acts 4:12|salvation in any other|in alio aliquo salus]]. Hence of the fruitfulness of Christ it is written in Isaias: Thus saith the Lord, [[Is 49:5|that formed me from the womb to be his servant, that I may bring back Jacob unto him|formans me ex utero servum sibi, ut reducam Jacob ad eum]]; [[Is 49:5|and I am glorified in the eyes of the Lord|et glorificatus sum in oculis Domini]]. [[Is 49:6|And he said: It is a small thing that thou shouldst be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to convert the dregs of Israel|Et dixit: Parum est ut sis mihi servus ad suscitandas tribus Jacob, et fæces Israel convertendas]]; [[Is 49:6|I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ]]. And this is what Daniel says: [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]]. Christ, then, was as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God: [[Heb 3:6|which house are we|quæ domus sumus nos]], according to the Apostle, because through him [[Rom 5:10|we were reconciled to God|reconciliati sumus Deo]]. Hence the Apostle says to the Ephesians: God hath re-established [[Eph 1:10|all things in Christ, that are in heaven and on earth|omnia in Christo, sive quæ in cœlo sunt, sive quæ in terra]].

paras.t: Speravi in misericordia Dei in æternum, et in sæculum sæculi. Christus, secundum quod homo et aliquo modo viator, perfectissime semper speravit in Domino, non per spem, quæ est virtus theologica, quia illam non habuit, sicut nec fidem, quemadmodum infra plenius elucebit; sed per fiduciam quamdam seu exspectationem, ex caritate et gratia procedentem.
paras.en: I [[51:10|have hoped in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever|Speravi in misericordia Dei in æternum, et in sæculum sæculi]]. Christ, as man and in some manner a wayfarer [*viator*, one still on the way, not yet in possession of the goal], always hoped most perfectly in the Lord: not by hope, which is a theological virtue, for that he did not have, any more than faith, as will be made plainer below; but by a certain confidence or expectation proceeding from charity and grace.

paras.t: Confitebor tibi, Domine, id est, laudabo te, in sæculum, quia fecisti justam discretionem inter bonos et impios. Hinc nempe scriptum est: Exsultavit Jesus Spiritu Sancto, et ait: Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis. Et exspectabo nomen tuum, quoniam bonum, etc. Sicut spes est exspectatio, sic idem sunt sperare et exspectare, convenitque utrumque Christo eodem modo, scilicet ut viatori. Speravit enim et exspectavit a Deo resuscitari a morte, et glorificari in corpore, atque super omnes cœlos ascendere.
paras.en: [[51:11|I will praise thee|Confitebor tibi]], O Lord, that is, I will laud thee, [[51:11|for ever, because thou hast done|in sæculum, quia fecisti]] a just separation between the good and the wicked. For hence it is written: Jesus [[Luke 10:21|rejoiced in the Holy Ghost and said|Exsultavit Jesus Spiritu Sancto, et ait]]: [[Luke 10:21|I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hidden these things from the wise and prudent and hast revealed them to little ones|Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]. [[51:11|and I will wait on thy name, for it is good|Et exspectabo nomen tuum, quoniam bonum]], etc. As hope is expectation, so to hope and to wait are the same, and both befit Christ in the same way, namely as a wayfarer. For he hoped and waited to be raised by God from death, to be glorified in his body, and to ascend above all the heavens.

paras.t: Quæ autem jam omissa sunt, in præcedenti expositione satis elucidata videntur.
paras.en: What has now been passed over seems to have been sufficiently explained in the preceding exposition.

51.title: EXPOSITIO EJUSDEM PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI PRIMI TROPOLOGICA SEU MORALIS.
51.title_en: Tropological or moral exposition of the same fifty-first psalm.

paras.t: MORALITER insuper, per David intelligitur unusquisque fidelis; per Doeg vero, quilibet invidus et terrenus; per Saulem vero, iniqua potestas seu regnum reproborum; per Achimelech vero, Ecclesia Dei. Igitur, juxta moralem intelligentiam, iste est tituli sensus: In finem, intellectus David, id est, doctrina psalmi præsentis, in finem, id est in considerationem finalis retributionis et justæ remunerationis nos dirigens, competit David, id est fideli; quum venit Doeg Idumæus ad Saulem, id est aliquis terrenus et obtrectator, ad principem malum seu quempiam pestiferum et potentem, bonos tyrannice opprimentem; et annuntiavit ei: Venit David in domum Achimelech, id est, fidelis quisque venit in obedientiam sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ. Ideo enim iniqui persequi solent justos, quoniam vitam atque præcepta eorum abominantur, et quoniam justi præceptis Ecclesiæ obsequuntur.
paras.en: Morally, moreover, by David is understood each one of the faithful; by Doeg, any envious and earthly man; by Saul, wicked power, or the kingdom of the reprobate; by Achimelech, the Church of God. According to the moral understanding, then, this is the sense of the title: [[51:1|Unto the end, understanding for David|In finem, intellectus David]], that is, the teaching of the present psalm, directing us *unto the end*, that is, to the consideration of the final retribution and of the just reward, belongs to *David*, that is, to the faithful man; [[51:2|When Doeg the Edomite came|quum venit Doeg Idumæus]] to Saul, that is, some earthly man and detractor, to a wicked prince, or to someone baneful and powerful who tyrannically oppresses the good; [[51:2|and told Saul|et annuntiavit ei]]: [[51:2|David went|Venit David]] [[51:2|to the house of Achimelech|in domum Achimelech]], that is, each one of the faithful comes into obedience to holy mother Church. For the wicked are wont to persecute the just for this reason, that they abhor their life and precepts, and because the just obey the precepts of the Church.

paras.t: Itaque dicit: Quid gloriaris in malitia? id est, cur ex electione et habitu malo atque proposito peccas? Quidam enim ex infirmitate peccant: et horum peccatum est veniale, vel minus grave. Quidam vero ex habitu malo: et hi gloriantur in malo, et difficillime corriguntur; estque gloriatio eorum mortalis et pessima, quia, secundum Philosophum, gloriatio seu delectatio operationi annexa, est signum habitus interioris. De sic quoque gloriantibus in Proverbiis scriptum est: Lætantur quum male fecerint, et exsultant in rebus pessimis; et in Evangelio: Væ vobis qui ridetis nunc, quia lugebitis et flebitis. Hæc namque est gloriatio mundi, in æternam tristitiam convertenda: cui contrariam tristitiam habent electi in æternam lætitiam permutandam, quemadmodum Christus discipulis protestatur: Amen, amen dico vobis, quia plorabitis et flebitis vos, mundus autem gaudebit; sed tristitia vestra vertetur in gaudium, et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis. Verumtamen nemo gloriatur in malo, sub ratione mali, sed sub ratione alicujus apparentis boni: quia, secundum Dionysium, nemo respiciens ad malum operatur, quum bonum sit objectum appetitus, in quo est prima radix peccati.
paras.en: So he says: [[51:3|Why dost thou glory in malice?|Quid gloriaris in malitia?]] that is, why dost thou sin from choice, and from an evil habit and purpose? For some sin from infirmity, and their sin is venial, or less grave. But some sin from an evil habit: and these glory in evil, and are corrected with the greatest difficulty[[Eccles 1:15||]]; and their glorying is mortal and most wicked, since, according to the Philosopher, the glorying or delight joined to an action is a sign of the inward habit. Of those who glory in this way it is also written in Proverbs: They [[Prov 2:14|are glad when they have done evil, and rejoice in the most wicked things|Lætantur quum male fecerint, et exsultant in rebus pessimis]]; and in the Gospel: [[Luke 6:25|Woe to you that now laugh: for you shall mourn and weep|Væ vobis qui ridetis nunc, quia lugebitis et flebitis]]. For this is the glorying of the world, which is to be turned into everlasting sorrow; and against it the elect have a sorrow that is to be changed into everlasting gladness, as Christ declares to his disciples: [[John 16:20|Amen, amen, I say to you, that you shall lament and weep, but the world shall rejoice|Amen, amen dico vobis, quia plorabitis et flebitis vos, mundus autem gaudebit]]: but [[John 16:20|your sorrow shall be turned into joy|tristitia vestra vertetur in gaudium]], [[John 16:22|And your joy no man shall take from you|et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis]]. Yet no one glories in evil under the aspect of evil, but under the aspect of some apparent good: for, according to Dionysius, no one acts with his eye upon evil, since the good is the object of the appetite, in which lies the first root of sin.

paras.t: Itaque: Quid gloriaris in malitia, qui potens es in iniquitate? Secundum Anselmum, qui potest quod sibi non expedit, quanto id amplius potest, tanto impotentior est. Posse enim peccare, impotentia magis dicenda est, quam potentia: sicut peccatum potius dicitur nihil, quam aliquid. Quomodo ergo aliquis potens est in iniquitate? Et respondendum, quod homo dicitur potens in iniquitate, non quod potentia male agendi, secundum quod est origo et causa peccati, sit vera potentia; sed quia potentia sibi divinitus ad bene agendum collata abutitur, atque per eam mala violenter et prompte exsequitur. Juxta hunc sensum in Jeremia scriptum est: Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala. Non quod sapientia malefaciendi, sit vera sapientia, sed quædam perversa industria. Unde Sapiens dicit: In malevolam animam non introibit sapientia. Sed quia nonnulli dato ingenio atque scientia abutuntur, et vias peccandi subtiliter indagantur; idcirco sapientes dicuntur ut faciant mala.
paras.en: So then: [[51:3|Why dost thou glory in malice|Quid gloriaris in malitia]], [[51:3|thou that art mighty in iniquity?|qui potens es in iniquitate?]] According to Anselm, he who is able to do what is not good for him is the more powerless the more he is able to do it. For to be able to sin ought rather to be called powerlessness than power, just as sin is rather called nothing than something. How then is anyone mighty in iniquity? The answer is that a man is called mighty in iniquity, not because the power of doing evil, as it is the origin and cause of sin, is true power; but because he abuses the power given him by God for doing good, and by it carries out evil things violently and readily. In this sense it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 4:22|they are wise to do evil|Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala]]. Not that the wisdom of evildoing is true wisdom; it is a kind of perverse industry. Hence the Wise Man says: [[Wis 1:4|wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul|In malevolam animam non introibit sapientia]]. But because some abuse the wit and knowledge given them, and track out the ways of sinning with subtlety, they are therefore said to be wise to do evil.

paras.t: Tota die, id est indesinenter et animo obstinato, injustitiam, id est dolum et detractionem, cogitavit lingua tua. Si linguam sumamus pro organo corporis, et cogitationem pro interiori actu meditantis; tunc linguæ non convenit cogitare, sed cordi. Per hoc ergo quod hæc duo consociat, Lingua et Cogitavit, insinuat, quod quam cito cogitavit injustitiam, elocutus est eam: quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico habetur, Cor fatui quasi vas confractum. Et iterum: In ore fatuorum, cor illorum; et in corde sapientium, os eorum. Hæc est expositio venerandi theologi Hugonis. Verumtamen, quia superius de viro sapienti et justo dictum est, Et lingua mea meditabitur justitiam tuam, ubi meditari seu cogitare adscribitur linguæ sapientis (cujus, ut dictum est, os est in corde ipsius, quoniam aptum tempus loquendi expectat, juxta illud, Totum spiritum suum profert stultus, sapiens differt et reservat in posterum); ideo superiores duæ expositiones acceptiores videntur.
paras.en: [[51:4|All the day long|Tota die]], that is, unceasingly and with an obstinate mind, [[51:4|thy tongue hath devised|cogitavit lingua tua]] [[51:4|injustice|injustitiam]], that is, guile and detraction. If we take the tongue for the bodily organ, and devising for the inward act of one who meditates, then devising does not belong to the tongue but to the heart. By joining these two, then, *tongue* and *hath devised*, he gives us to understand that as soon as he devised injustice he spoke it out: as is said in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 21:17|The heart of a fool is like a broken vessel|Cor fatui quasi vas confractum]]. And again: [[Ecclus 21:29|The heart of fools is in their mouth: and the mouth of wise men is in their heart|In ore fatuorum, cor illorum; et in corde sapientium, os eorum]]. This is the exposition of the venerable theologian Hugh. Yet since it was said earlier of the wise and just man, [[Ps 34:28|And my tongue shall meditate thy justice|Et lingua mea meditabitur justitiam tuam]], where meditating or devising is ascribed to the tongue of the wise man (whose mouth, as has been said, is in his heart, since he waits for the fit time to speak, according to the saying, [[Prov 29:11|A fool uttereth all his mind: a wise man deferreth, and keepeth it till afterwards.|Totum spiritum suum profert stultus, sapiens differt et reservat in posterum]]), the two expositions given before [that is, in the two preceding articles, on the literal and the allegorical sense] seem the more acceptable.

paras.t: Sicut novacula acuta fecisti dolum, decipiendo proximum tuum; idcirco maledictus es: juxta illud Malachiæ, Maledictus dolosus, qui habet in grege suo, etc.; quia rex magnus ego sum, dicit Dominus. Et alius Propheta: Fraudulenti vasa pessima sunt; ipse enim cogitationes suas concinnabit ad perdendos mites in sermone mendacii. Quocontra de Nathanaele Christus ait: Ecce vere Israelita, in quo dolus non est. Omnino ergo caveamus tam pessimum vitium, si Christo conformari optamus, de quo scriptum est: Nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus.
paras.en: [[51:4|as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit|Sicut novacula acuta fecisti dolum]], by deceiving thy neighbour; and therefore thou art cursed, according to that saying of Malachias: [[Mal 1:14|Cursed is the deceitful man that hath in his flock|Maledictus dolosus, qui habet in grege suo]], etc.; [[Mal 1:14|for I am a great King, saith the Lord|quia rex magnus ego sum, dicit Dominus]]. And another Prophet: [[Is 32:7|The vessels of the deceitful are most wicked: for he hath framed devices to destroy the meek, with lying words|Fraudulenti vasa pessima sunt; ipse enim cogitationes suas concinnabit ad perdendos mites in sermone mendacii]]. Against this Christ says of Nathanael: [[John 1:47|Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom there is no guile|Ecce vere Israelita, in quo dolus non est]]. Let us therefore beware altogether of so wicked a vice, if we desire to be conformed to Christ, of whom it is written: [[1 Pet 2:22|neither was guile found in his mouth|Nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus]].

paras.t: Dilexisti malitiam super benignitatem. Omnis qui peccat scienter, diligit malum magis quam bonum. Dilexisti etiam iniquitatem, id est verba illicita, magis quam loqui æquitatem, id est verba justa, vera et instructiva. Quocontra Ecclesiasticus dicit: Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccatum. Et Apostolus: Omnis, inquit, sermo malus ex ore vestro non procedat; et: Omnis amaritudo, et ira, et indignatio, et clamor tollatur a vobis. Estote autem invicem benigni, misericordes, donantes invicem, sicut et Deus in Christo donavit vobis.
paras.en: [[51:5|Thou hast loved malice more than goodness|Dilexisti malitiam super benignitatem]]. Everyone who sins knowingly loves evil more than good. Thou hast loved also [[51:5|iniquity|iniquitatem]], that is, unlawful words, [[51:5|rather than to speak righteousness|magis quam loqui æquitatem]], that is, words that are just, true and instructive. Against this Ecclesiasticus says: [[Ecclus 21:2|Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent|Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccatum]]. And the Apostle says: [[Eph 4:29|Let no evil speech proceed from your mouth|sermo malus ex ore vestro non procedat]]; and: [[Eph 4:31|Let all bitterness and anger and indignation and clamour|Omnis amaritudo, et ira, et indignatio, et clamor]] [[Eph 4:31|be put away from you|tollatur a vobis]]. [[Eph 4:32|And be ye kind one to another: merciful, forgiving one another, even as God hath forgiven you in Christ.|Estote autem invicem benigni, misericordes, donantes invicem, sicut et Deus in Christo donavit vobis]] [the margin gives only Eph. iv, 29; the rest comes from Eph 4:31–32].

paras.t: Dilexisti omnia verba præcipitationis: quod est caritati fraternæ contrarium, et per consequens mortale peccatum, cui debetur æternum tormentum. Unde subjungitur: Propterea Deus destruet te in finem. Expositio hujus versus, ex præcedentibus elucescit.
paras.en: [[51:6|Thou hast loved all the words of ruin|Dilexisti omnia verba præcipitationis]] [*præcipitatio*: a headlong casting down; Denis takes these as reckless words that ruin others]: which is contrary to brotherly charity, and consequently a mortal sin, to which everlasting torment is due. Hence there follows: [[51:7|Therefore will God destroy thee for ever|Propterea Deus destruet te in finem]]. The exposition of this verse is plain from what has gone before.

paras.t: Videbunt justi pœnam malorum in præsenti sæculo, et in finali judicio, et timebunt, id est, divinam justitiam reverebuntur, et filialem timorem concipient circa Deum. Hoc etenim modo etiam angeli sancti timebunt ex condemnatione reproborum, prout in Job de diabolo sub appellatione Behemoth dicitur: Quum sublatus fuerit, timebunt angeli, et territi purgabuntur. Et Christus in Evangelio: Virtutes, inquit, cœlorum movebuntur. Et super eum, scilicet iniquum et reprobum, ridebunt: sicut inferius dicitur, Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam. Propter quod, per Malachiam Dominus ait de justis: Egrediemini et salietis quasi vituli de armento, et calcabitis impios in die qua ego facio, dicit Dominus; et in Isaia, Egredientur, et videbunt cadavera virorum qui prævaricati sunt in me.
paras.en: [[51:8|The just shall see|Videbunt justi]] the punishment of the wicked in the present world and at the final judgment, [[51:8|and fear|et timebunt]], that is, they will reverence the divine justice and conceive a filial fear towards God. For in this way the holy angels too will fear at the condemnation of the reprobate, as is said in Job of the devil under the name of Behemoth: [[Job 41:16|When he shall raise him up, the angels shall fear, and being affrighted shall purify themselves|Quum sublatus fuerit, timebunt angeli, et territi purgabuntur]] [in the Vulgate this verse falls in the passage on Leviathan; Behemoth is described in Job 40]. And Christ in the Gospel: [[Luke 21:26|the powers|Virtutes]], he says, [[Luke 21:26|of heaven shall be moved|cœlorum movebuntur]] [Denis's wording is that of Luke 21:26; Matt 24:29 has *commovebuntur*]. [[51:8|and shall laugh|ridebunt]] [[51:8|at him|Et super eum]], that is, at the wicked and reprobate man: as is said further on, [[Ps 57:11|The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge|Lætabitur justus quum viderit vindictam]]. For which reason the Lord says of the just by Malachias: [[Mal 4:2|you shall go forth, and shall leap like calves of the herd|Egrediemini et salietis quasi vituli de armento]], [[Mal 4:3|And you shall tread down the wicked|et calcabitis impios]] [[Mal 4:3|in the day that I do this, saith the Lord|in die qua ego facio, dicit Dominus]]; and in Isaias: [[Is 66:24|And they shall go out, and see the carcasses of the men that have transgressed against me|Egredientur, et videbunt cadavera virorum qui prævaricati sunt in me]].

paras.t: Et dicent justi de impio: Ecce homo qui non posuit Deum adjutorem suum. Quod est contra exhortationem Isaiæ: Quis ambulat in tenebris, et non est lumen ei? Speret in nomine Domini, et innitatur super Deum suum. Sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum, vel corporalium, vel spiritualium, scilicet meritorum, reputans se aliquid esse, quum nihil sit, et de bonis operibus glorians in se, quasi non acceperit aliunde. Non ergo in propria justitia confidamus, nec in incerto divitiarum speremus, ut dicere valeamus cum sancto Job: Si justificare me voluero, os meum condemnabit me. Etiamsi simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea. Et rursum ait: Si putavi aurum robur meum, et obrizo dixi, Fiducia mea; si lætatus sum super divitiis meis multis. Hinc enim Apostolus dicit: Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe non sublime sapere, nec sperare in incerto divitiarum, sed in Deo vivo. Et alibi: Nemo, inquit, glorietur in hominibus, scilicet in se ipso; sed qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur. Omnem quippe vanam gloriam de propriis meritis excludit prorsus a nobis, quod Christus ait: Quum feceritis omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite: Servi inutiles sumus; quod debuimus facere, fecimus. Et prævaluit in vanitate sua, id est, in temporali prosperitate ad tempus floruit, et in desideriis propriis ambulavit, aliosque oppressit.
paras.en: [[51:8|and say|Et dicent]] the just of the wicked man: [[51:9|Behold the man that made not God his helper|Ecce homo qui non posuit Deum adjutorem suum]]. This is against the exhortation of Isaias: Who is there [[Is 50:10|that hath walked in darkness, and hath no light|ambulat in tenebris, et non est lumen ei]]? [[Is 50:10|let him hope in the name of the Lord, and lean upon his God|Speret in nomine Domini, et innitatur super Deum suum]]. [[51:9|But trusted in the abundance of his riches|Sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum]], either bodily riches or spiritual ones, that is, merits, thinking himself to be something when he is nothing, and glorying in himself over his good works, as though he had not received them from another. Let us not, then, trust in our own justice, nor hope in the uncertainty of riches, so that we may be able to say with holy Job: [[Job 9:20|If I would justify myself, my own mouth shall condemn me|Si justificare me voluero, os meum condemnabit me]]. [[Job 9:21|Although I should be simple, even this my soul shall be ignorant of|Etiamsi simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea]]. And again he says: [[Job 31:24|If I have thought gold my strength, and have said to fine gold: My confidence|Si putavi aurum robur meum, et obrizo dixi, Fiducia mea]]; [[Job 31:25|If I have rejoiced over my great riches|si lætatus sum super divitiis meis multis]]. For hence the Apostle says: [[1 Tim 6:17|Charge the rich of this world not to be highminded nor to trust in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God|Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe non sublime sapere, nec sperare in incerto divitiarum, sed in Deo vivo]]. And elsewhere: [[1 Cor 3:21|Let no man|Nemo]], he says, [[1 Cor 3:21|glory in men|glorietur in hominibus]], that is, in himself; but [[2 Cor 10:17|he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord|qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]]. For all vainglory over our own merits is wholly shut out from us by what Christ says: [[Luke 17:10|when you shall have done all these things that are commanded you, say: We are unprofitable servants; we have done that which we ought to do|Quum feceritis omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite: Servi inutiles sumus; quod debuimus facere, fecimus]]. [[51:9|and prevailed in his vanity|Et prævaluit in vanitate sua]], that is, flourished for a time in temporal prosperity, and walked in his own desires, and oppressed others.

paras.t: Ego autem sicut oliva fructifera in domo Dei. Hoc cuilibet homini competit, qui opera bona producit, alios vero vita et moribus instruit, atque in vitam æternam fructificat: qualem fuisse Levi patriarcham Malachias testatur, dicens: Pactum meum fuit cum Levi, et a facie nominis mei pavebat; in pace et æquitate ambulavit mecum, et multos avertit ab iniquitate. Istud autem ad prælatos et aliorum rectores maxime pertinet, de quorum manu Deus sanguinem pereuntium requiret. Speravi in misericordia Dei in æternum, et in sæculum sæculi. Scio enim quia non sum sufficiens cogitare aliquid ex me, quasi ex me, sed sufficientia mea ex Deo est. Cetera ex præhabitis lucent.
paras.en: [[51:10|But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God|Ego autem sicut oliva fructifera in domo Dei]]. This befits any man who brings forth good works, instructs others by his life and conduct, and bears fruit unto life everlasting: such as Malachias bears witness the patriarch Levi was, saying: [[Mal 2:5|My covenant was with|Pactum meum fuit cum]] Levi, [[Mal 2:5|and he was afraid before my name|et a facie nominis mei pavebat]]; [[Mal 2:6|he walked with me in peace, and in equity|in pace et æquitate ambulavit mecum]], [[Mal 2:6|and turned many away from iniquity|et multos avertit ab iniquitate]]. This belongs most of all to prelates and to those who rule others, at whose hand God will require the blood of those who perish. [[51:10|have hoped in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever|Speravi in misericordia Dei in æternum, et in sæculum sæculi]]. For I know that I am not sufficient to think anything of myself, as of myself, but my sufficiency is from God[[2 Cor 3:5||]] [Denis puts the Apostle's words in the first person singular]. The rest is clear from what has gone before.

paras.t: Ecce psalmum brevem et doctrinalem audivimus, in quo inter bonos et malos pulchre distinguitur, judiciumque divinum evidenter commemoratur. Studeamus ergo ab operibus tenebrarum diffugere, et olivæ fructiferæ comparari, omne tempus fructuose expendendo, et neminem scandalizando, ne simus aliis lapis offensionis et petra scandali; sed sic luceat vita nostra proximis nostris, ut ædificentur ex nobis.
paras.en: See, we have heard a short and instructive psalm, in which the good and the wicked are beautifully distinguished, and the divine judgment is plainly recalled. Let us strive, then, to flee from the works of darkness and to be likened to the fruitful olive, spending all our time fruitfully and scandalizing no one, lest we be to others a stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal; but let our life so shine before our neighbours that they may be edified by us.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Defensor vitæ et animæ nostræ, Domine, pravis conatibus nostris semper obsiste, et ne sinas nos in nostra prævalere vanitate: ut sicut oliva fructificantes in domo tua, in æternum exspectemus nomen tuum in conspectu Sanctorum tuorum.
paras.en: Prayer. O Lord, defender of our life and of our soul, ever withstand our wicked endeavours, and suffer us not to prevail in our own vanity: that, bearing fruit like the olive in thy house, we may wait on thy name for ever in the sight of thy Saints.

52.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI SECUNDI : DIXIT INSIPIENS IN CORDE SUO.
52.title_en: Exposition of the fifty-second psalm: The fool said in his heart.

paras.t: Est autem titulus psalmi jam explanandi : In finem, pro Amalec, intellectus David. De titulo isto plura dici possent, quia diversi de ipso diversimode sentiunt. Sed breviter transiens dico, sicut et Hugo affirmat, quod psalmus iste, quamvis videatur conscriptus occasione Amalecitarum, qui uxores David atque virorum suorum rapuerunt cum pueris et jumentis, succensa civitate Siceleg, quam Achis rex Geth dedit David fugienti Saulem, quemadmodum primo Regum scribitur ; non tamen agit psalmus iste de ipsa historia, sed de re significata per Amalec, qui interpretatur dolens sive parturiens, et designat corpus Christi mysticum, puta Ecclesiam pro peccatis gementem, et filios spiritualiter per verbum prædicationis parturientem, quemadmodum ait Apostolus : Filioli mei, quos iterum parturio, donec formetur Christus in vobis ; et alibi, Per Evangelium ego vos genui. In hoc autem psalmo increpantur homines contra Ecclesiam insurgentes. Et est tituli sensus : Intellectus David, id est psalmus iste in quo ponitur eruditio David, in finem, id est in Christum, nos dirigens, est conscriptus pro Amalec, id est pro significato per ipsum, videlicet pro Ecclesia, cujus adversarii hic increpantur. Præterea psalmus iste in verbis et sensu multum conformis est psalmo tertiodecimo. Quoniam tamen in titulo differt, quia illius psalmi titulus est, Psalmus David ; credendum est quod etiam intentione sensuque differat, saltem in parte.
paras.en: Now the title of the psalm now to be explained is: [[52:1|Unto the end|In finem]], for Amalec [Denis's text reads *pro Amalec*, "for Amalec", where the Clementine Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims have "for Maeleth"], [[52:1|understandings to David|intellectus David]]. Many things could be said of this title, since different men think differently about it. But passing over it briefly, I say, as Hugh also affirms, that although this psalm seems to have been written on the occasion of the Amalecites, who carried off the wives of David[[1 Kings 30:5||]] and of his men, with the children and the beasts[[1 Kings 30:2||]], having burnt the city of Siceleg[[1 Kings 30:1||]], which Achis king of Geth had given to David as he fled from Saul, as is written in the first book of Kings; yet this psalm does not treat of that history itself, but of the thing signified by Amalec, which is interpreted *grieving* or *being in labour*, and which stands for the mystical body of Christ, namely the Church, groaning for sins and spiritually bringing forth children by the word of preaching, as the Apostle says: [[Gal 4:19|My little children, of whom I am in labour again, until Christ be formed in you|Filioli mei, quos iterum parturio, donec formetur Christus in vobis]]; and elsewhere: [[1 Cor 4:15|by the gospel, I have begotten you|Per Evangelium ego vos genui]]. Now in this psalm men who rise up against the Church are rebuked. And the sense of the title is: [[52:1|understandings to David|Intellectus David]], that is, this psalm, in which the teaching of David is set down, directing us [[52:1|unto the end|in finem]], that is, unto Christ, was written for Amalec, that is, for what is signified by him, namely for the Church, whose adversaries are rebuked here. Moreover, this psalm agrees closely in words and sense with the thirteenth psalm. But since it differs in its title (for the title of that psalm is: [[Ps 13:1|a psalm for David|Psalmus David]]), it is to be believed that it differs also in intention and sense, at least in part.

paras.t: Ait ergo sanctus Propheta : Dixit insipiens in corde suo, id est, divinorum notitia carens, apud se cogitavit : Non est Deus. Quod dupliciter accipi potest. Primo, quod aliquis propter nimiam mentis cæcitatem putet Deum non esse, sicut quidam philosophi negabant prima principia : quum tamen nec Deum non esse, nec prima principia esse falsa, ab aliquo intelligi possit, quum utrumque sit per se notum, secundum opinionem probabilem. Secundo, sic accipi potest : Dixit insipiens in corde suo, Non est Deus : id est, omnis insipienter agens, et criminaliter vivens, ita se habuit, ac si putaret Deum non esse ; imo quem verbo confitetur, opere negat, sicut de quibusdam ait Apostolus : Dicunt se nosse Deum, factis autem negant. Unde et in prima Joannis habetur : Qui se dicit nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est. Quod de notitia formata intelligendum est. Notitiam enim informem de Deo reprobi habent, sicut de eis ait Apostolus : Quum cognovissent Deum, non sicut Deum glorificaverunt. Hoc secundo modo multi dicunt in corde suo, Non est Deus : omnes videlicet qui judicium Dei non timent ; sic enim agunt, ac si Deum putarent non esse justum. Sed primo modo pauci dicunt Deum non esse : quia, Augustino attestante, sicut magna perfectio paucorum est, sic magna quoque insania paucorum est.
paras.en: The holy Prophet says, then: [[52:1|The fool said in his heart|Dixit insipiens in corde suo]], that is, one who lacks the knowledge of divine things has thought within himself: [[52:1|There is no God|Non est Deus]]. This can be taken in two ways. First, that someone, through excessive blindness of mind, thinks that God does not exist, as certain philosophers denied the first principles; although neither that God does not exist, nor that the first principles are false, can be understood by anyone, since each is known of itself [*per se notum*, that is, self-evident], according to a probable opinion. Secondly, it can be taken thus: [[52:1|The fool said in his heart: There is no God|Dixit insipiens in corde suo, Non est Deus]]: that is, everyone who acts foolishly and lives in grave sin [*criminaliter*, that is, in mortal sin] has behaved as if he thought there were no God; indeed, the God whom he confesses in word, he denies in deed, as the Apostle says of certain men: [[Tit 1:16|They profess that they know God: but in their works they deny him|Dicunt se nosse Deum, factis autem negant]]. Hence also in the first epistle of John we have: [[1 John 2:4|He who saith that he knoweth him and keepeth not his commandments is a liar|Qui se dicit nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est]]. This is to be understood of formed knowledge [knowledge *formed*, that is, quickened by charity]. For the reprobate have an unformed knowledge of God, as the Apostle says of them: [[Rom 1:21|when they knew God, they have not glorified him as God|Quum cognovissent Deum, non sicut Deum glorificaverunt]]. In this second way many say in their heart: [[52:1|There is no God|Non est Deus]]: namely all who do not fear the judgment of God; for they act as if they thought that God is not just. But in the first way few say that God does not exist: for, as Augustine attests, just as great perfection belongs to few, so great madness too belongs to few.

paras.t: Deinde de insipientibus loquitur Propheta pluraliter, dicens : Corrupti sunt, et abominabiles facti sunt in iniquitatibus. Integritas mentis, est conversio ejus ad Deum ; corruptio vero ipsius, est aversio a Deo, et ad caduca conversio. Propter quod de quibusdam a summo uno aversis, atque ad ista terrena et vana conversis, in Osee scriptum est : Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt. De talibus quoque Apostolus ait : Homines mente corrupti, reprobi circa fidem. Sic ergo corrupti sunt mente, et abominabiles facti sunt, id est irrationabiles atque odibiles, in iniquitatibus, seu propter iniquitates. Non est qui faciat bonum æternæ vitæ meritorium, ex illis insipientibus, quoniam gratiam et caritatem non habent, sine quibus nemo valet mereri, aut Deo acceptus esse.
paras.en: Then the Prophet speaks of the fools in the plural, saying: [[52:2|They are corrupted, and become abominable in iniquities|Corrupti sunt, et abominabiles facti sunt in iniquitatibus]]. The soundness of the mind is its turning to God; its corruption is its turning away from God and turning to perishable things. For this reason it is written in Osee of certain men turned away from the one highest Good and turned to these earthly and vain things: [[Osee 10:2|Their heart is divided: now they shall perish|Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt]]. Of such men too the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 3:8|men corrupted in mind, reprobate concerning the faith|Homines mente corrupti, reprobi circa fidem]]. So, then, [[52:2|they are corrupted|corrupti sunt]] in mind, [[52:2|and become abominable|et abominabiles facti sunt]], that is, irrational and hateful, [[52:2|in iniquities|in iniquitatibus]], or on account of their iniquities. [[52:2|There is none that doth good|Non est qui faciat bonum]] meriting eternal life among those fools, since they have not grace and charity, without which no one can merit or be acceptable to God.

paras.t: Deus de cœlo prospexit super filios hominum. Quemadmodum Deus speciali modo dicitur esse et habitare in cœlo, sic dicitur specialiter de cœlo respicere, quum tamen ipse cœlum et terram impleat, omnia penetret, et universa in se ipso conspiciat. Itaque, Deus de cœlo et sancto habitaculo suo respexit super filios hominum, id est, omnes priorum parentum filios consideravit, ut videat, id est, aliquos scire faciat, vel se scire ostendat, si est intelligens aut requirens Deum, id est, an sit aliquis de Deo recte sentiens, et intellectu formato atque fideli ipsum cognoscens, seu bene operando, et quod in se est faciendo, ipsum requirens. Hoc est quod ait Scriptura : Fortissime, magne et potens, Dominus exercituum nomen tibi, cujus oculi aperti sunt super omnes filios Adam, ut reddas unicuique secundum vias suas.
paras.en: [[52:3|God looked down from heaven on the children of men|Deus de cœlo prospexit super filios hominum]]. Just as God is said in a special way to be and to dwell in heaven, so he is said in a special way to look down from heaven, though he himself fills heaven and earth[[Jer 23:24||]], penetrates all things, and beholds all things in himself. So God, from heaven and his holy dwelling place, looked down upon the children of men, that is, he considered all the children of our first parents, [[52:3|to see|ut videat]], that is, to make some know, or to show that he knows, [[52:3|if there were any that did understand, or did seek God|si est intelligens aut requirens Deum]], that is, whether there is anyone who thinks rightly of God and knows him with a formed [that is, quickened by charity] and faithful understanding, or who seeks him by doing good and doing what lies in him. This is what Scripture says: [[Jer 32:18|O most mighty, great, and powerful, the Lord of hosts is thy name|Fortissime, magne et potens, Dominus exercituum nomen tibi]], [[Jer 32:19|whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the children of Adam, to render unto every one according to his ways|cujus oculi aperti sunt super omnes filios Adam, ut reddas unicuique secundum vias suas]] [Denis's text reads "upon all the children of Adam", without "the ways"].

paras.t: Omnes prædicti insipientes declinaverunt a recta ratione, a via justitiæ, a vero Deo : a quo declinatur seu receditur, non locali distantia, sed mentis inobedientia, juxta illud Osee : Dominum dereliquerunt in non custodiendo. Simul inutiles facti sunt, id est ad veram felicitatem inepti, et ad ultimum finem, ob quem creati sunt, inidonei. Peccata namque impediunt homines ab adeptione vitæ æternæ, et separant inter Deum et eos. Non est qui faciat bonum, id est opus Deo acceptum, ex illis insipientibus ; non est usque ad unum, id est, omnino nullus est inter eos operans bonum, quoniam omnes gratia carent.
paras.en: [[52:4|All|Omnes]] the aforesaid fools [[52:4|have gone aside|declinaverunt]] from right reason, from the way of justice, from the true God: from whom one turns aside or departs not by distance of place but by disobedience of mind, according to that word of Osee: [[Osee 4:10|they have forsaken the Lord in not observing the law|Dominum dereliquerunt in non custodiendo]] [the Latin leaves "the law" to be understood]. [[52:4|they are become unprofitable together|Simul inutiles facti sunt]], that is, unfit for true happiness, and unsuited to the last end for which they were created. For sins hinder men from attaining eternal life, and divide between God and them[[Is 59:2||]]. [[52:4|There is none that doth good|Non est qui faciat bonum]], that is, a work acceptable to God, among those fools; [[52:4|no not one|non est usque ad unum]], that is, there is no one at all among them who does good, since they all lack grace.

paras.t: Nonne scient omnes qui operantur iniquitatem ? id est, nonne peccatores Deum cognoscent ? quasi dicat : Imo, quia ad minus post hanc vitam experientur in […] in libro Sapientiæ de eis inducitur : Videntes turbabuntur timore horribili, gementes, et præ angustia spiritus dicentes, Erravimus a via veritatis, et justitiæ lumen non luxit nobis. Et sequitur : Talia dixerunt hi, qui in inferno positi sunt. Qui devorant plebem meam, id est, qui opprimunt, lædunt, aut perimunt innocentes et bonos, ut cibum panis, id est, sicut panis, qui cibus est, a manducante conteritur atque consumitur.
paras.en: [[52:5|Shall not all the workers of iniquity know|Nonne scient omnes qui operantur iniquitatem]]? that is, shall not sinners know God? As if he said: Yes indeed, for at least after this life they shall experience in […] in the book of Wisdom it is said of them: [[Wis 5:2|These seeing it, shall be troubled with terrible fear|Videntes turbabuntur timore horribili]], [[Wis 5:3|groaning|gementes]], and saying [[Wis 5:3|for anguish of spirit|præ angustia spiritus]]: [[Wis 5:6|we have erred from the way of truth, and the light of justice hath not shined unto us|Erravimus a via veritatis, et justitiæ lumen non luxit nobis]]. And it follows: [[Wis 5:14|Such things as these the sinners said in hell|Talia dixerunt hi, qui in inferno positi sunt]] [Denis's text reads "Such things said they who have been placed in hell"]. [[52:5|who eat up my people|Qui devorant plebem meam]], that is, who oppress, hurt or destroy the innocent and the good, [[52:5|as they eat bread|ut cibum panis]] [literally "as food of bread"], that is, as bread, which is food, is chewed up and consumed by him who eats it.

paras.t: Deum non invocaverunt, id est, interno affectu ejus misericordiam non imploraverunt, quia non intellexerunt, nec exquisierunt eum, nec in ipso sperabant, nec gratiam Dei sibi necessariam attendebant. Illic trepidaverunt timore, ubi non fuit timor : id est, non timenda timuerunt, et timenda non timuerunt. Deum non timuerunt, sed homines ; pœnas temporales timuerunt, non infernales ; temporalem prosperitatem, honorem, famam et gloriam timuerunt amittere, non felicitatem cœlestem : morbos atque incommoda corporis timuerunt incurrere, et labores pœnitentiales subire, viamque perfectionis arripere ; sed gratiam Dei perdere, in mortalibus vitiis vivere, Deo judici displicere, non timuerunt. Sic ergo habuerunt timorem humanum, carnalem et inordinatum, non filialem, divinum et castum.
paras.en: [[52:6|They have not called upon God|Deum non invocaverunt]], that is, they did not implore his mercy with inward affection, because they did not understand him, nor seek him, nor hope in him, nor heed the grace of God which they needed. [[52:6|there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear|Illic trepidaverunt timore, ubi non fuit timor]]: that is, they feared what is not to be feared, and did not fear what is to be feared. They did not fear God, but men; they feared temporal punishments, not those of hell; they feared to lose temporal prosperity, honour, fame and glory, not heavenly happiness; they feared to incur sickness and bodily hardship, to undergo the labours of penance, and to take up the way of perfection; but to lose the grace of God, to live in mortal vices, to displease God the judge, this they did not fear. So, then, they had a fear that was human, carnal and inordinate, not filial, divine and chaste [chaste fear: the fear of a son who dreads to offend the Father he loves, as against the servile fear that dreads only punishment].

paras.t: Cujus contrarium Christus discipulis jussit : Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum. Et rursus : Nolite, inquit, timere eos qui corpus occidunt, animam autem non possunt occidere ; sed potius timete eum, qui habet potestatem et corpus et animam perdere in gehennam ignis. Unde et in Isaia habetur : Nolite timere opprobrium hominum, et blasphemias eorum ne metuatis. Vis scire virum qui timenda timuit, et non timenda non timuit? Audi Job de se ipso testantem : Si expavi ad multitudinem nimiam, et despectio propinquorum terruit me. Ecce non timuit millia populi circumdantis se, nec ab hominibus despici horruit. Sed quem timuit? Semper, inquit, quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Deum. Et rursum ait : Deus solus est, et cogitationem ejus nemo avertere potest ; idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor. Ad quem utique sanctum timorem hortatur nos Isaias, dicens : Dominum exercituum sanctificate : ipse pavor vester, et ipse terror vester.
paras.en: The contrary of this Christ commanded his disciples: [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom.|Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum]] And again: [[Matt 10:28|fear ye not|Nolite]], he says, [[Matt 10:28|them that kill the body, and are not able to kill the soul|timere eos qui corpus occidunt, animam autem non possunt occidere]]: [[Matt 10:28|but rather fear him that can destroy both soul and body in hell|sed potius timete eum, qui habet potestatem et corpus et animam perdere in gehennam ignis]] [no reference is printed in the margin; Denis's wording, "him that hath power to destroy both body and soul in the hell of fire", mingles Matt 10:28 with Luke 12:5]. Hence also in Isaias we have: [[Is 51:7|fear ye not the reproach of men, and be not afraid of their blasphemies|Nolite timere opprobrium hominum, et blasphemias eorum ne metuatis]]. Wouldst thou know a man who feared what is to be feared, and did not fear what is not to be feared? Hear Job bearing witness of himself: [[Job 31:34|If I have been afraid at a very great multitude, and the contempt of kinsmen hath terrified me|Si expavi ad multitudinem nimiam, et despectio propinquorum terruit me]]. See, he did not fear the thousands of the people around him, nor did he shrink from being despised by men. But whom did he fear? [[Job 31:23|I have always|Semper]], he says, [[Job 31:23|feared God as waves swelling over me|quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Deum]]. And again he says: [[Job 23:13|he is alone, and no man can turn away his thought|Deus solus est, et cogitationem ejus nemo avertere potest]] [Denis reads "God alone is"]; [[Job 23:15|therefore I am troubled at his presence, and when I consider him, I am made pensive with fear|idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor]] [the margin gives Job 33:13, 15; the words are Job 23:13, 15]. It is to this holy fear that Isaias exhorts us, saying: [[Is 8:13|Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself: and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.|Dominum exercituum sanctificate : ipse pavor vester, et ipse terror vester]]

paras.t: Quoniam Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent : id est, in præsenti vita spiritualem fortitudinem, omnesque perfectiones gratum facientes abstulit eis, qui hominibus, secundum quod homines sunt atque sæculariter vivunt, placent, aut placere desiderant ; in futuro quoque judicio dissipabit ossa eorum, non comminuendo ea in frusta, sed corpus et animam projiciendo in æterna tormenta. Hujusmodi etenim homines multipliciter a via æquitatis recedunt propter humanum favorem, amorem, timorem, aut aliam similem affectionem. Unde et scriptum est : Qui timet hominem, cito corruet. Et ad Galatas Apostolus asserit : Si adhuc hominibus placerem, Christi servus non essem. Et Christus ait suis electis : Si de hoc mundo fuissetis, mundus quod suum erat diligeret ; quia vero de mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo, propterea odit vos mundus.
paras.en: [[52:6|For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men|Quoniam Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent]]: that is, in the present life he has taken away spiritual strength and all the perfections that make one pleasing [to God: *gratum facientes*, the phrase used of sanctifying grace, *gratia gratum faciens*] from those who please men, or desire to please them, as men are and as they live in a worldly way; and in the judgment to come he will also scatter their bones, not by breaking them in pieces, but by casting body and soul into eternal torments. For men of this sort depart in many ways from the way of equity on account of human favour, love, fear, or some other like affection. Hence also it is written: [[Prov 29:25|He that feareth man shall quickly fall|Qui timet hominem, cito corruet]] [the margin gives Prov. xxiv, 25; the words are Prov 29:25]. And the Apostle declares to the Galatians: [[Gal 1:10|If I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ|Si adhuc hominibus placerem, Christi servus non essem]]. And Christ says to his elect: [[John 15:19|If you had been of the world, the world would love its own: but because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you|Si de hoc mundo fuissetis, mundus quod suum erat diligeret ; quia vero de mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo, propterea odit vos mundus]].

paras.t: Sed repugnare videtur quod ait Apostolus : Sine offensione estote Ecclesiæ Dei, sicut et ego per omnia omnibus placeo, non quærens quod mihi utile est, sed quod multis ; et alibi, Si fieri potest, quod ex vobis est, cum omnibus hominibus pacem habete. De Samuele quoque et aliis nonnullis, in primo libro Regum et in Ecclesiastico Scriptura pro magno præconio introducit, quod placebant tam Deo quam hominibus.
paras.en: But what the Apostle says seems to conflict with this: [[1 Cor 10:32|Be without offence|Sine offensione estote]] [[1 Cor 10:32|to the church of God|Ecclesiæ Dei]], [[1 Cor 10:33|As I also in all things please all men, not seeking that which is profitable to myself but to many|sicut et ego per omnia omnibus placeo, non quærens quod mihi utile est, sed quod multis]]; and elsewhere: [[Rom 12:18|If it be possible, as much as is in you, have peace with all men.|Si fieri potest, quod ex vobis est, cum omnibus hominibus pacem habete]] Of Samuel too, and of some others, Scripture records in the first book of Kings and in Ecclesiasticus, as high praise, that they pleased both God and men [no reference is printed; compare 1 Kings 2:26, "pleased both the Lord and men"].

paras.t: — Et respondendum, quod de hominibus loqui possumus dupliciter. Primo, secundum id quod sunt sine caritate, fide et gratia : et sic velle hominibus placere peccatum est, maxime quoad naturam corruptam, seu rationem concupiscentiis consentientem. Et ita de hominibus loquitur Apostolus : Quum sit inter vos zelus et contentio, nonne carnales estis, et secundum hominem ambulatis? Et rursus : Quum alius dicit, Ego quidem sum Pauli, alius autem, Ego Apollo, nonne homines estis? Hoc enim modo loquendo de homine, semper inclinatur ad errores et vitia opinionesque varias. Propter quod dicit iterum Apostolus : Obsecro vos, fratres, ut id ipsum dicatis omnes, et non sint in vobis schismata. Sitis autem perfecti in eodem sensu. Secundo autem loqui possumus de hominibus, secundum quod ratio informata est lege et gratia Dei : sicque laudabile est placere hominibus in Deo et propter Deum. Unde admonet Apostolus : Unusquisque vestrum proximo suo placeat in bonum ad ædificationem. Sic quoque venerari atque timere homines, maxime præsidentes, debemus, eo quod Christus dicat : Qui vos audit, me audit ; et qui vos spernit, me spernit.
paras.en: And the answer is that we can speak of men in two ways. First, according to what they are without charity, faith and grace: and so to wish to please men is a sin, above all as regards corrupt nature, or reason consenting to concupiscences. And it is so that the Apostle speaks of men: [[1 Cor 3:3|whereas there is among you envying and contention, are you not carnal and walk you not according to man?|Quum sit inter vos zelus et contentio, nonne carnales estis, et secundum hominem ambulatis?]] And again: [[1 Cor 3:4|while one saith: I indeed am of Paul: and another: I am of Apollo: are you not men?|Quum alius dicit, Ego quidem sum Pauli, alius autem, Ego Apollo, nonne homines estis?]] For, speaking of man in this way, he is always inclined to errors and vices and differing opinions. For which reason the Apostle says again: [[1 Cor 1:10|I beseech you, brethren|Obsecro vos, fratres]], [[1 Cor 1:10|that you all speak the same thing and that there be no schisms among you: but that you be perfect in the same mind|ut id ipsum dicatis omnes, et non sint in vobis schismata. Sitis autem perfecti in eodem sensu]]. Secondly, we can speak of men according as reason is informed by the law and grace of God: and so it is praiseworthy to please men in God and for God's sake. Hence the Apostle admonishes: [[Rom 15:2|Let every one of you Please his neighbour unto good, to edification.|Unusquisque vestrum proximo suo placeat in bonum ad ædificationem]] So too we ought to reverence and fear men, especially those set over us, since Christ says: [[Luke 10:16|He that heareth you heareth me: and he that despiseth you despiseth me|Qui vos audit, me audit ; et qui vos spernit, me spernit]].

paras.t: Confusi sunt, qui hominibus inordinate placere concupiscunt, quoniam Deus sprevit eos propter eorum peccata, quemadmodum per Osee testatur : Exosos habui eos propter malitiam adinventionum ipsorum. Maxime autem confundentur in die extremi judicii, quando in æternum peribunt.
paras.en: [[52:6|They have been confounded|Confusi sunt]], who inordinately desire to please men, [[52:6|because God hath despised them|quoniam Deus sprevit eos]] for their sins, as he testifies through Osee: [[Osee 9:15|I hated them|Exosos habui eos]] [[Osee 9:15|for the wickedness of their devices|propter malitiam adinventionum ipsorum]]. But they shall be confounded above all on the day of the last judgment, when they shall perish for ever.

paras.t: Quis dabit ex Sion, id est, quis de numero electorum Deum spiritualiter speculantium tribuet, salutare Israel, id est salutem seu liberationem Ecclesiæ militantis? Nemo utique nisi Christus, qui, in quantum homo, satisfecit pro nobis, et fratrem ac socium hominum per incarnationem se fecit, sicque ad numerum electorum pertinere cognoscitur. Vel sic : Quis dabit ex Sion, id est, quis ex civitate cœlesti atque triumphanti Ecclesia, dabit salutare Israel, id est populo fideli? Nemo plane, nisi ipsemet Deus sublimis et benedictus, qui per Osee ait : Ego Dominus Deus tuus, et salvator non est præter me. De quo Isaias dicit : Hæc dicit Dominus redemptor tuus : Ego Deus tuus docens te utilia, gubernans te in via qua ambulas.
paras.en: [[52:7|Who will give out of Sion|Quis dabit ex Sion]], that is, who of the number of the elect who contemplate God spiritually will bestow [[52:7|the salvation of Israel|salutare Israel]], that is, the salvation or deliverance of the Church militant? No one indeed but Christ, who as man made satisfaction for us, and by the incarnation made himself the brother and companion of men, and so is known to belong to the number of the elect. Or thus: [[52:7|Who will give out of Sion|Quis dabit ex Sion]], that is, who out of the heavenly city and the Church triumphant will give [[52:7|the salvation of Israel|salutare Israel]], that is, to the faithful people? Plainly no one but God himself, most high and blessed, who says through Osee: [[Osee 13:4|I am the Lord thy God|Ego Dominus Deus tuus]], [[Osee 13:4|and there is no saviour beside me|et salvator non est præter me]]. Of whom Isaias says: [[Is 48:17|Thus saith the Lord thy redeemer|Hæc dicit Dominus redemptor tuus]]: [[Is 48:17|I am the Lord thy God that teach thee profitable things, that govern thee in the way that thou walkest|Ego Deus tuus docens te utilia, gubernans te in via qua ambulas]].

paras.t: Quum converterit Deus captivitatem plebis suæ, id est, dum Christus per passionem suam electos redemerit de potestate diaboli vinculisque peccati, exsultabit Jacob : id est, tunc populi vitia supplantantes, et fidem ac opera sancti Jacob sequentes, spiritualiter exsultaverunt de tantis beneficiis Christi, sicut in Actibus Apostolorum frequenter impletum narratur ; et lætabitur Israel : id est, tunc viri contemplativi hominesque perfecti, videlicet veri Israelitæ, lætati sunt, non solum qui peregrinabantur in mundo, sed etiam qui detinebantur in purgatorio et in limbo. Vel sic : Quum converterit Deus captivitatem plebis suæ, id est, dum militantem Ecclesiam de corruptione atque miseriis hujus vitæ redemerit, et ad triumphantis Ecclesiæ societatem transtulerit, quod in die novissimo fiet ; tunc exsultabit Jacob et lætabitur Israel gaudio interiori et exteriori, consummato atque perpetuo, juxta illud propheticum : Qui redempti fuerint a Domino, revertentur, et venient in Sion laudantes, et lætitia sempiterna super capita eorum, et fugiet dolor et gemitus.
paras.en: [[52:7|when God shall bring back the captivity of his people|Quum converterit Deus captivitatem plebis suæ]], that is, when Christ by his passion shall have redeemed the elect from the power of the devil and the chains of sin, [[52:7|Jacob shall rejoice|exsultabit Jacob]]: that is, then the peoples who supplant vices [an allusion to the name Jacob, "supplanter"] and follow the faith and works of holy Jacob rejoiced spiritually at such great benefits of Christ, as the Acts of the Apostles relate to have been often fulfilled[[Acts 2:1||]][[Acts 6:1||]]; [[52:7|and Israel shall be glad|et lætabitur Israel]]: that is, then contemplative and perfect men, namely the true Israelites [Israel was commonly interpreted "a man seeing God"], were glad, not only those who were pilgrims in the world, but also those who were held in purgatory and in limbo. Or thus: [[52:7|when God shall bring back the captivity of his people|Quum converterit Deus captivitatem plebis suæ]], that is, when he shall have redeemed the Church militant from the corruption and miseries of this life, and brought it over into the fellowship of the Church triumphant, which will come to pass on the last day; then [[52:7|Jacob shall rejoice|exsultabit Jacob]], [[52:7|and Israel shall be glad|et lætabitur Israel]], with a joy inward and outward, consummate and everlasting, according to that prophetic word: [[Is 35:10|the redeemed of the Lord shall return, and shall come into Sion with praise, and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads|Qui redempti fuerint a Domino, revertentur, et venient in Sion laudantes, et lætitia sempiterna super capita eorum]], [[Is 35:10|and sorrow and mourning shall flee away|et fugiet dolor et gemitus]].

52.title: EXPOSITIO ALLEGORICA EJUSDEM PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI SECUNDI, PER RELATIONEM AD CHRISTUM.
52.title_en: Allegorical exposition of the same fifty-second psalm, by reference to Christ.

paras.t: Ex declaratione denique psalmi tertiidecimi facillime patet, quomodo psalmus iste applicari possit ad Christum. Breviter ergo tangendo, sicut per filios Core, secundum præhabita, intelliguntur imitatores et filii Jesu Christi crucifixi, eo quod Core interpretetur Calvaria, quod est nomen loci in quo cruci appensus est mundi Salvator; sic per Amalec, qui interpretatur dolens sive parturiens, intelligi potest Christus, de quo scriptum est : Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, et propter nos dolens factus est; et iterum, Ipse autem vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras, attritus est propter scelera nostra. Sic ergo sensus tituli erit : In finem, pro Amalec, intellectus David : id est, intellectus psalmi præsentis in finem vitæ æternæ nos dirigentis, a David conscriptus est pro Amalec, id est pro significato interpretationis hujus nominis, Amalec, puta pro Christo.
paras.en: Finally, from the explanation of the thirteenth psalm it is very easy to see how this psalm can be applied to Christ. To touch on it briefly, then: just as by the sons of Core, according to what was said before, are understood the imitators and sons of Jesus Christ crucified, because *Core* is interpreted *Calvary*, which is the name of the place in which the Saviour of the world was hung upon the cross; so by *Amalec*, which is interpreted *grieving* or *travailing*, Christ may be understood, of whom it is written: [[Is 53:4|Surely he hath borne our infirmities|Vere languores nostros ipse tulit]], and for our sake he became one grieving [Denis's wording; the Vulgate has "and carried our sorrows"]; and again: [[Is 53:5|But he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our sins|Ipse autem vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras, attritus est propter scelera nostra]]. So then the sense of the title will be: [[52:1|Unto the end|In finem]], for Amalec, [[52:1|understandings to David|intellectus David]] [Denis reads *pro Amalec*, "for Amalec", where the Vulgate has *pro Maeleth*, the Douay-Rheims "for Maeleth"; and he has *intellectus*, "the understanding", in the singular]: that is, the understanding of the present psalm, which directs us unto the end of life everlasting, was written by David for Amalec, that is, for what the interpretation of this name Amalec signifies, namely for Christ.

paras.t: Ait itaque : Dixit insipiens, id est populus Judæorum, Christum, Dei Sapientiam incarnatam, ac inter se conversantem irridens, spernens ac persequens ; in corde suo : Non est Deus, id est, iste Jesus Nazarenus similis nobis passibilis, non est Deus, nec Dei Unigenitus, sed seductor atque blasphemus. Unde Christus ostendit cæcitatem et insipientiam Judæorum, in ipsum credere contemnentium : In parabolis, inquit, loquor eis, quia videntes non vident, et audientes non audiunt, neque intelligunt, ut impleatur in eis prophetia Isaiæ, dicentis : Auditu audietis, et non intelligetis ; et videntes videbitis, et non perspicietis. Incrassatum est enim cor populi hujus. Quæ verba, quantum ad sensum, in libro visionum Isaiæ habentur. Insuper, quum dixissent Pharisæi ad Jesum, Magister, volumus a te signum videre ; increpat eos, quod tempus sui adventus non adverterunt ex Prophetarum scripturis, præsertim ex vaticinio Danielis, qui in libro visionum suarum tempus adventus passionisque Christi evidentissime declaravit, dum ait : Post hebdomadas sexaginta duas occidetur Christus. Et loquitur de hebdomadibus annorum, non dierum, ita quod una hebdomada continet septem annos. Sic igitur Christus Pharisæis respondit : Faciem cœli judicare nostis ; nam facto vespere, dicitis, Serenum erit, rubicundum est enim cœlum ; signa autem temporum non potestis ?
paras.en: He says therefore: [[52:1|The fool said|Dixit insipiens]], that is, the people of the Jews, mocking, spurning and persecuting Christ, the Wisdom of God incarnate, as he went about among them; [[52:1|in his heart: There is no God|in corde suo : Non est Deus]], that is: This Jesus of Nazareth, like us and able to suffer, is not God, nor the Only-begotten of God, but a seducer and a blasphemer. Hence Christ shows the blindness and folly of the Jews who scorned to believe in him: [[Matt 13:13|in parables|In parabolis]], he says, [[Matt 13:13|do I speak to them|loquor eis]]: [[Matt 13:13|because seeing they see not, and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand|quia videntes non vident, et audientes non audiunt, neque intelligunt]], that [[Matt 13:14|the prophecy of Isaias is fulfilled in them, who saith: By hearing you shall hear, and shall not understand: and seeing you shall see, and shall not perceive|impleatur in eis prophetia Isaiæ, dicentis : Auditu audietis, et non intelligetis ; et videntes videbitis, et non perspicietis]]. [[Matt 13:15|For the heart of this people is grown gross|Incrassatum est enim cor populi hujus]]. Which words, as to their sense, are found in the book of the visions of Isaias[[Is 6:9||]][[Is 6:10||]]. Moreover, when the Pharisees had said to Jesus: [[Matt 12:38|Master, we would see a sign from thee|Magister, volumus a te signum videre]][[Matt 16:1||]], he rebukes them because they had not marked the time of his coming from the writings of the Prophets, and above all from the prophecy of Daniel, who in the book of his visions declared most plainly the time of the coming and passion of Christ, when he says: [[Dan 9:26|after sixty-two weeks Christ shall be slain|Post hebdomadas sexaginta duas occidetur Christus]]. And he speaks of weeks of years, not of days, so that one week contains seven years. So then Christ answered the Pharisees: [[Matt 16:3|You know then how to discern the face of the sky|Faciem cœli judicare nostis]] [the margin gives Matt. xvi, 4: these words stand in verse 4 in the Vulgate, in verse 3 in the Douay-Rheims]; for [[Matt 16:2|When it is evening, you say, It will be fair weather, for the sky is red|facto vespere, dicitis, Serenum erit, rubicundum est enim cœlum]]; [[Matt 16:3|can you not know the signs of the times|signa autem temporum non potestis]]?

paras.t: Deinde Propheta hunc populum insipientem pluraliter exprimit, dicens : Corrupti sunt, id est ab omni gratia destituti, et etiam a Romanis corporaliter interfecti ; et abominabiles facti sunt, id est Deo atque hominibus odibiles, sicut de eis ait Apostolus : Deo non placent, et omnibus hominibus adversantur. Et hoc, in iniquitatibus suis, id est propter peccata quibus Christum persecuti sunt, eumque coram Pilato negaverunt et occiderunt, sicut de eis apud Jeremiam Christus testatur : Facta est mihi hereditas mea quasi leo in silva ; dedit contra me vocem suam, ideo odivi eam. Et rursus de incredulis Judæis Jeremias prædixit : Negaverunt Dominum, et dixerunt : Non est ipse. Unde in Osee Christus apertissime ait : Recesserunt a me, et ego erudivi eos, et roboravi brachia eorum, et in me cogitaverunt malitiam. Reversi sunt ut essent absque jugo, et ego redemi eos, et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia. Non est qui faciat bonum meritorium, ex illis insipientibus et perversis Judæis. Propter quod Christus in Evangelio ait ad eos : In peccato vestro moriemini; et iterum, Vos ex patre diabolo estis ; rursumque, Quomodo potestis bona loqui, quum sitis mali ?
