paras.en: Then the Prophet speaks of this foolish people in the plural, saying: [[52:2|They are corrupted|Corrupti sunt]], that is, stripped of all grace, and also slain in the body by the Romans; [[52:2|and become abominable|et abominabiles facti sunt]], that is, hateful to God and to men, as the Apostle says of them: [[1 Thess 2:15|please not God, and are adversaries to all men|Deo non placent, et omnibus hominibus adversantur]]. And this [[52:2|in iniquities|in iniquitatibus]] of theirs, that is, because of the sins by which they persecuted Christ, and denied him before Pilate and slew him[[Acts 3:13||]]; as Christ testifies of them in Jeremias: [[Jer 12:8|My inheritance is become to me as a lion in the wood: it hath cried out against me, therefore have I hated it|Facta est mihi hereditas mea quasi leo in silva ; dedit contra me vocem suam, ideo odivi eam]]. And again Jeremias foretold of the unbelieving Jews: [[Jer 5:12|They have denied the Lord, and said, It is not he|Negaverunt Dominum, et dixerunt : Non est ipse]]. Hence in Osee Christ says most openly: [[Osee 7:13|they have departed from me|Recesserunt a me]], [[Osee 7:15|And I have chastised them, and strengthened their arms: and they have imagined evil against me|et ego erudivi eos, et roboravi brachia eorum, et in me cogitaverunt malitiam]]. [[Osee 7:16|They returned, that they might be without yoke|Reversi sunt ut essent absque jugo]], [[Osee 7:13|and I redeemed them: and they have spoken lies against me|et ego redemi eos, et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia]] [Denis joins words of Osee 7:13, 15 and 16 in his own order; where he has *erudivi*, the Douay-Rheims reads "chastised"]. [[52:2|There is none that doth good|Non est qui faciat bonum]] (good that merits a reward) among those foolish and perverse Jews. For this reason Christ says to them in the Gospel: [[John 8:24|you shall die in your sin|In peccato vestro moriemini]]; and again: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]]; and once more: [[Matt 12:34|how can you speak good things, whereas you are evil?|Quomodo potestis bona loqui, quum sitis mali]]

paras.t: Deus de cœlo, id est Verbum Dei, veritas, atque sapientia Patris, de humanitate assumpta, in qua tanquam in cœlo purissimo habitavit, prospexit super filios hominum, id est specialiter super Judæos, primo prædicans eis regnum cœleste, sicut et Christus in Evangelio fatetur : Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel. Ut videat si est intelligens aut requirens Deum Patrem, et Filium ejus unicum Jesum Christum. Ideo enim Christus venit in mundum, ut Deum requirentes salvaret, et approbando cognosceret.
paras.en: [[52:3|God|Deus]] [[52:3|from heaven|de cœlo]], that is, the Word of God, the truth and wisdom of the Father, from the humanity he assumed, in which he dwelt as in a most pure heaven, [[52:3|looked down|prospexit]] [[52:3|on the children of men|super filios hominum]], that is, especially upon the Jews, preaching to them first the kingdom of heaven, as Christ too confesses in the Gospel: [[Matt 15:24|I was not sent but to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel]]. [[52:3|to see if there were any that did understand, or did seek God|Ut videat si est intelligens aut requirens Deum]] the Father, and his only Son Jesus Christ. For Christ came into the world for this, to save those who seek God, and to know them with approval [that is, with the knowledge by which God owns the just as his].

paras.t: Omnes prædicti increduli, declinaverunt a Christi doctrina et fide catholica, sicut de eis Dominus per Jeremiam ait : Verterunt ad me dorsum et non faciem.
paras.en: [[52:4|All|Omnes]] the aforesaid unbelievers [[52:4|have gone aside|declinaverunt]] from the doctrine of Christ and from the Catholic faith, as the Lord says of them by Jeremias: [[Jer 2:27|they have turned their back to me, and not their face|Verterunt ad me dorsum et non faciem]].

paras.t: Nonne scient omnes qui operantur iniquitatem ? id est, nonne prædicti infideles Judæi tandem cognoscent me esse verum Messiam ? quasi dicat, Imo cognoscent, quia in die judicii videbunt me in quem transfixerunt : quemadmodum per Zachariam dictum est. Et in Apocalypsi ait Joannes : Ecce venit cum nubibus, et videbit eum omnis oculus, et qui eum pupugerunt. Qui devorant plebem meam, id est, qui oppresserunt, tribulaverunt, et partim interfecerunt, partimque de suis finibus ejecerunt primitivam Ecclesiam in Jerusalem primo collectam, quemadmodum in Actibus Lucas inducit : Facta est, inquit, in die illa (quando videlicet Stephanum occiderunt) persecutio magna in Ecclesia quæ erat in Jerusalem, et dispersi sunt omnes præter Apostolos.
paras.en: [[52:5|Shall not all the workers of iniquity know|Nonne scient omnes qui operantur iniquitatem]]? that is, shall not the aforesaid unbelieving Jews know at length that I am the true Messias? As if to say: Yes, they shall know, for on the day of judgement [[Zach 12:10|they shall look upon me, whom they have pierced|videbunt me in quem transfixerunt]], as was said by Zacharias [Denis's wording, *videbunt … transfixerunt*, differs slightly from the Vulgate's *aspicient … confixerunt*]. And in the Apocalypse John says: [[Apoc 1:7|Behold, he cometh with the clouds, and every eye shall see him: and they also that pierced him|Ecce venit cum nubibus, et videbit eum omnis oculus, et qui eum pupugerunt]]. [[52:5|Who eat up my people|Qui devorant plebem meam]], that is, who oppressed and troubled the primitive Church first gathered in Jerusalem, and partly slew it and partly drove it out of their borders, as Luke relates in the Acts: [[Acts 8:1|there was raised|Facta est]], he says, [[Acts 8:1|at that time|in die illa]] (namely when they slew Stephen) [[Acts 8:1|a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem|persecutio magna in Ecclesia quæ erat in Jerusalem]], and [[Acts 8:1|they were all dispersed|dispersi sunt omnes]] [[Acts 8:1|except the apostles|præter Apostolos]].

paras.t: Deum non invocaverunt isti increduli, quia nec eum veraciter agnoverunt, sicut Christus ait ad eos : Neque me scitis, neque Patrem meum. Et si Deum labiis conclamabant, cor tamen eorum longe erat ab eo ; et ideo non invocaverunt illum. Illic trepidaverunt timore, ubi non fuit timor. Timebant enim adventum Romanorum, nisi Christum occiderent, sicut dicebant : Ne forte veniant Romani, et tollant locum nostrum et gentem. Sicque magis formidabant homines et temporalia damna, quam Deum et spiritualia detrimenta.
paras.en: These unbelievers [[52:6|have not called upon God|Deum non invocaverunt]], because they did not truly know him either, as Christ says to them: [[John 8:19|Neither me do you know, nor my Father|Neque me scitis, neque Patrem meum]]. And though they cried out to God with their lips, yet their heart was far from him[[Is 29:13||]]; and therefore they did not call upon him. [[52:6|there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear|Illic trepidaverunt timore, ubi non fuit timor]]. For they feared the coming of the Romans unless they slew Christ, as they said: Lest perhaps [[John 11:48|the Romans will come, and take away our place and nation|veniant Romani, et tollant locum nostrum et gentem]]. And so they dreaded men and temporal losses more than God and spiritual harm.

paras.t: Quoniam Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent, id est prædictorum infidelium Judæorum, vel qui Romanis displicere timentes, vel principibus sacerdotum placere optantes, mortem Christi procuraverunt : horum ossa Christus dissipavit, et dissipabit, secundum sensum in præcedenti expositione inductum. Nam Christus ait ad eos : Quomodo potestis vos credere, qui gloriam ab invicem accipitis, et gloriam quæ a solo Deo est non quæritis? Confusi sunt, tempore Titi et Vespasiani, et quotidie a fidelibus confunduntur ; tandemque a Christo æternaliter confundentur, quando implebitur quod Christus eis prædixit : Amodo videbitis Filium hominis sedentem a dextris virtutis Dei, et venientem in nubibus cœli. Sic ergo confusi sunt, quoniam Deus sprevit eos. Propterea informari convertique nequeunt, sed incorrigibiles sunt, ut verificetur in eis quod Salomon asserit : Considera opera Dei, quod nemo possit corrigere quem ille despexerit. Cetera ex præcedenti expositione clara sunt.
paras.en: [[52:6|For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men|Quoniam Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent]], that is, of the aforesaid unbelieving Jews, who, either fearing to displease the Romans or wishing to please the chief priests, brought about the death of Christ: the bones of these Christ has scattered and will scatter, according to the sense set out in the preceding exposition. For Christ says to them: [[John 5:44|How can you believe, who receive glory one from another: and the glory which is from God alone, you do not seek?|Quomodo potestis vos credere, qui gloriam ab invicem accipitis, et gloriam quæ a solo Deo est non quæritis?]] [[52:6|They have been confounded|Confusi sunt]] in the time of Titus and Vespasian, and they are confounded daily by the faithful; and at last they will be confounded eternally by Christ, when that is fulfilled which Christ foretold to them: [[Matt 26:64|hereafter you shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of the power of God and coming in the clouds of heaven|Amodo videbitis Filium hominis sedentem a dextris virtutis Dei, et venientem in nubibus cœli]]. So then [[52:6|they have been confounded|confusi sunt]], [[52:6|because God hath despised them|quoniam Deus sprevit eos]]. Therefore they cannot be reformed and converted, but are incorrigible, so that there is verified in them what Solomon declares: [[Eccles 7:14|Consider the works of God, that no man can correct whom he hath despised|Considera opera Dei, quod nemo possit corrigere quem ille despexerit]]. The rest is clear from the preceding exposition.

paras.t: Ecce quam multa salubria documenta ex psalmo præsenti elici valent, videlicet ne Deum quem ore confitemur, factis negemus ; Deumque omnia considerantem cogitemus, veneremur, et diligamus ; futurum judicium formidemus, impiorum tormenta vereamur : et super omnia versum illum diligentissime recolamus, quo dictum est, Quoniam Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent ; quatenus soli Deo placere quæramus, eique soli displicere vitemus, ne simus de numero eorum de quibus scriptum est : Dilexerunt gloriam hominum magis quam gloriam Dei.
paras.en: See how many wholesome lessons can be drawn from the present psalm: namely, that we should not deny by our deeds the God whom we confess with our mouth; that we should think of God, who considers all things, and revere and love him; that we should dread the judgement to come, and stand in awe of the torments of the wicked; and above all that we should most diligently call to mind that verse in which it is said: [[52:6|For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men|Quoniam Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent]]; so that we may seek to please God alone, and shun displeasing him alone, lest we be of the number of those of whom it is written: [[John 12:43|they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God|Dilexerunt gloriam hominum magis quam gloriam Dei]].

paras.t: PRECATIO. Propriis vitiis inutiles factos, Deus, de cœlo propitius prospice super nos ; suscita in nobis gratiam tuam : qua illustrati, non nobis ipsis, sed tibi placere studeamus.
paras.en: Prayer. Upon us, who by our own vices [[52:4|are become unprofitable|inutiles factos]], look down from heaven in thy mercy, O God; stir up in us thy grace, that, enlightened by it, we may strive to please not ourselves but thee.

53.title: EXPOSITIO DE CHRISTO PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI TERTII : DEUS, IN NOMINE TUO SALVUM ME FAC.
53.title_en: Exposition of the fifty-third psalm, of Christ: Save me, O God, by thy name.

paras.t: Ardens amator satiari non valet audiendo, loquendo et cogitando de eo quem diligit : idcirco devoti Christicolæ, qui omnia arbitrantur cum Apostolo ut stercora, propter eminentem scientiam Christi, atque ut Christum lucrifaciant, in expositione illa præcipue epulantur, qua dicta Prophetarum et legis ac Psalmorum, de Christo elucidantur. Ipse enim est finis legis, et omnium salus : et sicut Judæorum quoque magistri fatentur, omnes Prophetæ non sunt locuti nisi super dies Messiæ. Unde, secundum Augustinum, libri Prophetarum, nisi in eis Christus intelligatur, aqua sunt, et sine sapore ac fructu. Si vero in eis Christus intelligatur, vinum sunt, et reficiunt atque inebriant. Denique, licet tituli psalmorum frequenter ex historia quæ contigit David, videantur accepti, ex hoc non sequitur quod psalmi tales de David sint exponendi ad litteram, quanquam interdum littera ad hoc valeat applicari. Per hujusmodi etenim titulos datur intelligi, quæ fuerit occasio sancto David psalmos sic intitulatos scribendi. Sed quoniam David prophetico spiritu plenus fuit, et Christi mysteria excellenter agnovit, seque Christi figuram gerere scivit : imo, quoniam totum statum veteris Testamenti cognovit esse figuram status novi Testamenti seu legis Christi et gratiæ, sciens procul dubio quod omnia in figura contingebant eis, (alioqui, quomodo Prophetarum fuisset eximius ?) propterea certissime credendum est, quod sanctus David oculum cordis sui semper ad Christum et statum Ecclesiæ, secundum illuminationem sibi a Spiritu Sancto factam, convertit. Et quanquam in psalmis de se ipso aliquid recitare videatur, principalis tamen sua intentio erat, de Christo et ejus mysteriis atque Ecclesia loqui, juxta quod ipsemet innuit : Dixit (inquiens) David filius Isai, dixit vir cui constitutum est de Christo Dei Jacob : Spiritus Domini locutus est per me.
paras.en: An ardent lover cannot have his fill of hearing, speaking and thinking of the one he loves. Therefore devout worshippers of Christ, who with the Apostle count all things as dung for the excellent knowledge of Christ, that they may gain Christ[[Phil 3:8||]], feast above all on that exposition in which the sayings of the Prophets, of the Law and of the Psalms are made clear concerning Christ. For he is the end of the law, and the salvation of all; and, as even the masters of the Jews admit, all the Prophets spoke only of the days of the Messias. Hence, according to Augustine, the books of the Prophets, unless Christ is understood in them, are water, without savour or fruit; but if Christ is understood in them, they are wine, and they refresh and inebriate. Lastly, although the titles of the psalms often seem to be taken from something that happened to David, it does not follow that such psalms are to be expounded literally of David, though at times the letter can be applied to this. For by titles of this kind we are given to understand what was the occasion for holy David to write the psalms so entitled. But since David was full of the prophetic spirit, and knew the mysteries of Christ excellently, and knew that he bore the figure of Christ; nay more, since he knew that the whole state of the Old Testament was a figure of the state of the New Testament, that is, of the law of Christ and of grace, knowing beyond doubt that [[1 Cor 10:11|all these things happened to them in figure|omnia in figura contingebant eis]] (otherwise, how would he have been the foremost of the Prophets?), it is therefore most certainly to be believed that holy David always turned the eye of his heart to Christ and to the state of the Church, according to the light given him by the Holy Ghost. And though in the psalms he seems to tell something of himself, yet his chief intention was to speak of Christ and his mysteries and of the Church, as he himself hints, saying: [[2 Kings 23:1|David the son of Isai said|David filius Isai]]; [[2 Kings 23:1|The man to whom it was appointed concerning the Christ of the God of Jacob|vir cui constitutum est de Christo Dei Jacob]] said: [[2 Kings 23:2|The spirit of the Lord hath spoken by me|Spiritus Domini locutus est per me]].

paras.t: Insuper, si David in psalmis tam sæpe de se ipso, et non potius de Christo et Ecclesia loqueretur, ut aliqui somniant, qui hunc librum Psalmorum nimis superficialiter exponunt, pro magna parte exponentes ipsos psalmos ad litteram de David ; tunc psalmi tales non pertinerent ad dicta prophetica, sed ad sermones historicos. Videretur enim David non de futuro vaticinari, sed de præterito historiam texere : sicque satis parum prophetaret David de Christo. Imo, si subtiliter consideretur, inveniretur Isaias multo copiosius describere mysteria Christi et Ecclesiæ, quam David propheta : quod tamen nemo concedit.—Amplius, gratia prophetalis spectat ad gratias gratis datas : nam bonis et malis communis est. Gratiæ autem gratis datæ ordinantur ad aliorum utilitatem, juxta illud Apostoli : Unicuique datur manifestatio Spiritus ad utilitatem. Itaque Spiritus Sanctus, qui David tantam prophetalis notitiæ gratiam contulit, ad hoc eam ipsi donavit, ut tota Ecclesia informationem de Christo hauriret.
paras.en: Moreover, if David in the psalms spoke so often of himself, and not rather of Christ and the Church, as some dream who expound this book of Psalms too superficially, expounding the psalms themselves for the most part literally of David, then such psalms would not belong to prophetic sayings but to historical discourses. For David would seem not to prophesy of the future but to weave a history of the past; and so David would prophesy very little of Christ. Nay, if the matter were closely considered, Isaias would be found to describe the mysteries of Christ and the Church far more copiously than the prophet David: which nevertheless no one grants. Further, the grace of prophecy belongs to the graces freely given [gratiae gratis datae: gifts given for the good of others, not to make the one who receives them holy], for it is common to the good and the wicked. And graces freely given are ordained for the profit of others, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 12:7|the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man unto profit|Unicuique datur manifestatio Spiritus ad utilitatem]]. Therefore the Holy Ghost, who conferred on David so great a grace of prophetic knowledge, gave it to him for this, that the whole Church might draw from it instruction about Christ.

paras.t: Hæc propterea dico, ut sciatur quam inepta sint eorum commenta, qui in dictis Prophetarum et psalmis adeo superficiales ac litterales exsistunt, et ut semper conemur, quantum fieri potest, ipsos psalmos de Christo et corpore ejus mystico, quod est Ecclesia, explanare.
paras.en: I say these things so that it may be known how inept are the commentaries of those who are so superficial and literal in the sayings of the Prophets and in the psalms, and so that we may always strive, as far as can be, to explain the psalms themselves of Christ and of his mystical body, which is the Church.

paras.t: Quamvis itaque ex tenore tituli hujus psalmi videatur psalmus de David intelligendus, non tamen agit psalmus de historia tituli, sed de mysterio significato per illud quod contigit. Nihilo minus psalmus iste exponi posset de David, sicut et de unoquoque fideli moraliter intelligi potest : quæ expositio in sequenti explanatione elucebit.
paras.en: Although, then, from the tenor of the title of this psalm, the psalm seems to be understood of David, yet the psalm does not treat of the history in the title, but of the mystery signified by what happened. Nonetheless this psalm could be expounded of David, as it can also be understood morally of each one of the faithful: and that exposition will appear in the explanation that follows.

paras.t: Nunc vero de Christo exponendus est psalmus, qui talem titulum habet : In finem, in carminibus, intellectus David, quum venissent Ziphæi, et nuntiassent Sauli : Nonne David absconditus est apud nos ? Titulus iste ex historia primi libri Regum acceptus est. Legitur enim ibidem quemadmodum David cum suis a facie Saul fugiens, apud Ziphæos se abscondit. Ziphæi vero, quamvis essent de tribu Juda, sicut et David, tamen regi suo placere volentes, prodiderunt ipsum David. Dicuntur enim Ziphæi a Ziph, viculo ad sortem tribus Juda pertinente. Audiens autem David se proditum a Ziphæis, psalmum hunc edidit, liberari desiderans a tanto periculo. Ziphæi, qui interpretantur florentes, designant Judæos temporali prosperitate gaudentes ; David autem significat Christum ; Saul, Pilatum. Ziphæi ergo, id est Judæi, nuntiaverunt Sauli, id est Pilato : Nonne David absconditus est apud nos ? id est, nonne Jesum invenimus populum seducentem, et eum jam apud nos tenemus ligatum ? Est itaque tituli sensus : Intellectus David, id est sensus hujus psalmi Christo conveniens, et in æternam vitam nos dirigens, in carminibus, id est, ita quod semper Domino gratias referamus tam in adversis quam prosperis : intellectus, inquam, conscriptus et habitus pro eo, quum venissent Ziphæi, id est Judæi increduli, et nuntiassent Sauli, id est Pilato : Nonne David absconditus est apud nos ? id est, nonne Jesum hunc cepimus, et ligatum tibi adducimus ?
paras.en: But now the psalm is to be expounded of Christ; it has this title: [[53:1|Unto the end, in verses, understanding for David|In finem, in carminibus, intellectus David]], [[53:2|When the men of Ziph had come and said to Saul: Is not David hidden with us?|quum venissent Ziphæi, et nuntiassent Sauli : Nonne David absconditus est apud nos]] This title is taken from the history of the first book of Kings. For we read there how David with his men, fleeing from the face of Saul, hid among the Ziphites[[1 Kings 23:19||]][[1 Kings 26:1||]] [the margin gives 1 Kings 23:13–20 and 26:1]. And the Ziphites, though they were of the tribe of Juda, as David was, yet wishing to please their king, betrayed David. For they are called Ziphites from Ziph, a small town belonging to the lot of the tribe of Juda. When David heard that he had been betrayed by the Ziphites, he composed this psalm, desiring to be delivered from so great a peril. The Ziphites, whose name is interpreted *flourishing*, stand for the Jews rejoicing in temporal prosperity; David signifies Christ; Saul, Pilate. The Ziphites, then, that is, the Jews, told Saul, that is, Pilate: [[53:2|Is not David hidden with us?|Nonne David absconditus est apud nos]] that is, have we not found Jesus seducing the people, and do we not now hold him bound here with us?[[Luke 23:1||]][[Luke 23:2||]] The sense of the title, then, is this: [[53:1|understanding for David|Intellectus David]], that is, the sense of this psalm that fits Christ and directs us to eternal life; [[53:1|in verses|in carminibus]], that is, so that we may always give thanks to the Lord, in adversity as in prosperity: an understanding, I say, written and held for this, [[53:2|When the men of Ziph had come|quum venissent Ziphæi]], that is, the unbelieving Jews, [[53:2|and said to Saul|et nuntiassent Sauli]], that is, to Pilate: [[53:2|Is not David hidden with us?|Nonne David absconditus est apud nos]] that is, have we not taken this Jesus, and do we not bring him bound to thee?

paras.t: Propheta ergo in Christi persona loquens, seu Christus secundum quod homo et aliquo modo viator, et passioni jam proximus, ait ad Deum Patrem seu totam supergloriosissimam Trinitatem : Deus, in nomine tuo salvum me fac : id est, in te ipso omnium summo ac vero salvatore, et ad gloriam nominis tui, a morte resuscita me, et in ipsa passione conserva atque conforta me contra naturalem horrorem seu timorem mortis instantis. Unde et in Luca habetur : Apparuit illi angelus de cœlo confortans eum. Et in virtute tua judica me : id est, secundum justitiam tuam restitue mihi Filio tuo dilecto, separando et liberando me a generatione hac pessima, mihi non credente, meque atrociter persequente. Hoc enim Christus se desiderasse insinuat, dum ait : O generatio incredula, quamdiu apud vos ero ? quamdiu patiar vos ?
paras.en: The Prophet, then, speaking in the person of Christ, or Christ as man and in a manner a wayfarer [viator: one still on the way, not yet at the end, as Christ was in his mortal flesh], and now close to his passion, says to God the Father, or to the whole most supremely glorious Trinity: [[53:3|Save me, O God, by thy name|Deus, in nomine tuo salvum me fac]]: that is, in thyself, the highest and true Saviour of all, and for the glory of thy name, raise me from death, and in the passion itself keep and strengthen me against the natural horror or fear of the death at hand. Hence it is said in Luke too: [[Luke 22:43|there appeared to him an angel from heaven, strengthening him|Apparuit illi angelus de cœlo confortans eum]]. [[53:3|And judge me in thy strength|Et in virtute tua judica me]]: that is, according to thy justice give me, thy beloved Son, my due, separating and delivering me from this most wicked generation, which does not believe me and cruelly persecutes me. For Christ hints that he desired this when he says: [[Mark 9:18|O incredulous generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I suffer you?|O generatio incredula, quamdiu apud vos ero ? quamdiu patiar vos]] [the margin gives Mark ix, 48].

paras.t: Deus, exaudi orationem meam, qua oro pro corpore meo mystico, scilicet pro Ecclesia electorum, ut fructum passionis meæ participent. Hoc namque oravit Christus, dicens : Non pro mundo rogo, sed pro eis quos dedisti mihi. Et iterum : Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo, quos dedisti mihi, ut sint unum sicut et nos. Auribus percipe verba oris mei. Aures Dei, sunt sapientia qua cuncta cognoscit, et misericordia qua orantibus subvenit. Itaque, Domine Pater, auribus percipe verba oris mei, quæ pro me ipso, videlicet pro corporis mei glorificatione ascensioneque deprecor : Clarifica me tu, Pater, apud temetipsum, claritate quam habui priusquam mundus fieret. Et alibi Christus precatur : Tu scis, Domine, recordare mei, et visita me, et tuere me ab his qui persequuntur me.
paras.en: [[53:4|O God, hear my prayer|Deus, exaudi orationem meam]], by which I pray for my mystical body, namely for the Church of the elect, that they may share in the fruit of my passion. For Christ prayed this, saying: [[John 17:9|I pray not for the world, but for them whom thou hast given me|Non pro mundo rogo, sed pro eis quos dedisti mihi]]. And again: [[John 17:11|Holy Father, keep them in thy name whom thou hast given me: that they may be one, as we also are|Pater sancte, serva eos in nomine tuo, quos dedisti mihi, ut sint unum sicut et nos]]. [[53:4|Give ear to the words of my mouth|Auribus percipe verba oris mei]]. The ears of God are the wisdom by which he knows all things, and the mercy by which he comes to the help of those who pray. Therefore, Lord Father, [[53:4|give ear to the words of my mouth|auribus percipe verba oris mei]], which I pray for myself, namely for the glorifying and the ascension of my body: [[John 17:5|glorify thou me, O Father, with thyself, with the glory which I had, before the world was|Clarifica me tu, Pater, apud temetipsum, claritate quam habui priusquam mundus fieret]]. And elsewhere Christ prays: [[Jer 15:15|O Lord, thou knowest, remember me, and visit me, and defend me from them that persecute me|Tu scis, Domine, recordare mei, et visita me, et tuere me ab his qui persequuntur me]].

paras.t: Quoniam alieni insurrexerunt adversum me : id est, infideles Judæi, alieni a me non carnis propagine, sed vitæ imitatione ; non natura, sed gratiæ carentia, persecuti sunt me : prout Joannes ait, Cohors ergo, et tribunus, et ministri Judæorum accesserunt, et injecerunt manus in Jesum. Idcirco, per alienos intelligi possunt gentiles, qui procurantibus Judæis Christum interfecerunt. Et fortes quæsierunt animam meam : id est, principes sacerdotum quæsierunt animam meam, id est corporalem vitam meam, exstinguere : sicut Sapiens ex persona eorum asserit, Morte turpissima condemnemus eum. Et non proposuerunt Deum ante conspectum suum : id est, Deum non timuerunt committentes tantum peccatum, sed homines, quia dixerunt : Ne forte veniant Romani, et tollant locum nostrum et gentem. Nam et Pilatus, quum ei dixissent Judæi, Si hunc dimittis, non es amicus Cæsaris, statim adjudicavit fieri petitiones eorum.
paras.en: [[53:5|For strangers have risen up against me|Quoniam alieni insurrexerunt adversum me]]: that is, the unbelieving Jews, strangers to me not by descent of the flesh but in the imitation of my life, not by nature but by want of grace, persecuted me; as John says, [[John 18:12|Then the band and the tribune and the servants of the Jews|Cohors ergo, et tribunus, et ministri Judæorum]] [[Matt 26:50|came up and laid hands on Jesus|accesserunt, et injecerunt manus in Jesum]] [Denis joins to the words of John 18:12 those of Matt 26:50]. Hence also by *strangers* may be understood the gentiles, who at the instance of the Jews put Christ to death. [[53:5|And the mighty have sought after my soul|Et fortes quæsierunt animam meam]]: that is, the chief priests [[53:5|have sought after my soul|quæsierunt animam meam]], that is, my bodily life, to put it out; as the Wise Man says in their person, [[Wis 2:20|Let us condemn him to a most shameful death|Morte turpissima condemnemus eum]]. [[53:5|And they have not set God before their eyes|Et non proposuerunt Deum ante conspectum suum]]: that is, they did not fear God in committing so great a sin, but men, for they said: [[John 11:48|the Romans will come, and take away our place and nation|Ne forte veniant Romani, et tollant locum nostrum et gentem]] [the margin gives John vi, 48]. For Pilate too, when the Jews had said to him, [[John 19:12|If thou release this man, thou art not Caesar's friend|Si hunc dimittis, non es amicus Cæsaris]], at once gave sentence that their petitions should be granted.

paras.t: Consequenter declarat Christus se exauditum, illosque nihil proficere. Ecce enim Deus adjuvat me : quia divinitas Christi in omnibus cooperabatur humanitati assumptæ, eamque in omnibus confortavit atque protexit, juxta illud Jeremiæ : Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis ; idcirco qui me persequuntur, cadent et infirmi erunt. Et Salvator ait : Solus non sum ; sed ego, et qui misit me, Pater. Et Dominus, id est Deus Trinitas, susceptor est animæ meæ, id est exauditor orationum ipsius ; vel, Dominus susceptor est animæ meæ, id est, Verbum seu Filius Dei, verus Deus, ad suam divinam personalitatem animam meam assumpsit, nec eam in triduo mortis reliquit. Quamvis enim tempore mortis et sepulturæ Christi, separata fuerit anima ejus a corpore, utrumque tamen Verbo mansit unitum. Et hoc est quod apud Isaiam prophetam Deus ait de Christo homine : Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum ; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea.
paras.en: Next Christ declares that he has been heard, and that they gain nothing. [[53:6|For behold God is my helper|Ecce enim Deus adjuvat me]]: for the divinity of Christ worked together in all things with the humanity it had taken, and strengthened and protected it in all things, according to that saying of Jeremias: [[Jer 20:11|the Lord is with me as a strong warrior: therefore they that persecute me shall fall, and shall be weak|Dominus mecum est quasi bellator fortis ; idcirco qui me persequuntur, cadent et infirmi erunt]]. And the Saviour says: [[John 8:16|I am not alone, but I and the Father that sent me|Solus non sum ; sed ego, et qui misit me, Pater]]. [[53:6|And the Lord|Et Dominus]], that is, God the Trinity, [[53:6|is the protector of my soul|susceptor est animæ meæ]], that is, the hearer of its prayers; or, [[53:6|the Lord is the protector of my soul|Dominus susceptor est animæ meæ]] [susceptor, "protector", is literally "one who takes up"; hence this second reading], that is, the Word or Son of God, true God, took up my soul into his own divine personality, and did not leave it in the three days of death. For although at the time of Christ's death and burial his soul was separated from his body, both nonetheless remained united to the Word. And this is what God says of Christ as man in the prophet Isaias: [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant, I will uphold him: my elect, my soul delighteth in him|Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum ; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea]] [suscipiam, "I will uphold", is the verb from which susceptor comes].

paras.t: Averte mala inimicis meis : id est, mala et pœnas mihi a Judæis paratas, retorque in caput eorum, et libera me, ita ut laqueus quem mihi paraverunt, eos concludat : prout in Ecclesiaste scriptum est : Qui fodit foveam, incidet in eam ; et qui dissipat sepem, mordebit eum coluber. Et rursus Salomon : In insidiis suis capientur iniqui. Uniuscujusque enim malum in proprium redundat auctorem ; et prius nocet peccatum agenti, quam patienti. Istud quoque in Judæis impletum est, quoniam ipsi disposuerunt Christum occidere et nomen ejus omnino exstinguere ; sed oppositum contigit, quoniam Christus a morte est suscitatus, ipsi vero in ultionem sanguinis Christi occisi sunt atque dispersi. Et ideo subditur : In veritate tua, id est sicut per Prophetas dixisti, disperde illos, id est, variis plagis perde eos, scilicet gladio, fame et peste : quemadmodum tempore Titi factum constat. Vel, In veritate, id est in tua justitia, disperde illos, id est, de terra promissionis eos expelle, per totumque mundum diffunde et divide, sicut ab Osee prædictum est : Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus, quia non audierunt vocem ejus ; et erunt vagi in nationibus. Hanc quoque prophetiam in Judæis esse impletam, ostenditur per Osee : Circumdederunt, inquit, eos adinventiones ipsorum. Advertendum autem quod Christus hæc orat, vel conformando se divinæ justitiæ, vel prænuntiando quod erat futurum, vel insinuando quid illi meruerint ; non autem absolute imprecatur mala adversariis suis, præsertim quum ipse nobis præceperit, Diligite inimicos vestros, et orate pro persequentibus et calumniantibus vos.
paras.en: [[53:7|Turn back the evils upon my enemies|Averte mala inimicis meis]]: that is, turn back upon their own heads the evils and punishments prepared for me by the Jews, and deliver me, so that the snare they have prepared for me may close upon them; as it is written in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 10:8|He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it: and he that breaketh a hedge, a serpent shall bite him.|Qui fodit foveam, incidet in eam ; et qui dissipat sepem, mordebit eum coluber]] And again Solomon: [[Prov 11:6|the unjust shall be caught in their own snares|In insidiis suis capientur iniqui]]. For each man's evil recoils upon its own author, and sin harms the doer before the sufferer. This too was fulfilled in the Jews, for they planned to kill Christ and wholly to blot out his name; but the opposite came about, for Christ was raised from death, while they, in vengeance for Christ's blood, were slain and scattered. And so it is added: [[53:7|in thy truth|In veritate tua]], that is, as thou hast said by the Prophets, [[53:7|cut them off|disperde illos]], that is, destroy them by various plagues, namely by sword, famine and pestilence, as is known to have been done in the time of Titus. Or, [[53:7|in thy truth|In veritate]], that is, in thy justice, [[53:7|cut them off|disperde illos]] [disperde means both "destroy" and "scatter"; hence the two readings], that is, drive them out of the land of promise, and spread and scatter them through the whole world, as was foretold by Osee: [[Osee 9:17|My God will cast them away, because they hearkened not to him: and they shall be wanderers among the nations.|Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus, quia non audierunt vocem ejus ; et erunt vagi in nationibus]] That this prophecy too has been fulfilled in the Jews is shown by Osee: [[Osee 7:2|their own devices|eos adinventiones ipsorum]], he says, [[Osee 7:2|have beset them about|Circumdederunt]]. Now it should be noted that Christ prays these things either by conforming himself to the divine justice, or by foretelling what was to come, or by hinting at what they had deserved; but he does not absolutely call down evils on his adversaries, especially since he himself has commanded us: [[Matt 5:44|Love your enemies|Diligite inimicos vestros]], [[Matt 5:44|and pray for them that persecute and calumniate you|et orate pro persequentibus et calumniantibus vos]].

paras.t: Voluntarie sacrificabo tibi : id est, sponte atque ardentissima caritate Dei et proximi offeram me ipsum in ara crucis tibi Deo omnipotenti pro mundi salute, quemadmodum de me ait Isaias : Oblatus est quia voluit ; et ipse peccata multorum tulit. Unde in Evangelio dicit Salvator : Ego sum pastor bonus, et animam meam pono pro ovibus meis ; et rursus, Nemo tollit animam meam a me, sed ego pono eam. Propter quod Apostolus dicit : In fide vivo Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, et tradidit semetipsum pro me. Sic ergo Christus sacrificavit, id est, in sacrificium salutiferum dedit se ipsum ex ferventissima caritate, tam Dei quam proximi, scilicet ut Dei honorem recuperaret, hominumque salutem perficeret, quemadmodum testatur Apostolus : Sanguis Christi qui per Spiritum Sanctum semetipsum obtulit immaculatum Deo, emundabit conscientiam nostram ab operibus mortuis, ad serviendum Deo viventi.
paras.en: [[53:8|I will freely sacrifice to thee|Voluntarie sacrificabo tibi]]: that is, of my own accord, and with the most ardent charity towards God and my neighbour, I will offer myself on the altar of the cross to thee, almighty God, for the salvation of the world; as Isaias says of me: [[Is 53:7|He was offered because it was his own will|Oblatus est quia voluit]]; [[Is 53:12|and he hath borne the sins of many|et ipse peccata multorum tulit]]. Hence the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[John 10:14|I am the good shepherd|Ego sum pastor bonus]], [[John 10:15|and I lay down my life for my sheep|et animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]]; and again, [[John 10:18|No man taketh it away from me: but I lay it down|Nemo tollit animam meam a me, sed ego pono eam]]. For this reason the Apostle says: [[Gal 2:20|I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and delivered himself for me|In fide vivo Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, et tradidit semetipsum pro me]]. So, then, Christ sacrificed, that is, gave himself as a saving sacrifice out of most fervent charity towards God as well as neighbour, namely so as to recover the honour of God and accomplish the salvation of men; as the Apostle testifies: [[Heb 9:14|the blood of Christ, who by the Holy Ghost offered himself unspotted unto God, cleanse our conscience from dead works, to serve the living God?|Sanguis Christi qui per Spiritum Sanctum semetipsum obtulit immaculatum Deo, emundabit conscientiam nostram ab operibus mortuis, ad serviendum Deo viventi]].

paras.t: Et confitebor nomini tuo, Domine, confessione laudis, quoniam bonum est, quia naturaliter atque quomodolibet bonum est, et bonitas pura, perfecta atque infinita. Propter quod scriptum est : Nemo bonus nisi solus Deus. Ideoque tu, Domine Deus, propter te ipsum laudandus es, et omni laude superdignissimus. Confessus est autem Christus confessione laudis Deo Patri in omni vita sua, et in passione, dum dixit, Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum ; atque post mortem, dum ait, Ascendo ad Patrem meum. Hinc namque ait, Ego honorifico Patrem meum ; et, Ego non quæro gloriam meam ; et, Ego quæ placita sunt ei (scilicet Patri) facio semper. Ideo quoque, o Domine, confitebor nomini tuo, Quoniam ex omni tribulatione eripuisti me, in die resurrectionis, quando ad impassibilem vitam resuscitasti me : sicut Apostolus asserit, Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur.
paras.en: [[53:8|And will give praise, O God, to thy name|Et confitebor nomini tuo, Domine]] [confitebor, literally "I will confess"], with the confession of praise, [[53:8|because it is good|quoniam bonum est]]: for it is good by nature and in every way, and is goodness pure, perfect and infinite. For which reason it is written: [[Luke 18:19|None is good but God alone|Nemo bonus nisi solus Deus]]. And therefore thou, O Lord God, art to be praised for thine own sake, and art most supremely worthy of all praise. Now Christ confessed to God the Father with the confession of praise throughout his whole life; and in the passion, when he said, [[Luke 23:46|Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit|Pater, in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum]]; and after death, when he says, [[John 20:17|I ascend to my Father|Ascendo ad Patrem meum]]. Hence too he says, [[John 8:49|I honour my Father|Ego honorifico Patrem meum]]; and, [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|Ego non quæro gloriam meam]]; and, [[John 8:29|the things that please him|Ego quæ placita sunt ei]] (namely, the Father) [[John 8:29|I do always|facio semper]]. Therefore also, O Lord, I [[53:8|will give praise, O God, to thy name|confitebor nomini tuo]], [[53:9|For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble|Quoniam ex omni tribulatione eripuisti me]], on the day of the resurrection, when thou didst raise me to impassible life; as the Apostle declares, [[Rom 6:9|Christ, rising again from the dead, dieth now no more|Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur]].

paras.t: Duæ ergo sunt causæ laudandi Deum. Prima est bonitas ejus : propter quam dixit, Confitebor nomini tuo, quoniam bonum est. Secunda est exhibitio beneficiorum ipsius : propter quam ait, Quoniam ex omni tribulatione eripuisti me. Majus autem ac dignius est, magisque meritorium, laudare, honorare, diligere Deum propter propriam bonitatem, quam ob beneficia sua : quia procedit ex caritate purius perfectiusque divina. Sed Christi vestigia imitantes, laudare debemus atque amare Dominum Deum nostrum propter causam utramque : hoc enim perfectissimum est. Porro, quod dictum est, Quoniam ex omni tribulatione eripuisti me, referri potest ad id quod ait, Quoniam bonum est ; sed tunc conjunctio hæc, Quoniam, non denotat causam, sed signum. Non enim ideo Deus bonus est, quoniam eripit nos ; sed ideo eripit nos, quoniam bonus est : sicque ereptio qua eripit nos, est signum bonitatis divinæ, non causa ; vel, si dicatur causa, non est causa simpliciter et a priori, sed quoad nos et a posteriori, quia per hoc innotescit nobis bonitas Dei, quod tam misericordissime eripuit nos.
paras.en: There are, then, two causes for praising God. The first is his goodness, on account of which he said, I [[53:8|will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good|Confitebor nomini tuo, quoniam bonum est]]. The second is the showing of his benefits, on account of which he says, [[53:9|For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble|Quoniam ex omni tribulatione eripuisti me]]. Now it is greater and worthier, and more meritorious, to praise, honour and love God for his own goodness than for his benefits, because this proceeds more purely and perfectly from divine charity. But following in Christ's footsteps we ought to praise and love the Lord our God for both causes: for this is most perfect. Further, what was said, [[53:9|For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble|Quoniam ex omni tribulatione eripuisti me]], can be referred to what he says, [[53:8|because it is good|Quoniam bonum est]]; but then this conjunction *for* [in the Latin both clauses begin with quoniam, which the Douay-Rheims renders "because" and "for"] denotes not a cause but a sign. For God is not good because he delivers us; but he delivers us because he is good: and so the deliverance by which he delivers us is a sign of the divine goodness, not a cause; or, if it is called a cause, it is not a cause simply and a priori, but as regards us and a posteriori [that is, a cause of our knowing that he is good, not of his being good], because by this the goodness of God becomes known to us, that he has so most mercifully delivered us.

paras.t: Et super inimicos meos me persequentes, despexit oculus meus : id est, eos non timui, nec eorum falsam felicitatem atque malitiam pro aliquo reputavi, sed in omnibus constans atque victoriosus permansi. Quamvis namque Christus passione instante timorem sponte admisit, inordinatum tamen pavorem non habuit, sed potestative assumptum timorem deposuit, suisque hostibus intrepidus obviam ivit. Unde superius de viro justo præhabitum est : Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus. Et per Isaiam Christus ait : Juxta est qui justificat me ; quis contradicet mihi ? stemus simul. Quis est adversarius meus ? accedat ad me. Ecce Dominus Deus auxiliator meus, et ideo non sum confusus. Ad hunc quoque magnanimem despectum iniquorum, in quantum hujusmodi, Christus passione instante hortabatur discipulos : Non turbetur cor vestrum, neque formidet. Vere enim peccatores, in quantum peccatores, pro nihilo reputandi sunt ; et condolendum est eis, sicut et Jacobus in sua Canonica ait, loquens de eis, dicensque : Agite nunc, divites, plorate, ululantes in miseriis quæ advenient vobis.
paras.en: [[53:9|and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies|Et super inimicos meos me persequentes, despexit oculus meus]] [Denis's text reads "my enemies that persecute me"; despexit, "hath looked down upon", also means "hath despised", and he takes it so]: that is, I did not fear them, nor did I count their false happiness and their malice for anything, but remained constant and victorious in all things. For although, with his passion at hand, Christ freely admitted fear, yet he had no disordered dread, but by his own power laid aside the fear he had taken on, and went out fearless to meet his foes[[John 18:4||]] [the margin gives John 18:4–8]. Hence it was said above of the just man: [[Ps 14:4|In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing|Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus]]. And through Isaias Christ says: [[Is 50:8|He is near that justifieth me, who will contend with me? let us stand together, who is my adversary? let him come near to me.|Juxta est qui justificat me ; quis contradicet mihi ? stemus simul. Quis est adversarius meus ? accedat ad me]] Behold, [[Is 50:7|The Lord God is my helper, therefore am I not confounded|Dominus Deus auxiliator meus, et ideo non sum confusus]] [the margin gives Is. l, 8, 7; the opening "Behold" comes from Is 50:9]. To this magnanimous contempt of the wicked, as such, Christ also exhorted his disciples with his passion at hand: [[John 14:27|Let not your heart be troubled: nor let it be afraid|Non turbetur cor vestrum, neque formidet]]. For truly sinners, inasmuch as they are sinners, are to be reckoned as nothing; and we must grieve for them, as James too says in his Canonical Epistle, speaking of them and saying: [[Jas 5:1|Go to now, ye rich men: weep and howl in your miseries, which shall come upon you.|Agite nunc, divites, plorate, ululantes in miseriis quæ advenient vobis]]

53.title: EXPLANATIO EJUSDEM PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI TERTII MORALIS SIMUL ET LITTERALIS.
53.title_en: Explanation of the same fifty-third psalm, moral and literal together.

paras.t: MORALITER autem per Ziphæos, qui (sicut ostensum est) interpretantur florentes, intelliguntur sæculi amatores, temporaliter floridi : inter quos absconditur David, id est, inter quos nunc conversantur et latent fideles, temporalia contemnentes, atque a mundanis hominibus persecutionem perpessi. Per Saul quoque intelliguntur pestiferi principes et mali prælati, apud quos sæculares et impii justos accusant, produnt, ac lacerant.
paras.en: Morally, by [[53:2|the men of Ziph|Ziphæos]], whose name (as has been shown) means *flourishing*, are understood the lovers of the world, who flourish in temporal things: among whom David is hidden[[1 Kings 23:19||]], that is, among whom the faithful now live and lie hidden, despising temporal things and suffering persecution from worldly men. By [[53:2|Saul|Saul]] also are understood pestilent princes and wicked prelates, before whom worldly and impious men accuse, betray and tear to pieces the just.

paras.t: Quilibet ergo fidelis persecutiones variasque tentationes expertus ac patiens, seque perpendens naturali virtute non posse resistere, ferre seu prævalere, sed ope divinæ clementiæ indigere, totis medullis ad Deum confugiat, clamans et dicens : Deus, in nomine tuo increato, seu in te ipso, non in aliqua pura creatura, salvum me fac, culpam delendo et gratiam infundendo : salvum me fac ab omnibus malis præteritis, præsentibus et futuris ; salvum me fac a malo pœnæ, a malo culpæ, et a malo naturæ; salvum me fac ab omnibus hostibus visibilibus et invisibilibus, a tentationibus cunctis atque universis periculis. Itaque, Domine, salvum me fac in præsenti per fidem et gratiam et incessantem profectum, in futuro autem per beatificam tuæ bonitatis fruitionem. Et hoc fac, in nomine tuo, ita quod tu sis meæ salvationis causa efficiens atque finalis. Nec enim est aliud nomen datum hominibus, in quo oportet nos salvos fieri, nisi nomen tuum, sicut princeps Apostolorum testatur ; et sicut tu ipse per Isaiam locutus es, Deus justus et salvans non est præter me. Et non dubito, Domine Deus, quin precem meam exaudies, dummodo perseveranter oraverim, quoniam verum esse credo quod scriptum est : Omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit.
paras.en: Let every faithful man, then, who has met and suffers persecutions and various temptations, and who considers that by his natural strength he cannot resist, endure or prevail, but needs the help of the divine clemency, flee to God with his whole being [literally "with all his marrow"], crying and saying: [[53:3|O God, by thy name|Deus, in nomine tuo]], the uncreated name, that is, in thyself, not in any mere creature, [[53:3|save me|salvum me fac]], by blotting out guilt and pouring in grace: save me from all evils past, present and to come; save me from the evil of punishment, from the evil of guilt, and from the evil of nature; save me from all enemies visible and invisible, from all temptations and from every danger. And so, O Lord, save me in the present by faith and grace and unceasing progress, and in the future by the beatific enjoyment of thy goodness. And do this [[53:3|by thy name|in nomine tuo]], so that thou be both the efficient and the final cause of my salvation [that is, both the one who brings it about and the end for whose sake it is done]. For [[Acts 4:12|there is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved|Nec enim est aliud nomen datum hominibus, in quo oportet nos salvos fieri]] but thy name, as the prince of the Apostles testifies; and as thou thyself hast spoken through Isaias: [[Is 45:21|A just God and a saviour, there is none besides me|Deus justus et salvans non est præter me]]. And I do not doubt, O Lord God, that thou wilt hear my prayer, provided I pray perseveringly, since I believe that what is written is true: [[Joel 2:32|every one that shall call upon the name of the Lord, shall be saved|Omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit]].

paras.t: Et in virtute tua omnipotenti, cui nihil difficile est, judica me. Quum dicat Apostolus, Horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis ; præsertim quum nesciat homo an amore sit dignus an odio, inferiusque dicatur, Non intres in judicium cum servo tuo, Domine ; ad quod pertinet quod sanctus Job ait de Deo, Nolo multa fortitudine contendat mecum : quum, inquam, sit ita, nonne præsumptuosum et periculosum apparet, ut audeat quis dicere Deo, Et in virtute tua judica me? Sed advertendum quod duplex ponitur judicium Dei : videlicet discretionis, quod agitur in vita præsenti ; quo boni a malis, et electi a reprobis secernuntur ac dividuntur gratia, voto et merito, non loco et præmio. De isto judicio ait Salvator : Nunc judicium est mundi. Quamvis enim hoc judicium a principio mundi inceperit, tamen in adventu et prædicatione Christi atque Apostolorum maxime inchoavit, quia extunc gratia Dei copiosius effusa est, et fideles ac boni ab infidelibus et perversis abundantius evidentiusque discreti sunt. Istud ergo judicium optare debemus, videlicet ut Deus in hoc mundo separet nos a grege malorum, et inter electos nos reputet. Unde de isto judicio ad beatum Job dictum est : Numquid qui non amat judicium, sanari potest? Porro aliud est Dei judicium districtæ discussionis et justæ remunerationis : quod utique omnes timere debemus, et exorare ne ad illud non parati trahamur, aut in eo secundum nostras malitias, negligentias et imperfectiones judicemur, sed potius in hac vita misericordiam consequamur, satisfactionisque gratiam sortiamur. Unde, ob hujus judicii horrendum rigorem, ait beatus Job : Etiam si habuero quidpiam justum, non respondebo ei, sed meum judicem deprecabor ; et alibi : Si impius fuero, væ mihi est ; si justus, non levabo caput. Hæc autem memoriter sunt tenenda, quia in sequentibus frequenter occurrunt.
paras.en: And [[53:3|in thy strength|in virtute tua]], almighty, to which nothing is difficult, [[53:3|judge me|judica me]]. Since the Apostle says, [[Heb 10:31|It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God|Horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis]]; especially since [[Eccles 9:1|man knoweth not whether he be worthy of love, or hatred|nesciat homo an amore sit dignus an odio]], and further on it is said, [[Ps 142:2|enter not into judgment with thy servant|Non intres in judicium cum servo tuo]], O Lord; to which belongs what holy Job says of God, [[Job 23:6|I would not that he should contend with me with much strength|Nolo multa fortitudine contendat mecum]]: since, I say, this is so, does it not seem presumptuous and dangerous that anyone should dare to say to God, [[53:3|and judge me in thy strength|Et in virtute tua judica me]]? But it must be noted that a twofold judgment of God is spoken of. The first is the judgment of discernment [*discretionis*: of sorting out, setting apart], which takes place in the present life, by which the good are set apart from the wicked and the elect from the reprobate, and divided from them by grace, desire and merit, not by place and reward. Of this judgment the Saviour says: [[John 12:31|Now is the judgment of the world|Nunc judicium est mundi]]. For although this judgment began from the beginning of the world, yet it was begun above all at the coming and preaching of Christ and the Apostles, because from then on the grace of God was more copiously poured out, and the faithful and good were more abundantly and more evidently set apart from the unbelieving and perverse. This judgment, then, we ought to desire: namely, that God in this world separate us from the flock of the wicked and count us among the elect. Hence of this judgment it was said to blessed Job: [[Job 34:17|Can he be healed that loveth not judgment?|Numquid qui non amat judicium, sanari potest?]] The other is God's judgment of strict examination and just recompense: which surely we must all fear, praying that we be not dragged to it unprepared, nor be judged in it according to our malice, negligence and imperfections, but rather that in this life we may obtain mercy and receive the grace of making satisfaction. Hence, because of the dreadful rigour of this judgment, blessed Job says: [[Job 9:15|although I should have any just thing, would not answer, but would make supplication to my judge|Etiam si habuero quidpiam justum, non respondebo ei, sed meum judicem deprecabor]]; and elsewhere: [[Job 10:15|if I be wicked, woe unto me: and if just, I shall not lift up my head|Si impius fuero, væ mihi est ; si justus, non levabo caput]]. These things are to be kept in mind, because they occur frequently in what follows.

paras.t: Itaque, Domine, in virtute tua judica me, discernens et separans me a grege malo, de quo in Evangelio dicis, Multi sunt vocati ; et in pusillo grege me statuens, de quo ibi subdis, Pauci vero electi : de quo et ais, Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum.
paras.en: And so, O Lord, [[53:3|judge me in thy strength|in virtute tua judica me]], discerning and separating me from the wicked flock, of which thou sayest in the Gospel, [[Matt 22:14|many are called|Multi sunt vocati]]; and setting me in the little flock, of which thou addest there, [[Matt 22:14|few are chosen|Pauci vero electi]]; and of which thou sayest also, [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom.|Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum]].

paras.t: Deus, exaudi orationem meam jam fusam ; auribus percipe verba oris mei, id est, per exauditionem benignam ostende te precem meam advertere. Moris est sacræ Scripturæ, in his maxime quæ ad affectum pertinent, eamdem sententiam sub aliis verbis ubertim repetere, ad insinuandum magnum desiderium cordis, et ad facilius provocandam misericordiam Creatoris, atque ut ipse appetitus in se ipso accendatur et inardescat. Quo enim verba frequentius proferuntur, eo desiderium sæpius iteratur, cor amplius inflammatur, ipseque habitus caritatis vehementius confortatur.
paras.en: [[53:4|O God, hear my prayer|Deus, exaudi orationem meam]], already poured out; [[53:4|give ear to the words of my mouth|auribus percipe verba oris mei]], that is, by a kindly hearing show that thou heedest my prayer. It is the custom of Holy Scripture, above all in what pertains to the affections, to repeat the same thought abundantly in other words: to convey the great desire of the heart, to move the mercy of the Creator the more easily, and so that the longing itself may be kindled and burn the more within itself. For the more often the words are uttered, the more often the desire is renewed, the more the heart is inflamed, and the habit of charity itself is the more strongly confirmed.

paras.t: Quoniam alieni a caritate fraterna, a Dei timore atque justitia, insurrexerunt adversum me, resistendo, detrahendo, aut simili modo contrariando mihi et spirituali meo profectui, neque tentando, lædendo, aut molestando. Omnes enim qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur. Et fortes hostes invisibiles sive visibiles, scilicet dæmones et principes sæculares, quæsierunt animam meam a Deo avertere, in culpam allicere, spiritualiterque occidere, privando eam caritate et gratia, quæ est animæ vita ; vel, Quæsierunt animam meam, id est vitam meam corporalem, affligere sive exstinguere. Istud ad litteram David dicere potuit de Ziphæis et Saule, ejusque fautoribus. Et non proposuerunt Deum ante conspectum suum, considerando quam inique agerent, quam graviter Deum offenderent, et quantam pœnam in futuro sibi acquirerent, sicut de talibus scriptum est : Thesaurizastis vobis iram in novissimis diebus. Deum ante oculos cordis sui non proponit, qui divinam providentiam vel non credit, vel non attendit ; qui judicium Dei non timet ; qui nec terrore pœnarum, neque amore præmiorum a peccato retrahitur, sed sine timore legem Altissimi prævaricatur, et sine reverentia ante conspectum æterni Judicis cuncta cernentis conversatur. De homine tali scriptum est : Angustia vallabit impium, sicut regem qui paratur ad prælium. Tetendit enim contra Deum manum suam, et erecto collo cucurrit adversus eum.
paras.en: [[53:5|For strangers|Quoniam alieni]] to brotherly charity, to the fear of God and to justice, [[53:5|have risen up against me|insurrexerunt adversum me]], resisting, disparaging, or in some like way opposing me and my spiritual progress, and also by tempting, harming or troubling me. For [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution|Omnes enim qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur]]. [[53:5|and the mighty|Et fortes]] enemies, invisible or visible, that is, demons and worldly princes, [[53:5|have sought after my soul|quæsierunt animam meam]], to turn it away from God, to entice it into sin, and to slay it spiritually, depriving it of charity and grace, which is the life of the soul; or, [[53:5|have sought after my soul|Quæsierunt animam meam]], that is, my bodily life, to afflict or extinguish it. This David could say literally of the men of Ziph and of Saul and his supporters. [[53:5|and they have not set God before their eyes|Et non proposuerunt Deum ante conspectum suum]], by considering how wickedly they were acting, how gravely they were offending God, and how great a punishment they were gaining for themselves in the future; as it is written of such men: [[Jas 5:3|You have stored up to yourselves wrath against the last days|Thesaurizastis vobis iram in novissimis diebus]]. He does not set God before the eyes of his heart who either does not believe in the divine providence or does not heed it; who does not fear the judgment of God; who is drawn back from sin neither by the terror of punishments nor by the love of rewards, but without fear transgresses the law of the Most High, and lives without reverence in the sight of the eternal Judge who sees all things. Of such a man it is written: [[Job 15:24|distress shall surround him, as a king that is prepared for the battle|Angustia vallabit impium, sicut regem qui paratur ad prælium]] [Denis has "the wicked" for "him"]. [[Job 15:25|For he hath stretched out his hand against God|Tetendit enim contra Deum manum suam]], and [[Job 15:26|he hath run against him with his neck raised up|erecto collo cucurrit adversus eum]].

paras.t: Quamvis autem tot adversa obsideant justum, non tamen desperat, quoniam insuperabilem adjutorem habet. Ideo subditur : Ecce enim Deus adjuvat me, confortando me per gratiam, et custodiendo per angelicam protectionem. Unde Apostolus loquens de Deo : Ipse (inquit) dixit, Non te deseram nec dimittam : ita ut confidenter dicamus, Dominus mihi adjutor, non timebo quid faciat mihi homo. Et alibi : Ipse faciet cum tentatione proventum, ut possitis sustinere. Idcirco non debemus inordinate timere. Nam, si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Ecce quam plenum fiducia et amore est hoc verbum, Deus adjuvat me. Simus igitur grati et obedientes tanto adjutori, ne ejus subventione per ingratitudinem reddamur indigni. Propterea enim Samuel dicit : Præparate corda vestra Domino, et servite illi soli, et liberabit vos de manu inimicorum. Et alibi : Nolite, inquit, recedere a tergo Domini, sed servite ei in toto corde vestro, et nolite declinare post vana quæ non proderunt vobis, quia vana sunt. Et Dominus susceptor est animæ meæ, misericorditer eam brachiis pietatis amplectens, cito indulgens, pie conservans, et de omnibus ad salutem necessariis providens.
paras.en: But though so many adversities beset the just man, he does not despair, since he has a helper who cannot be overcome. Therefore it is added: [[53:6|For behold God is my helper|Ecce enim Deus adjuvat me]], strengthening me by grace, and guarding me by the protection of the angels. Hence the Apostle, speaking of God: He himself (he says) hath said, [[Heb 13:5|I will not leave thee: neither will I forsake thee|Non te deseram nec dimittam]]: [[Heb 13:6|So that we may confidently say: The Lord is my helper: I will not fear what man shall do to me.|ita ut confidenter dicamus, Dominus mihi adjutor, non timebo quid faciat mihi homo]] And elsewhere: He [[1 Cor 10:13|will make also with temptation issue, that you may be able to bear it|faciet cum tentatione proventum, ut possitis sustinere]]. Therefore we must not fear inordinately. For, [[Rom 8:31|if God be for us, who is against us?|si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos?]] See how full of trust and love is this word, [[53:6|God is my helper|Deus adjuvat me]]. Let us then be grateful and obedient to so great a helper, lest through ingratitude we be made unworthy of his succour. For this is why Samuel says: [[1 Kings 7:3|prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve him only, and he will deliver you out of the hand|Præparate corda vestra Domino, et servite illi soli, et liberabit vos de manu]] of your enemies [Denis has "of your enemies" where the Douay-Rheims has "of the Philistines"]. And elsewhere: [[1 Kings 12:20|depart not|Nolite]], he says, [[1 Kings 12:20|from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart|recedere a tergo Domini, sed servite ei in toto corde vestro]], [[1 Kings 12:21|and turn not aside after vain things, which shall never profit you|et nolite declinare post vana quæ non proderunt vobis]], [[1 Kings 12:21|because they are vain|quia vana sunt]]. [[53:6|and the Lord is the protector of my soul|Et Dominus susceptor est animæ meæ]] [*susceptor*: literally "one who takes up" or "receives", hence Denis's gloss], mercifully embracing it in the arms of his loving-kindness, quickly forgiving, tenderly preserving it, and providing it with all things necessary for salvation.

paras.t: Averte mala inimicis meis, id est, nocumenta mihi ab eis parata aufer a me, et in ipsos ea retorque. Videtur hoc esse contrarium documento Apostoli, dicentis, Vince in bono malum ; et iterum, Nulli malum pro malo reddentes. Sed ex dictis patet solutio. Non enim vir justus hæc ait absolute, malum aliquod adversariis imprecando, sed se divinæ justitiæ conformando, et quid impii mereantur prodendo. Impius namque meretur ut malum quod alteri parat, in ipsum redundet sibique noceat, quemadmodum Salomon fassus est : Iniquitates suæ capiunt impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringitur. Juxta hunc sensum scriptum est in Genesi : Quicumque effuderit humanum sanguinem, fundetur sanguis illius. Quam multi sanguinem effuderunt, quorum sanguis effusus non est, sicut nec Moysis ista dicentis, qui occidit Ægyptium, et in pace quievit! Quid ergo est, Quicumque effuderit humanum sanguinem, fundetur sanguis illius? nisi quod malitia homicidæ prius occidit ipsum spiritualiter, quam alium corporaliter. Similem quoque intelligentiam habet quod ait Salvator : Omnis qui acceperit gladium, gladio peribit.
paras.en: [[53:7|Turn back the evils upon my enemies|Averte mala inimicis meis]], that is, take away from me the harms they have prepared for me, and turn them back upon themselves. This seems contrary to the teaching of the Apostle, who says, [[Rom 12:21|overcome evil by good|Vince in bono malum]]; and again, [[Rom 12:17|To no man rendering evil for evil|Nulli malum pro malo reddentes]]. But the answer is plain from what has been said. For the just man does not say this absolutely, calling down some evil upon his adversaries, but in conforming himself to the divine justice, and in making known what the wicked deserve. For the wicked man deserves that the evil he prepares for another should recoil upon himself and harm him, as Solomon declared: [[Prov 5:22|His own iniquities catch the wicked, and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins|Iniquitates suæ capiunt impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringitur]]. In this sense it is written in Genesis: [[Gen 9:6|Whosoever shall shed man's blood, his blood shall be shed|Quicumque effuderit humanum sanguinem, fundetur sanguis illius]]. How many have shed blood whose blood was not shed: as was not that of Moses, who wrote these words [that is, as the writer of Genesis], who slew the Egyptian[[Ex 2:12||]] and rested in peace[[Deut 34:7||]]! What then is meant by [[Gen 9:6|Whosoever shall shed man's blood, his blood shall be shed|Quicumque effuderit humanum sanguinem, fundetur sanguis illius]]? Only that the murderer's malice slays himself spiritually before it slays another bodily. The same is to be understood of what the Saviour says: [[Matt 26:52|all that take the sword shall perish with the sword|Omnis qui acceperit gladium, gladio peribit]].

paras.t: In veritate tua disperde illos, id est, in tua justitia et justo judicio ac promissione fideli dejice adversarios meos, pugnando pro me : dejice (inquam) eos, impediendo eorum malitiam a pravo effectu, ne mihi prævaleant. Non autem desidero ut damnentur, sed in præsenti sæculo corrigantur. Invisibiles autem hostes omnino opprimi cupio, sicut promittit Apostolus : Deus autem pacis conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter.
paras.en: [[53:7|cut them off in thy truth|In veritate tua disperde illos]], that is, in thy justice and just judgment and faithful promise cast down my adversaries, fighting for me: cast them down, I say, by keeping their malice from its wicked effect, lest they prevail against me. Yet I do not desire that they be damned, but that they be corrected in this present world. But the invisible enemies I long to see utterly crushed, as the Apostle promises: [[Rom 16:20|And the God of peace crush Satan under your feet speedily|Deus autem pacis conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter]] [Denis reads *conteret*, "will crush", and so takes it as a promise; the Clementine text has *conterat*, "may he crush"].

paras.t: Voluntarie, id est sponte, et propter te ipsum dumtaxat, atque ad gloriam nominis tui, et non intuitu alicujus commodi temporalis, sacrificabo tibi sacrificium laudis, hostiam virtuosæ conversationis, Sacramentum altaris, imo me ipsum et totum quod sum, possum et ago : quia hæc tibi debeo, sicut a te ea sortitus sum. Quemadmodum enim totum meum esse, posse et agere, a te mihi collata sunt ; sic ea in tuum honorem et cultum expendere teneor, atque me totum divino mancipare obsequio obligor, quatenus tota mea substantia, potentia et vita, te Creatorem sanctum et benedictum venerentur atque loquantur. De his sacrificiis seu hostiis ait etiam divinus Apostolus : Per Christum offeramus hostiam laudis Deo semper. Et de sacrificio sanctæ conversationis subjungit : Beneficentiæ et communionis nolite oblivisci ; talibus enim hostiis promeretur Deus. De quo etiam sacrificio in Ecclesiastico habetur : Salutare sacrificium est attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate. De sacrificio autem quo homo offert se ipsum, superius dixit Psalmographus : Sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus. De Sacrificio demum altaris, in Evangelio ait Dominus : Hoc facite in meam commemorationem ; apud Malachiam quoque, In omni loco sacrificatur et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda.
paras.en: [[53:8|I will freely|Voluntarie]], that is, of my own accord, and for thy own sake alone, and for the glory of thy name, and not with an eye to any temporal advantage, [[53:8|sacrifice to thee|sacrificabo tibi]] the sacrifice of praise, the offering of a virtuous life, the Sacrament of the altar, nay, myself and all that I am, can do and do: because I owe these things to thee, as I have received them from thee. For just as all my being, power and action have been bestowed on me by thee, so I am bound to spend them in thy honour and worship, and obliged to give myself over wholly to the service of God, so that all my substance, power and life may revere thee, the holy and blessed Creator, and speak of thee. Of these sacrifices or offerings the divine Apostle also says: Through Christ [[Heb 13:15|let us offer the sacrifice of praise always to God|offeramus hostiam laudis Deo semper]]. And of the sacrifice of a holy life he adds: [[Heb 13:16|do not forget to do good and to impart: for by such sacrifices God's favour is obtained|Beneficentiæ et communionis nolite oblivisci ; talibus enim hostiis promeretur Deus]]. Of this sacrifice it is said also in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 35:2|It is a wholesome sacrifice to take heed to the commandments, and to depart from all iniquity.|Salutare sacrificium est attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate]] Of the sacrifice by which a man offers himself the Psalmist said above: [[Ps 50:19|A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit|Sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus]]. Of the Sacrifice of the altar, lastly, the Lord says in the Gospel: [[Luke 22:19|Do this for a commemoration of me|Hoc facite in meam commemorationem]]; and in Malachias also: [[Mal 1:11|in every place there is sacrifice, and there is offered to my name a clean oblation|In omni loco sacrificatur et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda]].

paras.t: Et confitebor nomini tuo, Domine, mea mala et tua bona, me accusando teque laudando, me spernendo et te exaltando.
paras.en: [[53:8|and will give praise, O God, to thy name|Et confitebor nomini tuo, Domine]] [*confitebor* means both "I will confess" and "I will give praise"; Denis takes it both ways]: confessing my evils and thy good things, accusing myself and praising thee, despising myself and exalting thee.

paras.t: Quoniam ex omni tribulatione, a qua hucusque liberatus sum, tu eripuisti me in re, a futuris quoque tribulationibus jam eripuisti me in spe. Non enim propria virtute prævalui, sed omnis victoria mea a te est : ideo, et super inimicos meos despexit oculus meus, propter fiduciam magnam quam in te habeo fixam, et quoniam toties expertus sum gratiam tuam. Hinc ergo iniquos parvi pendo, et te solum formido, quemadmodum primo libro Machabæorum præcipitur : A verbis peccatoris ne timueritis, quia gloria ejus stercus et vermis. Hodie extollitur, et cras non invenietur.
paras.en: [[53:9|For|Quoniam]] [[53:9|thou hast delivered me|eripuisti me]] in fact [[53:9|out of all trouble|ex omni tribulatione]] from which I have so far been set free, and from future troubles also thou hast already delivered me in hope. For I did not prevail by my own strength, but all my victory is from thee: therefore [[53:9|my eye hath looked down upon my enemies|et super inimicos meos despexit oculus meus]] [*despexit*: "looked down upon", and so also "despised"], because of the great trust that I have fixed in thee, and because I have so often known thy grace. Hence I make little of the wicked, and fear thee alone, as is commanded in the first book of the Machabees: [[1 Mach 2:62|fear not the words of a sinful man, for his glory is dung and worms|A verbis peccatoris ne timueritis, quia gloria ejus stercus et vermis]]. [[1 Mach 2:63|Today he is lifted up, and tomorrow he shall not be found|Hodie extollitur, et cras non invenietur]].

paras.t: Ecce psalmus hic brevis quam ingentem sanctæ devotionis ignem includit. Discamus ergo ex eo ardentes Deo offerre preces, in omni persecutione et tentatione ad ipsum confidenter recurrere, eumque amorose affari, de ipso affectuose ac fiducialiter loqui, ei quoque nos ipsos promptissime sacrificare, in omnibus gratias agere, eum laudare, et ejus beneficia grata mente recolere.
paras.en: See how great a fire of holy devotion this short psalm holds within it. Let us learn from it, then, to offer ardent prayers to God; in every persecution and temptation to run back to him with confidence; to speak to him lovingly, and to speak of him with affection and trust; to sacrifice ourselves to him most readily; to give thanks in all things; to praise him; and to call his benefits to mind with a grateful heart.

paras.t: PRECATIO. Deus, in te sperantium salus summa, in nomine tuo nos salva, et contra fortes quærentes animas nostras nos potenter adjuva : ut ex omni tribulatione erepti per te, cunctos inimicos despiciamus securi.
paras.en: Prayer. O God, the highest salvation of those who hope in thee, save us [[53:3|by thy name|in nomine tuo]], and help us mightily against [[53:5|the mighty|fortes]] who seek our souls: that, delivered by thee [[53:9|out of all trouble|ex omni tribulatione]], we may look down on all our enemies, free from fear.
